At a high level, the C-3PO algorithm proceeds by enumerating small cuts and reconstructing the original measure through cluster expansions. Underlying the algorithm is an improvement of subspace enumeration methods via active regression.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Closing All-Exp Gaps in Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem and Maximum Constraint Assignment
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We prove the all-exp property for the Traveling Salesman Problem with the $2$-opt neighborhood, and for $(3,2,2)$- and $(2,3,2)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment with the flip neighborhood. The all-exp property states that infinitely many instances have an initial solution from which every sequence of improving moves to a local optimum, and hence every run of local search, has exponential length. For the Traveling Salesman Problem, the all-exp property was previously known for every $k$-opt neighborhood with $k \ge 3$, so our result for $2$-opt completes the picture for all $k$-kopt neighborhoods. In $(p,q,r)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment, each constraint involves at most $p$ variables, each variable occurs in at most $q$ constraints, and each domain has size $r$. Decreasing any of the parameters of $(3,2,2)$ or $(2,3,2)$ yields a problem in which every sequence of improving flips has polynomial length, so both Maximum Constraint Assignment results are tight. All three results settle long-standing open problems. Our proofs build on a common construction idea, which reveals a close connection between the local-search dynamics of the three problems.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Optimal Average Distortion for Non-Expansive Embeddings of Euclidean Metrics into the Line: With applications to cut-matching games and vertex expansion
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We show that any $n$-point Euclidean metric admits a non-expansive embedding into the line with average distortion at most $O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}}\right)$, matching a known lower bound.
  We also present two applications of this result. First, we give a cut-player strategy with an optimal spectral guarantee for the undirected cut-matching game. Second, we give an improved spectral approximation for vertex expansion in high-degree graphs.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Revisiting the directed pathwidth of h-semicomplete digraphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: A digraph is $h$-semicomplete if every vertex has at most $h$ non-neighbors. In semicomplete digraphs, $k$-triples are obstructions to bounded directed pathwidth with many algorithmic applications: Fradkin and Seymour [JCTB 2013] showed that a large triple contains a subdivision of every small digraph, and triples were used for irrelevant vertex arguments in routing problems by Fomin and Pilipczuk [JCTB 2019] and Gomes, Lopes, and Sau [ICALP 2025]. Fradkin and Seymour also showed that there is a function $f(k)$ such that every semicomplete digraph of directed pathwidth at least $f(k)$ contains a $k$-triple, and their proof gives $f(k)$ triply exponential in $k$. For $h$-semicomplete digraphs, a result of Kitsunai et al. [ESA 2015] also yields a $k$-triple, but only existentially, and finding one in fixed-parameter time remained open. We improve the bound on $f(k)$ to a single exponential and extend the result to $h$-semicomplete digraphs: we show that every $h$-semicomplete digraph of directed pathwidth greater than $(h+1) \cdot k \cdot 2^{27k+9}$ contains a $k$-triple, which we find in polynomial time, and no bound subexponential in $k$ or sublinear in $h$ is possible. We also extend the approximation algorithm for directed pathwidth of Fomin and Pilipczuk to $h$-semicomplete digraphs, so its certificates of large directed pathwidth remain valid. Our proof is much shorter than the analysis of Kitsunai et al., and while their algorithm is exact, ours runs in polynomial time. As an application, we show that Arc-Disjoint Paths on $h$-semicomplete digraphs is fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number of paths and $h$, generalizing the semicomplete case. Finally, unlike in semicomplete digraphs, directed pathwidth does not bound directed cliquewidth: for every $k$, some acyclic $1$-semicomplete digraph, so of directed pathwidth zero, has directed cliquewidth at least $k$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Compressing the Lawler-Moore Dynamic Program for Weighted Tardy Jobs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: The classic scheduling problem of minimizing the total weight of tardy jobs ($P_m||\sum_jw_jU_j$) asks for a schedule of jobs each with a processing time, weight, and due date on a constant number of parallel identical machines. A job is late in a schedule if it completes after its due date, and an optimal schedule is one where the total weight of all late jobs is minimized. The classic dynamic programming algorithm of Lawler and Moore [Manag. Sci., 1969] solves this problem in $O(nd_{\max}^m)$ where $n$ is the number of jobs, $d_{\max}$ is the maximum due date of any job, and $m$ is the number of identical machines. We show that it is sufficient to only compute part of the dynamic program and obtain the running time $\tilde{O}(n + d_{\max}^{m + 1})$ where $\tilde{O}$ suppresses polylogarithmic factors. This affirmatively answers the open question posed by Hermelin, Molter, and Shabtay [INFORMS J. Comput., 2024], whether a running time of $\tilde{O}(n + d_{\max}^2)$ is possible on a single machine.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Degree Realization with Maximum Matching
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: The Maximum Matching Degree Realization problem requires, for a sequence $d$ of $n$ positive integers, to compute a realizing graph(whose degree sequence corresponds to $d$) with the maximum possible matching. We present a polynomial-time algorithm for this problem. The decision version of this problem requires to determine whether a sequence $d$ admits a realization with a matching of size $ν$ (without computing such a realization). Recently, it was shown that it can be done by verifying a series of inequalities. We improve the existing characterization by reducing the number of inequalities.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Catalytic space-efficient algorithms for Distance and Determinant
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Catalytic computation reuses potentially large but in-use space (or catalytic space) which must be restored to its initial contents while the clean space is small. This allows all problems in $\mathsf{NL}$ and even larger classes to be in catalytic logspace [Buhrman et al, STOC2014]. In [Chmel et al, CCC2026] the catalytic space for reachability was restricted to sublinear space (specifically, $n \big/ 2^{θ(\sqrt{\log n})}$ space) while remaining in polynomial time. This matches the non-catalytic bounds from [Barnes et al, SICOMP1998].
  We extend the reachability bound to shortest distance, proving a simultaneous sublinear catalytic space and polynomial time bound (henceforth called, sublinear $\mathsf{CLP}$). This is the first simultaneous sublinear space and polynomial time bound for distance even without the catalytic discipline. Moreover, our bound works even for polynomially weighted graphs.
  Along the way we prove simultaneous near linear catalytic space ($\mathcal{O}(n\log^{O(1)}{n})$) and polynomial time bounds for the determinant. We also show some applications to planar matching problems.
  Our starting point was catalytic computation of reachability in directed graphs by [Cook-Pyne, ITCS2026]. [Edenhofer, arXiv:2602.21088] used it to give a tradeoff between catalytic and non-catalytic space, while [Chmel et al, CCC2026] compress the graph to a smaller graph preserving $s,t$-reachability to achieve a smaller space bound. All three can be modified to yield an algorithm for unweighted distance.
  Our contribution is to define an approximation to the walk polynomial in weighted graphs that allows us to infer weighted $s,t$-distance in sublinear $\mathsf{CLP}$. We do so by non-trivially combining elements from each of the above three papers.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A Fully Polynomial Randomized Approximation Scheme for Hypergraph Unreliability
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We give a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for all-terminal unreliability in explicitly represented undirected hypergraphs of arbitrary rank. The algorithm estimates the probability that independent hyperedge failures disconnect the hypergraph, allowing a different rational failure probability for every edge. For a common failure probability, this improves the quasi-polynomial approximation schemes of Cen, Li, and Panigrahi to polynomial time and answers the polynomial-time approximation question reiterated in their subsequent work on graphs.
  The construction turns their representative-survival bound into an importance sampler whose relative second moment is bounded solely in terms of the number of vertices. We protect one randomly chosen representative pair during contraction, correct the path likelihood, and divide by the number of pairs surviving at the end. The resulting unbiased estimator has relative second moment at most $\binom n2$, even when unreliability is exponentially small.
  A minimum-cut normalization makes this estimator implementable with polynomially bounded precision: the residual likelihood becomes a survival probability in an auxiliary absorbing process, which admits rational discretization with a fixed random-bit budget. Logarithmic rate rounding and an exact weighted minimum cut extend the construction to unequal rational failure probabilities. The algorithm's worst-case running time and random-bit usage are polynomial in the input length, the inverse relative error, and $\log(1/δ)$ for confidence $1-δ$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A Better Lower Bound for Sublinear Metric Steiner Tree
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
In the metric Steiner tree problem, we are given an $n$-point metric space $(V,w)$ and a set of terminals $T\subseteq V$, and we are interested in the smallest total weight $\mathsf{st}(V,T,w)$ of a tree that contains every terminal and may also use points of $V\setminus T$. We work in the distance-oracle model: the algorithm knows $V$ and $T$ in advance and learns $w$ only by querying a single entry $w(u,v)$ at a time. The goal is to estimate $\mathsf{st}(V,T,w)$ with the minimum number of queries.
  A factor of $2$ is achievable with nearly linear number of queries, so the interesting question is the query complexity of algorithms with an approximation ratio strictly below $2$. We prove that for every fixed $η\in(0,1)$, every randomized $(2-η)$-approximation algorithm must make more than $\widetildeΩ(n^{7/5})$ queries, improving upon the previously known bound of $\widetildeΩ(n^{6/5})$. Given that the best known upper bound shows that $\widetilde O(n^{5/3})$ queries suffice, the exponent of this problem now lies between $7/5$ and $5/3$, up to logarithmic factors.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Lowered crossover points of Anthropic's subexponential 3-SAT algorithm
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: The October 2026 refutations of the Exponential Time Hypothesis count satisfying assignments in time $2^{o(n)}$, but an asymptotic bound does not say from which input size, the crossover point, they beat the best known algorithms. We make the #3-SAT recursion of Anthropic's algorithm explicit and lower its crossover points, computed from the main term of the proved bound, by proved changes. For the bound in the number $m$ of clauses, at clause density one, the crossover point drops to about $2^{420}$ clauses from $2^{33858}$; for general 3-SAT, in the number $n$ of variables, our estimate drops to $2^{8.6\cdot10^9}$ variables from $2^{2.2\cdot10^{12}}$. With integer tables the recursion counts, for every $j$, the assignments satisfying exactly $j$ clauses in time $2^{O(m/\sqrt{\log m})}$. We observe that this refutes the Sparse Max-3-SAT Hypothesis of Alman and Vassilevska Williams, which also follows from either refutation by the reduction of Impagliazzo, Paturi and Zane, and we lower the crossover point of this computation to about $2^{1016}$ clauses from $2^{68364}$. The distance is structural: we define a rewrite-and-merge class that contains the recursion and all our constructions, and prove that in the main-term model no grid algorithm in it can gain for general 3-SAT below about $2^{6000}$ variables. For two balanced homogeneous merges we prove with quantum functionals an exponent of at least $(\log_2K)^{-3}$ per edge bit, which excludes running times $2^{n^{1-c}}$. Independently of SAT, we formalise the algorithm as a model of computation, Signed Network Sums, which contains rank-one methods and contraction trees. On the complete graph with four nodes, one-level constructions contract the network in $N^{23/6}$ if $ω=2$ and in about $N^{3.93}$ on the current (preprint) matrix-multiplication curve, below the bound $N^4$ of every rank-one method or contraction tree.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: List 3-Coloring in tame classes of graphs in quasipolynomial time
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
A class of graphs $\mathcal{G}$ is tame if there is a constant c such that every $n$-vertex graph in $\mathcal{G}$ has at most $n^c$ minimal separators. Many important graph classes are tame, including chordal graphs, permutation graphs, and circle graphs. Several fundamental problems, most notably Max Weight Independent Set, can be solved in polynomial time on every tame class, which explains in a unified way their tractability on all these classes.
  We show that List 3-Coloring can be solved in quasipolynomial time on every tame class of graphs.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Accelerated Approximate Optimization of Multi-Commodity Flows on Directed Graphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We provide $m^{1+o(1)}kε^{-1}$-time algorithms for computing multiplicative $(1 - ε)$-approximate solutions to multi-commodity flow problems with $k$-commodities on $m$-edge directed graphs, including concurrent multi-commodity flow and maximum multi-commodity flow.
  To obtain our results, we provide new optimization tools of potential independent interest. First, we provide an improved optimization method for solving $\ell_{q, p}$-regression problems to high accuracy. This method makes $\tilde{O}_{q, p}(k)$ queries to a high accuracy convex minimization oracle for an individual block, where $\tilde{O}_{q, p}(\cdot)$ hides factors depending only on $q$, $p$, or $\mathrm{poly}(\log m)$, improving upon the $\tilde{O}_{q, p}(k^2)$ bound of [Chen-Ye, ICALP 2024]. As a result, we obtain the first almost-linear time algorithm that solves $\ell_{q, p}$ flows on directed graphs to high accuracy. Second, we present optimization tools to reduce approximately solving composite $\ell_{1, \infty}$-regression problems to solving $m^{o(1)}ε^{-1}$ instances of composite $\ell_{q, p}$-regression problem. The method builds upon recent advances in solving box-simplex games [Jambulapati-Tian, NeurIPS 2023] and the area convex regularizer introduced in [Sherman, STOC 2017] to obtain faster rates for constrained versions of the problem. Carefully combining these techniques yields our directed multi-commodity flow algorithm.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Steiner Tree Parameterized by Multiway Cut: Single-Exponential Time and Polynomial Space
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In the Steiner Tree problem, the goal is to find a minimum-weight tree containing a given set of terminals in an edge-weighted graph. Given a multiway cut of size $s$, we propose a deterministic algorithm running in $2^{O(s)}\operatorname{poly}(n,b)$ time and polynomial space ($n$ vertices, non-negative $b$-bit integer weights). A multiway cut for the terminals is a set of vertices whose deletion leaves at most one terminal in each connected component. This result answers a question of Jansen and Swennenhuis (ESA 2024). Building on their component decomposition, we show that it suffices to connect the selected cut vertices together with $O(s)$ additional terminals and attach the remaining terminals by shortest paths. We use colour coding to optimize over the choice of these additional terminals.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: New bounds for online coloring three-colorable graphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We prove new lower and upper bounds for online coloring of three-colorable graphs, improving classical bounds of Vishwanathan [FOCS'1990] that have stood for more than three decades. For the lower bound against deterministic algorithms, we improve Vishwanathan's $Ω(\log^2n)$ to \(\exp\!\bigl(Ω((\log n)^{1/3}(\log\log n)^{2/3})\bigr)\). For the upper bound of randomized algorithms, we give a randomized algorithm that achieves $O(\sqrt{n})$ improving Vishwanathan's $O(\sqrt{n \log n})$.
  Technically, for the lower bound construction, we introduce the language of $t$-fold coloring for simpler description of recursive construction, and the notion of post-degree for future control, and use the flexibility of two-sided colors of bipartite graph, constructed using the independent set amplification method of Vishwanathan, as building blocks to ensure three-colorability. The randomized algorithm integrates, in a new way, some of the ideas in offline coloring of Wigderson and Blum with ideas of Vishwanathan in the online setting, such as the degree control from Wigderson, the offline-monochromatic class from Blum, and the anchor-sampling from Vishwanathan and the CBIP algorithm by Lov{á}sz, Saks and Trotter.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Improved Approximation Guarantees for Periodic-Review Stochastic Inventory Control
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
In periodic-review stochastic inventory control, replenishment policies must balance holding and backlogging costs while responding to uncertain demands and evolving forecasts that may be arbitrarily correlated and nonstationary. In this general information setting, Levi, P{á}l, Roundy, and Shmoys (Mathematics of Operations Research 2007) established that the fully adaptive optimum can be approximated within factor $2$, which had remained the best-known performance guarantee since then. Their marginal cost accounting and dual-balancing framework made this comparison possible without computing optimal decisions across future trajectories, opening a broad research program on approximation algorithms for stochastic inventory systems.
  We break this long-standing barrier for periodic-review stochastic inventory control, showing how to compete against the fully adaptive benchmark within factor $\frac{ e }{ e-1 } \approx 1.582$ while retaining general demand correlations and evolving forecasts. We attain these advances by discovering a structural connection between marginal inventory accounting and weighted stopping problems, where each unit's conditional holding charge forms a supermartingale, while postponing its order incurs a history-dependent backlog charge. To leverage the random thresholding approach of Ma and Tzamos (ICML 2023) in this context, we develop a potential-function analysis, leading to an $\frac{ e }{ e-1 }$-approximation with respect to any unit's stopping problem. Subsequently, our common-threshold policy coordinates these marginal decisions into a global replenishment policy without additional loss.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Massively Parallel Algorithms for Huffman Coding
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Huffman coding is one of the oldest and most fundamental problems in computer science. Given a string of length $\TextLength$ over a general alphabet, the goal is to assign a binary codeword to each character so that no codeword is a prefix of another and the total encoded length of the string is minimized. Huffman coding is widely used in practical compression systems, including file compression. As modern datasets continue to grow, it is natural to study whether a Huffman code can be constructed efficiently in the massively parallel computation (\MPC) model. The celebrated Huffman coding algorithm admits two straightforward \MPC implementations: for any constant $ε\in(0,1)$, one uses $O(\TextLength^ε)$ memory per machine but requires $Θ(\log \TextLength)$ rounds, while the other runs in $O(1)$ rounds but requires $Θ(\sqrt{\TextLength})$ memory per machine. We give the first nontrivial \MPC algorithm for Huffman coding that bypasses both limitations. For every constant $ε>0$, our algorithm uses $O_ε(\log\log \TextLength)$ rounds and $\softO(\TextLength^ε)$ memory per machine, while its total memory and total computation are $\softO(\TextLength)$.
  {\color{black}Although our framework is tailored to the \MPC model, we show that it has applications in the \PRAM setting as well. Specifically, we show that the same algorithm can be implemented in the \PRAM model with total work close to linear. In particular, whenever the text length is at most $2^{O\left(\left(\frac{\log \AlphabetSize}{\log\log \AlphabetSize}\right)^2\right)}$ (slightly superpolynomial), where $\AlphabetSize$ is the alphabet size, our parallel running time is asymptotically better than that of all previously known \PRAM algorithms and is essentially optimal.}

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Random-Sign IBLTs: Calibration-Free Self-Sizing After Decoding Failure
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We propose the random-sign Invertible Bloom Lookup Table (IBLT) for calibration-free self-sizing after decoding failure. In a two-round set
  reconciliation protocol, the receiver uses the failed first-round table to estimate an upper bound on the unknown difference size $d$ and size the
  second-round table. In standard IBLTs, failure selection couples the overlap bias with the sign composition of the set difference, making practical
  sizing depend on offline simulation calibration.
  A shared pseudorandom sign independent of the position mapping removes this dependence while preserving cell fields, field widths, and ideal peeling
  recovery. We prove exact unbiasedness on every fixed mapping, a Gaussian limit after failure for $d\gg\sqrt M$, and a discrete limit dominated by
  duplicate edge pairs at smaller scales, where $M$ is the number of cells. These results yield a Skellam upper-bound rule whose conditional miss rate
  is asymptotically at most the target risk, uniformly over all $d\ge2$, without offline calibration.
  More than 500 million paired decoding trials and end-to-end protocol experiments support the design. For small differences, the Gaussian rule's
  conditional miss rate exceeds the target by more than a factor of 8. The Skellam rule meets the target within sampling error across all 189 tested
  load configurations. Total two-round communication approaches that of an oracle using the true $d$ in the same protocol. With fixed deployment
  parameters, precomputed table lookup reduces sizing to less than one microsecond, with total protocol time within 0.5 percent of the Gaussian rule.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: The implementation, frozen experimental configurations, and summary data are available at https://github.com/whitewum/random-sign-artifact

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Multiple Swap Local Search Approximations for Uniform-Cost Capacitated Facility Location with Extensions to Outliers
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We study metric facility location with customer incompatibilities, where the clients assigned to each facility must satisfy prescribed independence constraints. We first consider the setting of facility-opening costs and where there is a single matroid $\mathcal M$ over the clients and the set of clients assigned to an open facility must be an independent set in $\mathcal M$. We develop a polynomial-time \((1+\sqrt{2}+ε)\)-approximation algorithm for this setting. We further obtain a polynomial-time \((15+ε)\)-approximation algorithm for the case of non-uniform facility-opening costs when $\mathcal M$ is a partition matroid that only permits $b_g$ clients to be assigned to a facility for each group $g$ in the partition. Both settings are substantial generalizations of Capacitated Facility Location with uniform capacities.
  Our algorithms are based on local search using add, delete, and single-swap operations. As with CFL, bounding the connection cost is reasonably straightforward using supermodularity of the minimum connection-cost function. However, bounding the facility opening costs requires novel arguments in both cases. We use a ``compression'' argument based on matroid exchange principles to identify a subset of the locally opened facilities whose size is no larger than that of an optimal facility set. The opening costs of facilities outside this subset can be bounded using supermodularity, while bounding the costs of the remaining facilities requires different arguments.
  It is natural to consider a variant where each possible facility $i$ has its own matroid $\mathcal M_i$ defining the subsets of clients it can feasibly serve. We also show problem is at least as hard to approximate as Set Cover even if all $\mathcal M_i$ are partition matroids that have the same partition of clients, just different group bounds $b_g$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Traveling Salesman Problem on Graphs with Proportional Independent Set
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We give a deterministic algorithm for minimum-cost Hamiltonian cycle in undirected graphs with arbitrary real edge costs and an independent set of size at least $αn$, for any fixed $3/7<α\le1/2$. It runs in $O^*(γ(α)^n)$ time for an explicit constant $γ(α)<2$; for bipartite graphs, the bound is $O^*((1+2\sqrt2)^{n/2})\approx O^*(1.957^n)$. The algorithm is based on a restricted Held--Karp dynamic program. Its state enumeration uses structural properties of minimum-cost assignments arising from a regular triangulation of a product of simplices.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: The Competitive Ratio of Online Budgeted Allocation is Strictly Smaller than $1-1/e$
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: A well-known conjecture in online algorithms is that the (randomized) competitive ratio of online budgeted allocation is $1-1/e$. We refute this conjecture and show that every randomized online algorithm has competitive ratio at most $1 - 1/e - \varepsilon$ for a (small) absolute constant $\varepsilon > 0$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Stochastic Weighted Caching with Per-Request Predictions
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Both the unweighted and weighted variants of caching are cornerstone problems in competitive analysis, with tight randomized competitive ratios of $Θ(\log k)$, where $k$ is the cache size. We study weighted caching with per-request predictions, where each page request is accompanied by a prediction of the next arrival time of the same page. For unweighted caching, such perfect predictions suffice to implement Belady's offline optimal rule. For weighted caching, however, previous work shows that a logarithmic lower bound persists even with perfect predictions on adversarial request sequences. Stochastic assumptions alone are also insufficient: the classical caching lower bounds already apply to uniform independent requests. In this work, we ask whether combining these two sources of additional information can overcome this barrier, and answer this question affirmatively.
  Specifically, we develop an efficient cache eviction policy that achieves a competitive ratio of $15.75$ using perfect per-request predictions when page requests are drawn independently from an arbitrary, known static distribution in every step, and page costs are arbitrary. Underlying our analysis is a novel lower bound on the optimal cost obtained through an ex-ante relaxation of the cache's covering constraints. Our algorithm's performance degrades gracefully under erroneous predictions: we prove a bound of $O(\min\{1+E,\log k\})$ on the competitive ratio, where $E$ aggregates each page's average prediction error, and may be unknown to the algorithm.

Signal Processing.title: GazeRIB: Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Reader Gaze-Guided Chest X-ray Learning
Signal Processing.summary: Radiologists' visual attention can supervise medical image learning, but how reader panel composition affects its value remains untested. We evaluated GazeRIB (Gaze-guided Radiologist-Informed Blackout), which masks unviewed regions during training and uses unmasked images at inference. Eight experts repeatedly read the same 80 chest X-rays (CXRs). We compared individual readers with three-, five- and eight-reader panels across seven architectures and 10 seeds, evaluating 910 models on a separate 2,897-CXR cohort for four-class severity prediction. Every panel improved macro F1 over the no-gaze baseline by 5.33-7.47 percentage points (pp; Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.007); no individual reader reached significance on this endpoint. Three readers captured 73-80% of the eight-reader gain in macro F1, the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AU-PRC). On external validation without retraining, all four panels improved ROC-AUC on SIIM-FISABIO-RSNA by +1.93 to +4.24 pp (p <= 0.004); on MIMIC-Eye no panel differed significantly from baseline, whereas the single-reader average declined (-1.40 pp, p = 0.008). Reader composition therefore influenced performance, although transfer depended on the cohort.
Signal Processing.comment: 20 pages on main manuscripts (3 tables + 4 figures), 14 pages supplementary (10 tables + 8 figures)

Signal Processing.title: Embodied Movable Antennas
Signal Processing.summary: This paper introduces embodied movable antennas (MAs), a new MA architecture that rethinks the source of antenna mobility. Unlike conventional MAs that rely on dedicated antenna actuators, embodied MAs harness the mechanical degrees of freedom already present in physical agents to reconfigure antenna position and orientation. We distinguish two modes of embodied MAs: task-coupled and task-preserving. Focusing on the latter, we show how wireless channels can be reconfigured by exploiting task-equivalent host configurations without altering the prescribed physical task. Using a redundant robotic manipulator as a canonical realization, we characterize the intrinsically coupled antenna translation and orientation induced by task-preserving self-motion and derive an exact Fourier representation of the resulting multipath channel. Our analysis reveals that the wireless value of embodied mobility depends not merely on how far an antenna can move, but on which configurations remain feasible under the physical task and how their coupled motion interacts with polarization and multipath propagation. Building on this insight, we develop a cross-task antenna mounting design that enables wireless adaptation with a fixed physical installation. Numerical results demonstrate substantial communication gains through task-preserving motion. These findings establish mechanical redundancy as a new, quantifiable resource for wireless channel reconfiguration.

Signal Processing.title: Grid-Refinement SBL for AFDM Channel Estimation Under Fractional Delay and Fractional Doppler Channels
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates channel estimation for affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) systems over channels with fractional delay and fractional Doppler (FDFD) shifts. An exact FDFD channel model is first established, and the corresponding input--output relationship is also derived. To address the FDFD-induced delay--Doppler coupling, a first-order linear approximation grid-refinement sparse Bayesian learning (FLA-GR-SBL) method is developed. To further remedy the convergence and stability issues caused by the limited accuracy of the first-order approximation, we propose a two-dimensional grid-approximation SBL (2D-GA-SBL) algorithm, which iteratively refines the delay--Doppler grid and thereby characterizes the channel more accurately. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithms significantly outperform existing on-grid and off-grid SBL benchmarks in terms of both normalized mean square error (NMSE) and bit error rate (BER).

Signal Processing.title: Variational decomposition autoencoding improves disentanglement of latent representations
Signal Processing.summary: Understanding the structure of complex, nonstationary, high-dimensional time-evolving signals is a central challenge in scientific data analysis. In many domains, such as speech and biomedical signal processing, the ability to learn disentangled and interpretable representations is critical for uncovering latent generative mechanisms. Traditional approaches to unsupervised representation learning, including variational autoencoders (VAEs), often struggle to capture the temporal and spectral diversity inherent in such data. Here we introduce variational decomposition autoencoding (VDA), a framework that incorporates a strong structural bias toward signal decomposition into variational representation learning. VDA is instantiated through variational decomposition autoencoders (DecVAEs), i.e., encoder-only neural networks that perform latent autoencoding at the level of distributions to learn multiple latent subspaces aligned with time-frequency characteristics. We evaluate DecVAEs on simulated data and three publicly available scientific datasets, spanning speech recognition, dysarthric speech evaluation, and emotional speech classification. DecVAEs improve on VAE-based methods in disentanglement quality and robustness, and their latent subspaces become factor-specific when the generative factors have distinct spectral signatures. These findings position decomposition-aware architectures as potential tools for extracting structured representations from speech, and potentially from other dynamic signals with factors exhibiting distinct spectral signatures, with applications in clinical diagnostics, human-computer interaction, and adaptive neurotechnologies.
Signal Processing.comment: Supplementary information file at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1sZl2AcCtRK-1oav7XZSaxlu0Cq0-3MMs?usp=sharing

Signal Processing.title: B-ExposNet: Bayesian Deep Learning for EMF Exposure Mapping with Uncertainty Quantification
Signal Processing.summary: Electromagnetic field exposure in urban environments is highly variable, and conventional exposure maps provide a deterministic estimate, without considering its uncertainty. To address the gap, this paper proposes B-ExposNet, a Bayesian neural network for spatial exposure estimation with uncertainty quantification. B-ExposNet extends ExposNet by treating the weights of regression head as random variables, inferred by variational inference, so that the model provides probabilistic estimates from posterior predictive distribution. The method is evaluated on drive-test measurement campaigns conducted in three French cities, and compared with conventional method such as universal Kriging, in both predictive accuracy and the quality of the estimated uncertainty. On the test region, B-ExposNet achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 28.19\% and a continuous ranked probability score of 0.198~V/m, improving on canonical methods in both accuracy and uncertainty quantification.

Signal Processing.title: A Manifold-Based Framework for Coupling-Aware Surrogate Optimization of Antenna Arrays Using Characteristic Modes
Signal Processing.summary: A surrogate-based synthesis framework for antenna arrays is presented that incorporates mutual coupling while keeping optimization computationally efficient. The method combines a common characteristic-mode basis, a global modal coupling model, and element-wise generalized scattering matrices (GSMs). Array design variables are formulated and optimized on physically meaningful manifolds, in particular the manifold of unitary symmetric matrices for reciprocal and lossless element GSMs. A staged penalty strategy is used to progressively enforce sidelobe and cross-polarization constraints during multi-beam optimization. The framework is demonstrated for an $8\times8$ left-handed circularly polarized patch phased array with scan behavior in one principal plane. Different degree-of-freedom assignment strategies are compared, showing that constrained non-identical element classes can satisfy stringent pattern requirements where equal-element designs fail. For the demonstrated case, the optimization converges within seconds on a single CPU core, and full-wave verification of the realized arrays confirms the predicted trends, with good agreement for the SLL and useful accuracy for the XPR. The results indicate that the proposed formulation is a practical and scalable route for coupling-aware array synthesis and realization.
Signal Processing.comment: 16 pages, 18 figures

Signal Processing.title: Improving Spectral Resolution via Simultaneous Extracochlear and Apical Ground Contacts: A Neural Simulation Study
Signal Processing.summary: Objectives: While cochlear implants (CI) can provide excellent speech perception outcomes, speech recognition in noise remains a consistent problem for many patients due to channel interaction. Recent work shows the clinical feasibility of an apical return contact placed in the cochlear helicotrema, which presents new possibilities in terms of experimental stimulation schemes. This study explores the interactions between apical and extracochlear ground contacts, aiming to characterize the effects of dual ground usage on auditory nerve fiber (ANF) dynamics and determine their utility in improving spectral resolution. Design: 6 patients with CIs were used in this retrospective study. Volume conduction models encompassing patient specific electro-anatomical characteristics and ANF compartment models defining neural dynamics were used to generate activation thresholds for 75 evenly spaced fiber bundles throughout each modeled cochlea and for 4 different grounding configurations, including the use of combined grounds. We compare our intra-patient models in terms of threshold shifts and standard deviation of fiber proportions to determine the effects of ground configuration used on channel interaction. Results: For all 6 patients, we observe shifts in ANF activation thresholds for the combined ground models indicative of more specific fiber stimulation per contact. Additionally, our combined ground models exhibit reduced fiber proportion standard deviation for several contacts of the stimulating array when compared to the standard extracochlear ground configuration or apical ground configuration. Conclusions: The shifts in activation thresholds and reduction in standard deviations suggest that stimulation schemes utilizing extracochlear and apical grounds in conjunction can provide reduced channel interaction and enhanced spectral resolution for certain contacts in an array.

Signal Processing.title: RadioTraj3D: Height-Aware Adaptive Sampling for 3D Radio-Map Reconstruction from Ultra-Sparse Trajectories
Signal Processing.summary: Aerial networks require radio propagation information at unvisited positions and heights to plan routes, select links, and allocate wireless resources. A three-dimensional radio map (3D RM) represents propagation conditions over the service area, enabling these decisions before flight. However, constructing such a map from autonomous aerial vehicle (AAV) measurements is challenging, since radio measurements are available only along the trajectory, whereas the target covers the 3D service volume. Existing methods use fixed AAV trajectories that ignore how building distributions and heights affect electromagnetic propagation, missing the heights most informative for RM reconstruction. To address these issues, we propose RadioTraj3D, which uses building-height information to coordinate measurement selection and layer-wise reconstruction. Building-height variations reveal propagation-sensitive layers that guide height-adaptive sampling. We therefore propose G-METS to select geometry-sensitive heights and allocate an exact budget across edge, corridor, and open regions before channel acquisition. A dual-view reconstructor then integrates local three-dimensional boundaries with full-height context through one bounded coefficient per layer. Simulated outdoor and indoor maps demonstrate state-of-the-art reconstruction across environments and vertical grids. On real-world AAV measurements from the LACN dataset, RadioTraj3D improves peak signal-to-noise ratio by 0.84 dB and reduces normalized mean squared error by 17.5% over Completion AE.

Signal Processing.title: RSS-Based Verification of Drone Remote ID Position Claims with Unknown Transmit Power
Signal Processing.summary: Broadcast Remote Identification (Remote ID) is a key enabler for integrating unmanned aircraft into the airspace. However, the position it reports is self-declared and can be falsified with low-cost hardware. In this paper, we study how Remote ID receivers can verify the declared position from the received signal strength (RSS) when neither the transmit power nor the path-loss exponent is known. In particular, we derive a Rao score test whose null distribution is exactly chi-squared for any number of packets. Its threshold and detection probability therefore follow in closed form. We then bound the detection probability of any detector that is invariant to the unknown link parameters. This bound saturates as the falsified position recedes along a fixed bearing, so a sufficiently large falsification can remain undetectable. From this limit, we obtain the worst-case bearing in closed form, the observation length needed to close it, and a receiver placement rule. Simulation results show that the proposed test considerably outperforms an estimate-then-threshold detector at low false-alarm rates.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027: Communication & Information System Security Track

Signal Processing.title: RFLocMatch: Reference-Conditioned Residual Learning from Angle-Delay Spectra for Accurate Localization
Signal Processing.summary: Radio fingerprint localization supports mobile robots and location-aware services when satellite positioning is unreliable. Angle-delay power fingerprints capture power distributions over angles and delays, but localization remains vulnerable to spatial ambiguity and measurement perturbations. Reflections and blockage can produce similar fingerprints at distant locations, while noise in query fingerprints can alter query-reference rankings despite a clean reference library. These effects can place a distant reference first in the ranking, creating tail errors. Similarity scores can generate plausible candidates, but reliable selection requires candidate-specific residual evidence and comparison across alternatives. This separation motivates RFLocMatch, which uses complementary joint and link-specific matching to preserve candidate locations supported by different links. Reference-conditioned residual learning then scores each candidate using the query and reference fingerprints, their absolute difference, and their element-wise product, while candidate-context modeling compares alternatives. Tail-focused training emphasizes costly errors, and inference replaces the initial match only when a candidate's score advantage exceeds a validation-calibrated threshold. On ray-tracing-generated data, RFLocMatch reduces dual-transmitter 99th-percentile error by 75.2% under link and receiver perturbations relative to the best-performing baseline. On real-world single-transmitter channel impulse response (CIR) measurements with motion-assisted angular-spectrum estimation, it attains 8.25-m 90th-percentile error and 3.83-m mean absolute error.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables

Signal Processing.title: Feasibility of Common-Stream-Only Sensing in ZF-RSMA with Imperfect CSIT
Signal Processing.summary: Reusing the Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) common stream for sensing eliminates dedicated probing signals in Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC), but creates a feasibility bottleneck: the common-power fraction must simultaneously support common decoding, private decoding, and target detection. This paper investigates this tradeoff in downlink zero-forcing RSMA with imperfect channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT) and imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC). With the common beam fixed over a sensing dwell through sensing geometry, the common-power fraction becomes the sole design variable. We prove that the communication-feasible set is either a closed interval or empty. Analytical outage expressions localize these endpoints, revealing a high-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) floor-ceiling effect: common decoding dictates a common-power floor, while imperfect CSIT and SIC impose a private-decoding ceiling. For sensing, the conditional detection constraint is affine, preserving the interval structure. A geometry-matched common beam ensures monotonic detection improvement, reducing joint-feasibility check to the communication-feasible upper endpoint. Simulations validate our analysis, identifying regimes where common-stream-only sensing is viable.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026. 6 pages, 5 figures

Signal Processing.title: Limitation of Bessel Beams in Near Field Communications: A Depth of Field Perspective
Signal Processing.summary: Bessel beams have recently been explored as a candidate complement to focused beams in radiative near-field communications due to their non-diffracting and self-healing properties. However, recent work has shown that the practically useful range of finite-aperture Bessel beams can occupy only a fraction of the radiative near-field region, establishing the existence of a finite propagation limit. In this paper, we establish such a limitation analytically from a depth-of-field perspective for Bessel beams generated by finite circular and square apertures. To quantify the Bessel beam depth, we first derive analytical expressions for the normalized array gain and use them to establish absolute and peak-normalized $3$-dB depth-of-field criteria. These criteria reveal critical cone-angle thresholds that partition the Bessel-beam configuration space into (i) undefined, (ii) finite, and (iii) infinite depth-of-field regimes. Our analysis further reveals that the maximum usable non-diffracting range under the proposed depth-of-field criterion is limited to $\approx22\%$ and $\approx19\%$ of the Fraunhofer distance for circular and square apertures, respectively. Numerical results confirm the accuracy of the derived limits for discrete planar arrays, providing practical engineering guidelines for the design of finite-aperture Bessel beams in future near-field communications.

Signal Processing.title: Dynamic-Aware LC-DMA Beam Tracking for LEO Satellite Communications
Signal Processing.summary: Liquid crystal (LC)-based dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) offer a power-efficient, low-cost, and scalable solution for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications where large apertures are needed to compensate for large path loss in the Earth-satellite link. However, beam tracking with LC-DMAs is governed by two coupled dynamics: the required time-varying beam direction caused by user and satellite mobility, and the finite response time of the LC phase shifters. This raises the question of whether LC-DMAs can reconfigure sufficiently fast to support high-mobility LEO satellite links. To address this problem, we develop a dynamic-aware beam-tracking framework that explicitly accounts for both dynamics. In particular, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the cumulative received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) over a predictive tracking horizon subject to the physical dynamics of the LC unit cells as well as transmit power constraints. To solve this non-convex problem efficiently, we develop an alternating optimization framework combining a closed-form maximum ratio transmission (MRT) digital precoder and maximum ratio combining (MRC) with a parallel, closed-form dynamic-aware phase-shift update. Simulation results show that when the time response of LC-DMAs is properly accounted for, it can support practical mobility scenarios. Moreover, the proposed dynamic-aware algorithm maintains stable SNR and outperforms conventional designs, particularly at high vehicle velocities and low orbital azimuth angles.

Signal Processing.title: Near-Field Multipath MIMO Channels: Modeling Reflectors and Exploiting NLOS Paths
Signal Processing.summary: Near-field (NF) communications is receiving renewed interest in the context of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems involving large physical apertures with respect to the signal wavelength. While line-of-sight (LOS) links are typically expected to dominate in NF scenarios, the impact of non-LOS (NLOS) components at both in centimeter- and millimeter-wave frequencies may be in general non-negligible. Moreover, although weaker than the LOS path, NLOS links may be essential for achieving multiplexing gains in MIMO systems. The commonly used NF channel models for NLOS links in the literature are based on the point scattering assumption, which is not valid for large reflectors such as walls, ceilings, and the ground. In this paper, we develop a generalized statistical NF MIMO channel model that extends the widely adopted point scattering framework to account for imperfect reflections from large surfaces. This model is then leveraged to investigate how the physical characteristics of these reflectors influence the resulting NF MIMO channel. In addition, using the proposed channel model, we analytically demonstrate for a multi-user scenario that, even when users are located within the NF regime, relying solely on LOS NF links may be insufficient to achieve multiplexing gains, thus exploiting NLOS links becomes essential. Our simulation results validate the accuracy of the proposed model and show that, in many practical settings, the contribution of NLOS components is non-negligible and must be carefully accounted for in the system design.

Signal Processing.title: Optimizing GEDI Simulator Configuration for European Temperate Forests
Signal Processing.summary: Accurate estimation of aboveground biomass density is essential for quantifying forest carbon stocks. NASA's GEDI mission provides valuable canopy structure data, but its sparse sampling necessitates the use of simulators to calibrate biomass models at field inventory locations. The widely used simulator of Hancock et al. (2019) emulates GEDI waveforms from airborne LiDAR point clouds, yet it has never been validated over European temperate forests. Here, we compare approximately 8,100 pairs of observed and simulated GEDI relative height (RH) profiles across French forests using the national airborne LiDAR program as input. We separate two sources of error: waveform modeling differences, assessed by referencing both simulated and real RH metrics to a common ALS-derived ground elevation, and ground detection bias, evaluated by comparing each GEDI L2A processing algorithm against the ALS reference. Under the baseline configuration, the mean absolute bias across the full RH profile reaches 0.67 m in leaf-on and 1.20 m in leaf-off conditions. Switching to intensity-based return weighting and selecting the a3 L2A algorithm reduces these biases to 0.43 m and 0.42 m respectively. The a3 algorithm also achieves near-unbiased ground detection (+0.04 m versus -0.82 m for the default), directly reducing a previously overlooked source of error. We also show that leaf-off acquisitions and low-sensitivity shots, both typically excluded from standard biomass products, are simulated as reliably as their counterparts, substantially expanding the potential calibration and inference datasets.

Signal Processing.title: HAPS-Enabled 6G TN-NTNs: Achieving Superior QoS-Energy Tradeoffs Compared with LEO
Signal Processing.summary: Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) can reduce terrestrial energy consumption by absorbing traffic from lightly loaded base stations (BSs), allowing them to be switched off. We study how the NTN platform shapes this quality of service (QoS) energy trade-off, comparing one low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite at 600 km with 1, 4, and 9 high-altitude platform stations (HAPS) at 20 km. Using a traffic-aware framework that jointly optimizes user association, NTN bandwidth, and terrestrial BS activation over a 24-hour traffic profile, we show that 9 HAPS reduce terrestrial energy consumption by 34.1%, versus 26.0% for LEO. At the same QoS, 9 HAPS save 20% more terrestrial energy than LEO while improving cell-edge throughput.

Signal Processing.title: Learning Joint Synchronization, Channel Estimation, and Decoding: Comparison with a Finite-Blocklength Achievability Bound
Signal Processing.summary: Learned schemes that jointly perform tasks such as synchronization and decoding have achieved promising results for short-packet communication. However, it remains unclear how close their performance is to information-theoretic bounds. To investigate this question, we extend the turbo autoencoder (TurboAE) proposed in Dörner et al. (2023) to a single-input single-output waveform channel with an unknown delay and memoryless block fading, for which an achievability bound from finite-blocklength information theory is available. Our extension incorporates a pilot-free, model-guided neural synchronizer and enables joint synchronization, channel estimation, and decoding. At a blocklength of $64$ complex symbols and a rate of one bit per channel use, the proposed TurboAE achieves a lower bit error rate (BER) than all evaluated pilot-assisted 5G baselines, with gains of $1.9$ dB at a BER of $10^{-3}$ over a baseline involving a low-density parity-check (LDPC) code and $1.7$ dB over a baseline involving a polar code and successive cancellation list decoding (list size $8$). In terms of block error rate (BLER), the TurboAE outperforms the LDPC-coded baseline, but lags behind the polar-coded baseline by about $0.8$ dB at a BLER of $10^{-3}$. Moreover, all evaluated schemes remain at least $2.1$ dB away from a pilot-assisted achievability bound, indicating substantial room for improved designs.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages

Signal Processing.title: Group Physical-Layer Authentication and Confidential Beamforming in Non-Terrestrial Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Coordinated high-altitude platform station (HAPS) networks need to authenticate group responses and protect private data under shared power constraints. This paper studies joint group physical-layer authentication (PLA) and confidential beamforming using a fresh secret tag superimposed on private data. For received attacks independent of the current tag, we derive exact finite-block expressions for false acceptance and legitimate rejection. These expressions translate authentication error targets into a required tag signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR). We establish a nonzero asymptotic tag-energy floor and analyze residual frequency offset and peak-power restrictions. The legitimate receiver removes the tag by orthogonal projection, which discards one temporal dimension. For colluding eavesdroppers, we identify the spatial coverage condition under which artificial noise (AN) keeps their SINR bounded as data and AN powers increase together. We jointly optimize the private beams, tag beam, and AN covariance to minimize transmit power under authentication, secrecy, and per-HAPS power constraints. The method combines semidefinite relaxation (SDR), exact private-beam rank reduction, and feasible successive convex approximation. A corrected dual lower bound measures the remaining optimality gap. Numerical results show that increasing the tag length from 16 to 64 symbols reduces the required tag SINR by 7.16 dB. Joint beam design reduces mean transmit power by 27.4% relative to an optimized fixed-tag-direction baseline. The authentication guarantee requires fresh secret tags and excludes relays of the current response.

Signal Processing.title: Covariance Learning for Direction-of-Arrival Estimation with Sparse Linear Arrays
Signal Processing.summary: Covariance learning (CL) estimates source powers and sensor-noise variance by minimizing the Type-II (marginal) negative log-likelihood of the array measurements. We develop both grid-based and gridless CL direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimators applicable to arbitrary sparse linear array (SLA) geometries. The grid-based DOA estimator minimizes the Type-II objective on an angular grid via successive convex approximation (SCA) and estimates the noise variance by a scalar bisection search. The gridless DOA estimator then refines each grid-based DOA over the continuum using a Newton method. Simulations on a six-sensor nested array, including an underdetermined case with nine sources, show that the proposed DOA estimators outperform state-of-the-art methods, despite jointly estimating the sensor noise variance.

Signal Processing.title: GNSS Receiver Operating Point Comparison Between Vector and Scalar Tracking Under High-Dynamics
Signal Processing.summary: This paper presents a measurement noise adaptation mechanism for Kalman filter-based carrier tracking in a navigation-aided GNSS receiver designed for launch-vehicle applications. The tracking loop is tuned for 20\,g acceleration steps, which requires a wide bandwidth that makes the loop vulnerable to noise-driven pull-out at low carrier-to-noise density ratios. To resolve this tradeoff, the measurement noise covariance, $R$, is inflated via a two-layer gate: a sigmoid envelope keyed to the signal $C/N_0$, modulated by a dynamics indicator derived from the discriminator output statistics of the Loop Bandwidth Control Algorithm. During noise-dominated periods the gate inflates~$R$, reducing the Kalman gain so the filter coasts on the navigation-aided prediction; when dynamics are detected the gate opens within one epoch, restoring the high-bandwidth tuning. The navigation aiding is formulated as a stochastic control input whose uncertainty is propagated from the navigation EKF covariance. Simulation results on a 20\,g acceleration step scenario show that the adapted vector architecture doubles the lock-retention rate relative to the standalone scalar filter at $C/N_0 = 31$\,dB-Hz. The receiver is implemented in MSGR, an open-source MATLAB GNSS software-defined receiver.

Signal Processing.title: PolarFlow: Spectral Geometric Flow Matching for Directed Graph Generation via Polar Decomposition
Signal Processing.summary: Directed graphs model asymmetric relationships in biology, transportation, social networks, and electronic design automation. Recent discrete diffusion and flow-matching methods generate directed graphs effectively, but their edge-wise categorical formulations require dense predictions over all ordered node pairs and repeated categorical updates during generation. This motivates a fundamental question: can comparable generative quality be achieved through a more computationally efficient formulation that better exploits the structure of directed adjacency matrices? Existing benchmarks also cover limited network structures, restricting comprehensive evaluation. We introduce PolarFlow, a continuous geometric flow-matching framework based on polar decomposition and truncated spectral coordinates. Its representation comprises four coupled components: a Stiefel frame and rotation angles encoding the orthogonal factor, and a second Stiefel frame and nonnegative eigenvalues characterizing the positive-semidefinite factor. PolarFlow learns a joint velocity field along geometry-aware conditional paths on this product space, reconstructs a continuous adjacency-score matrix, and discretizes it into a binary directed graph. By replacing discrete edge-wise generation with joint continuous transport, PolarFlow improves computational efficiency while retaining global adjacency structure. To broaden evaluation, we introduce complementary Circuit and Twitter benchmarks spanning engineered functional and naturally evolved social networks. Across synthetic and real-world datasets, PolarFlow achieves generative quality comparable to competitive discrete methods while substantially reducing training and sampling time.

Signal Processing.title: Beamfocusing Beyond the Near Field: Frequency Diverse Arrays for OFDM-ISAC Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Traditional phased arrays (PAs) achieve near-field (NF) beamfocusing through spherical wavefront curvature, but lose this range selectivity in the far field (FF). Frequency diverse arrays (FDAs) instead introduce frequency offsets across antenna elements. These offsets synthesize a range-dependent beam whose beamdepth is governed by the aggregate frequency-offset span rather than the physical aperture, thereby extending finite beamdepth into the FF. Although FDAs have been extensively studied for radar, their broader potential for wireless communications remains largely unexplored. Accordingly, this article examines how this capability can support wireless communications and integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). We compare PA and FDA focusing mechanisms, explain FDA coupling and periodicities, and assess coexistence with orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM). Integer-multiple offsets preserve alignment with the OFDM subcarrier grid and avoid offset-induced intercarrier interference under ideal synchronization, but require suitable symbol mapping and receiver processing. We also distinguish FDA beamdepth from waveform-based radar range resolution and discuss their complementary roles in sensing. For the configurations studied, FDAs offer no additional single-user spatial degrees of freedom. Interestingly, their principal benefit is multiuser separation through location division multiple access (LDMA). Numerical case studies under an idealized FDA channel model show that FDA-LDMA achieves higher sum-rates than PA-based schemes for users with small angular separation in the FF, even after accounting for the bandwidth reserved for frequency offsets.
Signal Processing.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Interactive figures and code: https://akadircelik.com/demos/fda-ofdm-isac/

Signal Processing.title: Movable-Antenna-Empowered ISAC: 3D Ambiguity Function Analysis, Waveform Design and Antenna Position Optimization
Signal Processing.summary: Multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) provides abundant spatial and time-frequency degrees of freedom for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), while movable-antennas (MAs) further introduce reconfigurable spatial freedom through array geometry adjustment. However, how the array geometry and the MIMO-OFDM waveform design jointly influence the sensing performance, i.e., the three dimensional (3D) ambiguity function property, remains insufficiently understood. Against this background, we investigate MA-empowered ISAC design under the MIMO-OFDM architecture, where the radio-frequency (RF) antenna positions and the baseband waveform are co-designed with symbol-level precoding (SLP) philosophy. The discrete periodic angle-range-Doppler ambiguity function is firstly derived for the MA-enabled ISAC framework, revealing its interesting features with respect to the waveform matrix rank. Specifically, it is proved that a rank-one waveform yields a 3D ambiguity function that is separable into angular and range-Doppler components. On the other hand, a higher-rank waveform combines multiple spatial components with angle-dependent weights, allowing the range-Doppler ambiguity function to vary across candidate angles and enabling the MA positions to further shape the 3D ambiguity function. Based on the aforementioned analysis, a 3D integrated sidelobe level ratio (ISLR) is defined, a joint optimization problem of the MA positions and the SLP waveform matrix is formulated, and a penalty dual decomposition based alternating optimization algorithm is developed. For the radar-only case, the existence of a rank-one globally optimal waveform is established, which reduces the original high-dimensional waveform optimization to a low-dimensional joint design of the spatial beam and MA positions.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages, 9 figures, submitted to IEEE for possible publication

Signal Processing.title: Fluid Antenna Systems for ISAC Design: A Survey
Signal Processing.summary: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) introduce dynamic positional degrees of freedom (DoFs), extending the spatial domain from a static and discrete resource to a quasi-continuous and reconfigurable design space. This spatial flexibility provides an effective means of alleviating the geometric rigidity and functional conflicts that constrain integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Against this backdrop, we provide a comprehensive overview of FAS-enabled ISAC, tracing the evolution from theoretical performance limits to practical transceiver architectures. To illustrate the surveyed design evolution, we further propose the fluid antenna multi-mode modulation (FA-MM) framework as a representative case study of multidimensional physical-layer design for FAS-ISAC. Finally, several open challenges are discussed, with emphasis on predictive sensing, adaptive coordination, and secure spatial-state management in future FAS-ISAC systems.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Communications Magazine. 7 pages, 2 figures

Signal Processing.title: Pinching Antennas for ISAC: Waveguide Architectures, Solutions, and Future Directions
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a core design principle for sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems, yet fixed antenna geometry limits its performance. Pinching antenna systems (PASS) guide electromagnetic waves along dielectric waveguides and radiate them through position-adaptive antennas, allowing communication links and sensing observations to benefit from spatial reconfiguration. This article reviews PASS-enabled ISAC through single-waveguide, multi-waveguide, and segmented-waveguide architectures, comparing their feed structures, spatial degrees of freedom, operating protocols, and uplink/downlink support. We organize solution pathways around physics-consistent modeling, joint spatial-signal optimization, dynamic channel acquisition, and stable real-time control. A segmented waveguide-enabled pinching-antenna array (SWAN) case study demonstrates joint segment selection, antenna po?sitioning, and transmit beamforming using segment-hysteresis reinforcement learning. The results illustrate how waveguide loss and per-segment aperture gain create communication-sensing tradeoffs. We conclude with research directions in joint transmit?receive operation, measurement-calibrated digital twins, and trustworthy control.

Signal Processing.title: Downlink MU-MIMO for LEO Direct-to-Device: Feasibility, Architecture, and Implementation
Signal Processing.summary: Direct-to-device connectivity from low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites is commercially available, but its throughput is limited by the satellite antenna size and by payloads that separate users only by beams and frequency reuse. This article shows that a single LEO satellite with a meter-scale array can serve hundreds of users on the same time-frequency resource through multi-user multiple-input multiple-output precoding. The number of users it can separate with a single stream each, i.e., its spatial degrees of freedom (DoF), follows from the aperture in wavelengths, the orbit altitude, and the minimum elevation angle. With minimum mean-square error (MMSE) precoding, the throughput of these users grows with the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), whereas maximum-ratio transmission becomes interference-limited. The precoder can be computed from the user positions and the satellite ephemeris and attitude, with a throughput loss of less than 0.5\% at 20~dB SNR compared with perfect channel knowledge under the 3GPP non-terrestrial channel models. The DoF also set the number of digital chains of a hybrid payload, and the functional split among satellites and ground trades inter-satellite-link and feeder-link load against on-board processing. As the satellite moves, the precoder can be updated from the known geometry every radio frame, i.e., 10~ms, while the computationally intensive user pairing can be kept for a few seconds with a throughput loss below 1\%. Finally, we keep the cell-specific signals on fixed beams while precoding the user data jointly across all cells of the satellite. For a $50\times50$ array at 600~km and a minimum elevation angle of $60^\circ$, one satellite serves 410 users at 6.1~bps/Hz on average, more than four times the throughput of fixed beams with four-color frequency reuse.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted IEEE WCM

Signal Processing.title: Prediction-Induced Sparsity for Tracked FMCW Radar: A Track-Conditioned Event-Gap FPGA Architecture
Signal Processing.summary: Tracked FMCW radar already carries a prediction of the next target state, yet the downstream digital hardware is commonly provisioned for a fixed spectral search. We present prediction-induced sparsity (PIS), a tracked-mode architecture that uses the prior before event formation and hardware scheduling. The predicted beat is derotated to an innovation-centred coordinate, while tracker covariance is propagated to a bounded residual support K. Sparse level-crossing packets are then executed by an exact event-gap resonator engine with a shared complex processing element and K-dependent state/coefficient memory. On a public FMCW dataset, causal prior-only con- ditioning reduces event records by 33.1% on average, and the representative fixed-point stream is bit-exact in RTL. And on an Artix-7 implementation, reducing physical support from 129 to 23 states lowers LUT and BRAM use by 65.0% and 88.1%, respectively, and reduces measured VCCINT power by 19.9% at matched throughput. The results show how tracking uncertainty can become a hardware-capacity implication for future adaptive radar accelerators.

Signal Processing.title: Finite-Sample FDR Control for Greedy Aggregation over Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Distributed multiple testing asks $N$ sites, each holding p-values for its own hypotheses, to control the false discovery rate (FDR) of the discoveries made across the whole network while communicating only a small number of bits. Greedy interval aggregation (Pournaderi and Xiang, IEEE TSIPN, 2023) meets the communication budget but controls FDR only asymptotically, and its FDR can exceed the target at finite sample sizes; the same interval counts both select the rejection regions and calibrate the stopping rule, which biases the selected interval densities upward. We propose \emph{budgeted BONuS-GA}: each site mixes synthetic uniform p-values into its data, the center ranks candidate p-value intervals across sites using the pooled counts, and each site's false discoveries are estimated from its own synthetic counts under a per-site share of the level. The procedure needs no knowledge of the null proportions, uses every p-value for both selection and inference, and controls $FDR\leα$ at every sample size for any fixed assignment of hypotheses to sites, assuming only that the null p-values are independent uniforms, independent of the non-null p-values. It keeps the original $O(\sqrt m\log m)$ communication, $m$ being the total number of p-values, when $N=O(\sqrt m)$. We also give a sample-splitting alternative, cross-fit greedy aggregation, with finite-sample control under a random-site model, and we quantify the selection bias behind the original procedure's failure. In a monitoring-network simulation the budgeted procedure retains most of the power of its heuristic counterpart at moderate-to-large site sizes.

Signal Processing.title: Curved Monopoles and Yagi-Uda Arrays for Low-Angle HF Skywave Radiation over Lossy Ground: Analysis, Hybrid Bayesian Optimization, and Validated Full-Wave Design
Signal Processing.summary: High-frequency (HF) skywave radars require high gain at take-off angles of 3 degrees-30 degrees, where vertically polarized monopoles and Yagi-Uda arrays over lossy land suffer from pseudo-Brewster cancellation. This paper shows that curving the elements of HF monopoles and Yagi-Uda arrays converts radiation from this soil-limited transverse-magnetic route into a transverse-electric route that is nearly insensitive to soil conditions. Closed-form half-space bounds quantify both routes and yield design rules; a separability result extends the soil insensitivity to arrays. A hybrid design method combines Bayesian optimization on analytical and method-of-moments models with full-wave simulations of a screened site on moist soil; current extraction differs by at most 5.1% RMS, and Fresnel post-processing agrees with independent perfect-ground results within 0.16 dB in pointwise gain for four arrays. At 15 MHz, a self-matched 2-element curved Yagi-Uda array and a Bayesian-optimized 3-element array achieve realized forward-sector gains of 6.8 and 8.3 dBi over moist soil, 6.4 and 6.3 dB above straight quarter-wave Yagi-Uda arrays optimized by the same procedure, with 92%-95% efficiency. Their gain changes by about 1 dB from a perfect ground to very dry soil, whereas that of the straight arrays falls by 9 dB. Bayesian optimization, confirmed by full-wave simulation, identified a design 0.2 dB above the sweep optimum and a gain-bandwidth Pareto front that offers up to twice the matched bandwidth. The results also show that the native far field of full-wave solvers can overestimate the low-angle gain of vertical arrays over soil by more than 4 dB.

Signal Processing.title: FESTiVE: Self-calibrated Spatial-temporal Gradient Characterization for Non-cartesian Imaging on High Performance Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Gradient imperfections disrupt the encoding benefits of long-readout imaging applications on high-performance systems. Currently, external field monitoring hardware provides the only reliable solution for general spatial-temporal gradient characterization. We present FESTiVE, a data-driven alternative to higher-order field monitoring. FESTiVE leverages parallel imaging to both implicitly model and explicitly recover field imperfections. Using a fast k-t mapping calibration scan, FESTiVE formulates a time-varying GRAPPA problem which maps k-space data corrupted by a time-varying gradient imperfection against a clean reference. This mapping is represented compactly with an implicit neural representation, from which the spatial-temporal fields are recovered in image space using coil sensitivities. In phantom, FESTiVE produces comparable field measurements to a Skope field camera across multiple non-cartesian 2D acquisition strategies and gradient specifications. In vivo, FESTiVE achieves state-of-the-art image quality for a high-performance diffusion spiral protocol on the head-only MAGNUS 3T, where higher-order phase imperfections are significant. At 7T, on the head-only Siemens TerraX system, FESTiVE enables 300μm spiral imaging where conventional field camera-based approaches fall below probe dephasing limits. In conclusion, FESTiVE enables robust high-resolution non-cartesian imaging on high-performance gradients, characterizing gradient imperfections using parallel imaging rather than field monitoring hardware.

Signal Processing.title: Keep Pace to Learn: Movable-Antenna Compensation of Channel Aging in Over-the-Air Split Learning
Signal Processing.summary: Split learning (SL) trains a neural network across devices by exchanging intermediate activations and gradients. In over-the-air SL, the wireless channel serves as an inter-layer linear map, and when the forward and backward channels match, reciprocity and conjugation supply the backward product without channel estimation at the base station (BS). Passive user motion, which the learning link does not control, breaks this match. Movable antennas let the antenna move relative to the user device, and we use this freedom to compensate the displacement. For a stationary BS and a propagation environment quasi-static within each exchange, returning the antenna to its forward-transmission position restores the channel and yields a conditionally unbiased gradient estimate. We also derive when discrete positioning or mechanical movement can achieve this in time. A residual displacement below a quarter wavelength keeps the real part of the channel correlation positive for any angular spectrum. At zero effective offset, independent Gaussian jitter attenuates this correlation without reversing its sign, whereas a persistent offset can reverse it, and in arrays the tolerance depends on the receive-combining direction. These effects enter a nonconvex convergence bound, and a local analysis shows that partial mechanical compensation saves cycle time to first order at only a second-order loss in correlation. In CIFAR-10 experiments, a user terminal without channel state information stays at chance level under uncompensated walking motion, while discrete positioning stays within about 0.3 percentage points of exact restoration, including at a speed beyond the modeled actuator's limit.
Signal Processing.comment: v2: revised/extended; new title (v1: "Keep Pace to Learn: Movable Antennas Restore the Backpropagated Gradient Under User Mobility"); added coauthor Zhaoyang Zhang. Same research question/system model; expanded analysis/experiments. Extended manuscript submitted to IEEE JSAC; Appendices C-K omitted from journal submission for space. 22 pages, 15 figures, 10 tables

Signal Processing.title: mmWave UE Positioning Under Blockage: Limits for ISAC-Assisted Handover
Signal Processing.summary: Proactive handover can save a millimeter-wave (mmWave) link before a passing body blocks it, but only if the network knows where the user is. We ask whether the radio units that serve a user can localize it accurately enough from its uplink sounding reference signals. We derive position error bounds that include synchronization and array calibration errors, with and without reflected paths known from a digital twin, and test two estimators in a ray-traced street canyon on held-out scenarios. Three findings stand out. First, with line of sight to both radio units, array calibration, not bandwidth, limits the bound. Second, blockage degrades the line-of-sight-only bound sharply, whereas known reflections keep the map-aided bound low. Third, a simple dominant-path estimator fails where it matters most: its errors grow sharply around blockage, and proactive handover becomes worse than the 3GPP baseline. A map-aided multipath tracker cuts the median error from 12 to 3.7 cm and removes this significant penalty at link margins of 15 dB and above, but does not yet beat the baseline.

Signal Processing.title: Sense Less, Miss Less: Evidence-Driven Sensing Schedules for ISAC
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) lets a base station detect human motion with the same signals it uses for data, but every sensing transmission takes resources from users.
