After two-stage PPO, the best GTAC policy outperforms the non-real-time teacher by 11.6% in carrier SE, while exceeding its PF utility and preserving the cell-edge throughput. A CUDA implementation of GTAC achieves a 69.6 us inference latency on an RTX PRO 4500 GPU, below the targeted 100 us inference budget in practical systems.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

Signal Processing.title: Distributed Cross-Layer Optimization for Covert Multi-Hop, Multi-Modal Networks: Exponentially Fast Convergence and Robust Tracking
Signal Processing.summary: This paper develops the first distributed cross-layer algorithm for joint congestion control, routing, scheduling, and power control in covert multi-hop, multi-modal wireless networks, where adversarial wardens (Willies) monitor radio modalities via energy detection. The Detection Error Probability (DEP), the probability that a Willie fails to reliably detect ongoing transmissions, is generally non-concave in the transmit powers, making DEP-based covert network optimization challenging. We resolve this by constructing the tightest concave lower bound on the log-DEP, yielding a conservative convex problem that guarantees satisfaction of the original DEP constraints and unifies hard covertness constraints and covertness-utility maximization in a single problem. We develop a Parallel Proximal Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (PP-ADMM) algorithm for the resulting cross-layer problem and prove global Q-linear convergence, i.e., exponentially fast convergence, to the set of optimal solutions under standard regularity conditions. Numerical results confirm linear convergence and demonstrate robust tracking performance under channel fading and Willie mobility.
Signal Processing.comment: 18 pages, 6 figures. Full technical report corresponding to the paper accepted to IEEE MILCOM 2026

Signal Processing.title: Timely Ground-Station Status Delivery via UAV-Assisted Data Collection and Hierarchical RL
Signal Processing.summary: We consider a UAV-assisted status-update system in which a rotary-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) collects updates from multiple sensors, stores the newest update of each sensor, and forwards selected buffered updates to a ground station (GS). We minimize a weighted sum of the time-average GS-side age of information (AoI) and UAV energy consumption over a finite horizon. The optimization is subject to half-duplex operation, sensor and UAV energy-causality constraints, transmission-rate and power limits, and a terminal-location constraint. Because collection changes the information age at the UAV but does not reduce the GS-side AoI until the buffered update is forwarded, mobility, collection, and forwarding decisions are coupled over time. We use a hierarchical AoI-energy actor-critic (HAE-AC) controller in which a coarse-timescale actor selects return-feasible UAV movements, while a deterministic per-slot scheduler constructs feasible collection or forwarding sets and assigns the minimum transmit power required for each scheduled transmission. In a 100-sensor deployment, HAE-AC reduces the average GS-side AoI by about 22% relative to an adaptive staleness-gated benchmark. Compared with forward-upon-collection, selective buffered forwarding reduces the number of downlink bursts by roughly 30% while increasing the number of collections per sensor by more than 23%.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures. Author's accepted manuscript. Accepted for publication in the proceedings of the 2026 Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers

Signal Processing.title: Beyond TR 38.811 for 6G NTN Channel Models
Signal Processing.summary: As the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) expands 6G non-terrestrial network (NTN) to S, Ku, and Ka bands for integration with existing terrestrial cellular networks, the necessary satellite channel model for link and network performance evaluation remains tied to TR 38.811, last revised in 2020. We identify issues on multiple fronts: inappropriate parameter specifications based on very limited site-specific environments considered, omission of satellite-induced Doppler spread and directional antenna effects and lack of a transparent channel model generation procedure. To address these limitations, we re-derive the channel parameters using ray tracing (RT) over urban and rural environments based on ITU-R building statistics. Our results show that TR 38.811 substantially overestimates the K-factor at low elevations and predicts a decreasing trend with elevation, which is inconsistent with RT. The Ka-band clutter loss (CL) also exceeds the RT estimates by more than 15 dB in urban cases. It also underestimates rural delay spread (DS) at low elevations and predicts an elevation trend inconsistent with RT. We further quantify the previously neglected satellite-induced Doppler spread. Finally, we demonstrate that the conventional TR 38.811 channel generator significantly underestimates the K-factor in the presence of directional antenna (beamforming), while our modified generator substantially reduces this discrepancy.

Signal Processing.title: HHK: A Hardware-Oriented Cross-Location PPG Key Generation Architecture for Body Area Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Body area networks (BANs) require session keys that wearable nodes establish without user interaction and with proof that both nodes are on the same body. This paper presents a multi-site photoplethysmography (PPG) key-agreement processor for BANs, incorporating signal conditioning, band-pass filtering, pulse onset detection, beat alignment, Gray-coded quantization and a polar-code fuzzy commitment. The algorithm reaches 95.6% key agreement on resting wrist and fingertip recordings, and on 16 ambulatory participants the processor reaches 69.2, 54.8 and 50.0% between head and wrist, wrist and ankle, and head and ankle, respectively, against 2.3% for the best of five prior methods. Implemented and tested on an AMD XC7Z020 FPGA, the processor consumes 261 $μ$W. Synthesized with the NanGate 45 nm library, it occupies 0.394 mm$^2$, operates at up to 258 MHz and requires 0.208 $μ$J per decoding. We further attack the system and show that the public helper data reveals more bits than the inter-beat intervals carry, so an eavesdropper who knows only the mean heart rate recovers 39.4% of the session keys. To our knowledge, the processor is the first synthesizable RTL architecture for inter-beat-interval-based PPG key agreement in BANs evaluated on free-living ambulatory data.

Signal Processing.title: TransfoRhythm: A Transformer Architecture Conductive to Blood Pressure Estimation via Solo PPG Signal Capturing
Signal Processing.summary: Recent statistics indicate that approximately 1.3 billion individuals worldwide suffer from hypertension, a leading cause of premature death globally. Blood Pressure (BP) serves as a critical health indicator for accurate and timely diagnosis and/or treatment of hypertension. Traditional BP measurement methods rely on cuff-based approaches, which lack real-time, continuous, and reliable BP estimates, crucial for the timely diagnosis/treatment of hypertension. Driven by recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), there has been a surge of interest in developing data-driven and cuff-less BP estimation solutions. In this context, current literature predominantly focuses on coupling Electrocardiography (ECG) and Photoplethysmography (PPG) sensors, though this approach is constrained by reliance on multiple sensor types. An alternative, utilizing standalone PPG signals, presents challenges due to the absence of auxiliary sensors (ECG), requiring the use of morphological features while addressing motion artifacts and high-frequency noise. To address these issues, the paper introduces the TransfoRhythm framework, a Transformer-based DNN architecture built upon the recently released physiological database, MIMIC-IV. Leveraging the Multi-Head Attention (MHA) mechanism, TransfoRhythm identifies dependencies and similarities across data segments, forming a robust framework for cuff-less BP estimation solely using PPG signals. To our knowledge, this paper represents the first study to apply the MIMIC IV dataset for cuff-less BP estimation. TransfoRhythm achieves highly accurate results with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of [2.21, 1.84] and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of [1.37, 1.06] for systolic and diastolic blood pressures, respectively.

Signal Processing.title: Data-Driven Spectrum Access Technologies for 6G
Signal Processing.summary: The surge in global mobile traffic, driven by 5G adoption and emerging applications, necessitates new spectrum allocations for 6G systems. With most major swaths of spectrum below 15 GHz already allocated to other services, co-existence between cellular and incumbent services such as satellite or radar systems is critical to make such spectrum accessible for 6G. At the same time, the advent of artificial intelligence offers a new opportunity for designing more efficient spectrum sharing techniques. This paper presents four novel data-driven spectrum access techniques to enable efficient use of spectrum for the 6G era: 1) co-existence technique for efficient protection of fixed incumbent receivers within an established protection area; 2) data-driven approach for protecting satellite receivers via control of radiated power above the horizon; 3) spectrum sensing-based fast-time-scale physical resource block blanking; and 4) base station-based spectrum occupancy detection to enable fast-time-scale spectrum sharing with satellite and non-terrestrial network incumbents. These techniques leverage artificial intelligence and extreme multiple-input multiple-output capabilities to enable efficient spectrum co-existence/sharing while maintaining cellular network performance.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted for publication in the IEEE Communications Magazine

Signal Processing.title: Single-visit screening for intracochlear tissue growth validated against multi-visit electrical measurement changes
Signal Processing.summary: Purpose: Tissue growth (TG) around cochlear implant electrodes raises impedance but is not reliably visible on CT scans. Routinely recorded stimulus current-induced non-stimulating electrode voltages (SCINSEVs) carry this information, but a single recording has no patient-specific reference. We present an algorithm for detecting signs of significant TG from a single SCINSEV measurement. Methods: TG is assumed to concentrate basally near the electrode insertion site, leaving the apical region mostly unaffected. A patient-specific forward model built from CT is fitted to the apical measurements and predicts the basal ones. The misfit score, T, measures each basal contact's signed relative misfit against the apical misfit, accounting for apical fit quality and measurement noise. An ear is flagged when two adjacent basal contacts cross a predetermined threshold. We compare T with T-delta, a model-free reference, tracking basal relative to apical SCINSEV change since the intra-operative recording, persisting over the last two visits. Results: T had a false-positive rate of 3% on growth-free ears. It agreed with T-delta in 81% of 68 ears (sensitivity 71%; specificity 86%; p = 6e-6). Over 200 patient-level two-fold splits, median held-out agreement was 78% at a false-positive rate of 5.1%. Conclusion: An apically fitted patient-specific model predicts basal SCINSEVs well enough to flag signs of significant TG at a single visit, without an intra-operative baseline. Detections largely agree with persistent multi-visit basal-versus-apical change, a surrogate ground truth for significant TG.

Signal Processing.title: Thought-deciphering via hierarchical EEG-to-text alignment
Signal Processing.summary: Communication is important for our well-being, but it can be impaired by disabilities, such as locked-in syndrome (LIS), cerebral palsy (CP), and dysarthria. Non-invasive brain-to-text brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) offer a promising solution by providing an alternative communication pathway for people with communication disabilities. However, most recent breakthroughs have relied on large, cumbersome, and costly neuroimaging modalities, such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and magnetoencephalography (MEG). Numerous studies have attempted decoding using the lighter and cheaper electroencephalography (EEG), but the results remain inferior compared to the other modalities. More importantly, we do not understand how these modalities are related to text at the letter, word, sentence, and higher semantic levels. Many prior studies have focused on decoding below the sentence level because it is considerably easier to design an experiment around phonemes, letters, and words. However, during communication, sentences play a much more important role than words and letters. This is because sentences carry information at such a high level that they can be understood even if some words and letters are missing. However, within sentence-level decoding, sentence classification is not as well investigated as sentence generation, making it difficult to decide whether a sentence should be retrieved or generated in the context of EEG-to-text decoding. This paper strives to investigate sentence-level EEG-to-text classification via a novel hierarchical alignment framework, where the main goal is to retrieve a read sentence using its context and EEG as inputs.

Signal Processing.title: Quantum Private Information Retrieval on Forests
Signal Processing.summary: We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting. We focus on a specific type of graphs, namely the forest graphs. A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees. We consider the quantum setting where all the servers share an entangled state. Each server is allowed to send only one qudit per retrieval round. We design a scheme for the forest graphs that achieves the rate of $\frac{3}{N}$. The scheme uses a GHZ state as the initial entangled state between the servers prior to the scheme initiation. We compare our scheme with the only work done in the literature that considered the quantum setting of graph PIR. We show that our scheme is more efficient in this setting. We derive the quantum capacity for the case of $G=3K_2$, which is equal to $4/6$. $G=3K_2$ is a special case of the forest graph. We design a scheme that is specialized for this graph, achieving a rate equal to $4/6$ and provide the corresponding matching upper bound, establishing it as the capacity.

Signal Processing.title: ST-GFM: Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting with Measured Perturbation Bounds and Masked Spectral Reconstruction
Signal Processing.summary: Graph forecasters for sensor networks are trained in one regime and deployed in others, where sensor coupling and signal frequency content both change. We split this spectral shift into an operator channel and a frequency channel, each with a dimensionless measure. ST-GFM (Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting Model) filters every input step with Chebyshev and bidirectional diffusion filters on one learned, non-symmetric operator and alternates them with per-node temporal attention. For the operator channel we prove Frobenius-norm perturbation bounds for both graph branches, show that the Chebyshev bound is attained to first order, and compute its constant from the trained weights and the measured operator norm: 17.9 on METR-LA and 21.5 on PEMS-BAY. Under random edge dropout the trained layer moves by 2.0% to 3.1% of this bound. Masked Spectral Reconstruction (MSR), a self-supervised loss active in the first 40 epochs, matches the log power spectrum of the encoder output to that of the input. For small log-spectral residuals on unclamped bins it is proportional to an Itakura-Saito divergence to leading order. Removing it raises the 60-minute MAE by 0.30 on METR-LA, close to the 0.33 lost when all three self-supervised losses go. Under one shared evaluation pipeline, the 60-minute MAE of ST-GFM is 3.5% below a retrained STAEformer on METR-LA and 13.0% below it on PEMS-BAY. Its 60-minute MAE is 3.0980.017 on METR-LA (five seeds) and 1.5760.006 on PEMS-BAY (three seeds), the lowest PEMS-BAY MAE among twelve published baselines.
Signal Processing.comment: 21 Pages, 11 Figures, 12 Tables, Supplementary Materials attached, Under Review

Signal Processing.title: Receiver-Domain Behavioral Probing for Backdoor-Resilient Federated GPS Spoofing Detection in UAV Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Federated learning (FL) allows unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) fleets to train a shared GPS spoofing detector without exchanging raw receiver observations. Some UAV-FL schemes use client-reported performance to determine aggregation weights, which allows compromised clients to manipulate their influence on the global model. We study an attack in which two of ten clients poison part of their data, scale their model updates, and inflate their reported accuracy. The accuracy-weighted rule produces a backdoor lift of +0.3036, compared with +0.2415 for attacked FedAvg. To address this vulnerability, we develop receiver-domain behavioral probing. The coordinator evaluates submitted models on counterfactual spoofed samples constructed by assigning benign values to discriminative GPS features and computes trust from the models' responses without using reported accuracy. With independent and identically distributed (IID) client data, our method reduces backdoor lift to -0.0265 and flags the compromised clients. It assumes an honest majority but does not require a configured Byzantine-tolerance parameter. When the number of attackers exceeds the tolerance configured for Multi-Krum, its lift increases from +0.0061 to +0.2837, whereas our method remains close to the honest baseline. We evaluate the approach using a public single-receiver dataset partitioned into simulated UAV clients and examine its limitations under strong client heterogeneity.
Signal Processing.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Signal Processing.title: ISAC-Assisted Proactive Handover in mmWave Networks: Value of Foresight and Localization Requirements
Signal Processing.summary: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) links can lose tens of decibels within milliseconds when a person or vehicle crosses the line of sight, and reactive handover recovers only after the outage has begun. Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) promises to let the network see blockers coming and move users to another cell in advance. This paper asks how much such foresight is worth relative to the best reactive handover, and what sensing accuracy is needed to harvest it. We formulate cost-aware cell selection with knowledge of the future signal-to- noise ratio as a sequential decision problem, define the value of foresight through a policy-independent bound, and develop an ISAC-assisted handover framework in which a radio unit senses blockers with its own communication waveform and a simulated Open RAN xApp plans handovers. Ray-traced experiments in a 28 GHz street canyon, reported on held-out scenarios, show that, with a short look-ahead, perfect foresight closes most of the gap between service-aware (Layer-3) reactive handover and an instantaneous oracle. Harvesting this value, however, requires the user and nearby blockers to be localized to about a decimeter, well beyond what our radar tracker and meter- level user positioning provide; with realistic errors, even an uncertainty-aware planner largely defers to reactive handover.

Signal Processing.title: GIST: Location-Dependent Uplink Path Structure Transfer for FDD Downlink Channel Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: A key challenge of downlink (DL) channel estimation in frequency division duplex (FDD) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems is the pilot overhead, which grows with the numbers of antennas and subcarriers. However, a prior on path delays and directions shared by the uplink (UL) and DL channels can reduce this overhead. A model trained only on UL channels measured at a base station (BS) can predict the path structure (delays, directions and power gains) from the location of a user equipment (UE) and thereby assist DL channel estimation. In this paper, we propose Gaussian-Informed Structure Transfer (GIST), in which each Gaussian primitive models one propagation path, whose delay, directions and power gain are predicted from the UE location relative to the primitive center. The complex gains of the predicted paths are estimated from DL pilots by linear minimum mean square error estimation with this prior. Experiments on a ray-traced and a measured dataset show that GIST outperforms all baselines, reaching a lower DL estimation error with fewer pilot subcarriers. Further experiments demonstrate its robustness to UE location errors, its low storage and computational requirements.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

Signal Processing.title: Octree-Context Gaussian Splatting with Multi-Order Propagation for Channel Knowledge Maps
Signal Processing.summary: Channel knowledge maps (CKMs) can support environment-aware wireless communications by providing site-specific channel knowledge as a function of the transmitter position, the receiver position or both. Existing Gaussian splatting CKM methods can reduce the high training and inference costs of implicit neural methods yet represent all multipath interactions by one wireless radiance field. We propose octree-context Gaussian splatting (OctCGS), which anchors Gaussian primitives on an octree as virtual scattering nodes and decomposes multi-bounce propagation into orders by the number of node-level interactions along each path. Shared tree attention gives each node local context from neighboring octree cells and room-wide context from ancestor cells at a cost linear in the number of cells, and the order-wise scattering of each node is predicted from this context. The order-wise contributions of the power transported between the nodes are summed in power with a line-of-sight (LoS) term to give the channel gain and the spatial spectrum. OctCGS raises the spatial-spectrum structural similarity (SSIM) by 0.13 to 0.23 and lowers the mean absolute error (MAE) of the channel gain by 0.9 to 3.8 dB on five indoor ray-tracing scenes, relative to the best baseline per scene and metric.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

Signal Processing.title: G-NAC: Graph Neural Automata Clustering via Emergent Domain Formation
Signal Processing.summary: We introduce Graph Neural Automata Clustering (G-NAC), an unsupervised clustering method in which observations interact as cells on a fixed neighborhood graph. A shared recurrent graph-neural cellular rule evolves latent domain states through local interactions, which are converted into a rank-based spectral affinity for partitioning. Across 73 clustering tasks from 57 benchmark datasets, G-NAC achieved a mean adjusted Rand index (ARI) of 0.7951, comparable to Genie at 0.7941 and higher than the other evaluated baselines. Empirical training time and GPU memory scaled approximately linearly from 5,000 to 100,000 nodes. Learned transition rules also transferred from smaller source graphs to independent 100,000-node samples generated under matched conditions. These results demonstrate a recurrent graph-clustering formulation while identifying dependencies on graph quality, readout design, and source-target similarity.
Signal Processing.comment: 39 pages, 2 figures

Signal Processing.title: Multi-User Precoding with Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces via Neural Reparameterization
Signal Processing.summary: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) enable wave-domain signal processing, and provide a promising architecture for enhancing spectral efficiency in multi-user wireless communication systems. However, jointly optimizing transmit power and multi-layer phase shifts in SIM-assisted wireless systems under quality-of-service (QoS) constraints results in a large-scale nonconvex problem, for which conventional numerical optimization-based methods, such as alternating optimization (AO), suffer from high computational burden and limited scalability. In this paper, we develop a QoS constraint-aware neural reparameterization framework for SIM-assisted downlink precoding. By embedding the cascaded wave-propagation structure of the SIM into a model-based differentiable architecture, both the phase shift configuration and transmit power allocation are reparameterized as parameters of a structured neural model that inherently satisfies feasibility constraints of the original problem. The resulting formulation enables efficient optimization that does not rely on a channel-to-precoding mapping learned through offline training. Instead, it directly updates the reparameterized optimization variables to realize real-time precoding for any channel realization. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior sum rate performance under QoS constraints, while significantly improving computational efficiency compared with conventional numerical optimization approaches.
Signal Processing.comment: 15 pages, 9 figures, Submitted to an IEEE journal for publication

Signal Processing.title: Non-Coherent Over-the-Air Distributed Consensus: Algorithm Design and Power Control Optimization
Signal Processing.summary: Non-coherent over-the-air (NCOTA) aggregation offers a scalable and communication-efficient approach to distributed average consensus in wireless networks, without requiring instantaneous channel state information (CSI) or phase alignment. However, persistent aggregation errors pose fundamental challenges in achieving exact average consensus under nominal distributed averaging protocols. In this paper, we develop an NCOTA consensus framework that accommodates row-stochastic mixing, without requiring the conventional average-preservation property of doubly stochastic mixing matrices. Building on a distributed optimization formulation of average consensus, we propose a decentralized projected gradient descent with row-stochastic mixing (DPGD-RS) algorithm and establish its mean-square convergence to the exact average of the agents' initial states. We further derive a closed-form upper bound on the mean-square consensus error, characterizing the effects of aggregation uncertainty, network connectivity, and mixing imbalance. Guided by this analysis, we propose a spectral-reshaping power control (SR-PC) scheme that jointly optimizes transmit powers and receive-scaling factors to accelerate convergence by balancing aggregation accuracy and network mixing. Numerical results validate the theoretical convergence guarantees and demonstrate that the proposed power control scheme significantly accelerates convergence compared with full-power transmission and spectral-radius-minimization benchmarks.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages, 4 figures. Extended version of a paper published in Proc. IEEE ICC 2025

Signal Processing.title: Empirical Ciphertext Distinguishability Testing of KEMs and Hybrid Encryption via Deep Learning
Signal Processing.summary: We model indistinguishability under chosen-plaintext attack (IND-CPA) games as binary classification tasks for deep neural networks (DNNs). We apply this methodology to the public-key encryption (PKE) schemes used to construct PQC key encapsulation mechanisms (KEMs) such as ML-KEM and HQC, and to cascaded symmetric algorithms, demonstrating methodological generality. Moreover, we present a novel extension of this approach to empirical distinguishability testing of hybrid KEMs. For IND-CPA-secure schemes and their combinations, no DNN achieves accuracy significantly different from random guessing (measured via Bonferroni-corrected binomial tests), consistent with theoretical security guarantees. For insecure schemes, such as plain RSA, AES-CTR and AES-CBC with IV or counter reuse, or RC4, the DNNs classify the ciphertexts better than random guessing. Thus, this framework is shown to serve as a practical, scheme-agnostic tool for flagging distinguishable ciphertexts in both individual and composed constructions.

Signal Processing.title: Joint Data Association and Tracking for Surveillance Radar Using Gaussian Processes
Signal Processing.summary:
The growing presence of unmanned aerial vehicles or drones has increased the necessity of developing methods to detect and track them to secure restricted airspaces. This can be done using radars which is a common sensor around e.g. airports, an emerging method to track targets is by using Gaussian processes. However, false alarms is ever present in radars especially if tracking weak targets complicating the data association task.
  We propose a joint data association and tracking algorithm for a single target using a variational Bayesian approach to approximate the full posterior of both the association variable as well as the track. We show that the proposed algorithm outperforms a state of the art data association and tracking algorithm in the form of a Bernoulli filter, as well as the classical Kalman filter, for a large range of detection probabilities.

Signal Processing.title: HoloTrace: a Location Privacy-Preserving Framework for mmWave MIMO-OFDM Systems
Signal Processing.summary: High-resolution radio localization is becoming increasingly important for next-generation vehicular and mobile networks, enabling infrastructure-assisted positioning for connected and automated mobility. However, the same mmWave multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) links used for communication may allow a serving base station (BS) to infer the location of a vehicle-mounted or mobile user equipment (UE) from routine uplink pilot transmissions, even without an explicit positioning request. This paper introduces HoloTrace, a signal-level location-privacy framework for single-BS localization in mmWave MIMO-OFDM systems. HoloTrace modifies user-side pilot symbols while keeping the analog precoder fixed to bias localization-relevant channel features, including angle of arrival (AoA), angle of departure (AoD), and time difference of arrival (TDoA), toward a prescribed fictitious geometry. We formulate pilot-level spoofing as a subspace projection-based signal design problem and derive closed-form oracle designs assuming UE-side channel-gain knowledge. We further develop blind designs that operate without complex path-gain information, while relying on geometric side information, and explicitly characterize their limitations in multipath scenarios. Simulation results with a two-path single-anchor geometry show that oracle HoloTrace can steer the inferred position toward a desired spoofed location, whereas blind variants mainly provide obfuscation or approximate spoofing due to angle-delay pairing ambiguities. The communication impact is geometry-dependent rather than intrinsic to the proposed method: selecting a spoofed location compatible with the serving beams can preserve channel-rate quality while providing effective location privacy.
Signal Processing.comment: submitted to IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology (IEEE TVT)

Signal Processing.title: Harnessing Mutual Coupling in Cell-Free mMIMO
Signal Processing.summary: This letter investigates a cell-free massive MIMO system with $L$ access points (APs), each employing a small fixed-form-factor, uniform linear array of $N$ potentially closely spaced antennas. Utilizing multiport communication theory, we analyze the impact of mutual coupling on uplink and downlink spectral efficiency (SE) under various impedance-matching strategies. We compare two deployment regimes: ($i$) increasing $N$ while $L$ is kept fixed, and ($ii$) increasing $N$ while fixing the total antenna count $M = NL$. Numerical results show that, with a full matching network, mutual coupling itself becomes beneficial when an AP serves several user equipments, which is the typical operating regime of user-centric cell-free networks. Furthermore, with full matching, antenna densification can enhance SE or allow for a reduction in the number of APs without performance loss. Since full matching networks remain of manageable size in the small arrays of distributed APs, unlike in large centralized arrays, cell-free networks offer a natural setting for exploiting mutual coupling.

Signal Processing.title: A Tightly Coupled Magnetic-Inertial SLAM System for Field Robots
Signal Processing.summary: Field robots operating in mines, tunnels, and disaster areas require reliable localization despite GNSS denial and degraded camera and LiDAR measurements caused by dust, smoke, or poor illumination. Missions involving both ground and aerial robots further motivate complementary sensing modalities that do not depend on visibility, preinstalled infrastructure, or wheel contact. This letter presents MISLAM, a tightly coupled magnetic-inertial simultaneous localization and mapping system using an IMU and a nine-magnetometer array, without relying on external odometry or platform-specific motion assumptions. The system combines the inertial navigation model with local polynomial magnetic-field models for short-term motion estimation and a global Gaussian process model for drift correction using an error-state Kalman filter. Offline evaluation on three indoor datasets collected with a handheld rig shows reductions in total endpoint closure error of 45.7% - 78.0% relative to magnetic-inertial odometry. Under poor illumination, MISLAM maintains tracking after visual-inertial odometry fails, achieving a horizontal closure error of 0.332 m, although vertical drift remains a limitation. These results support magnetic-inertial SLAM as a complementary localization modality for robotic sensor suites operating under degraded visual conditions.

Signal Processing.title: Resilient Cell-Free MIMO ISAC Under Uncertainties: An Impairment-Aware Graph Neural Network Framework
Signal Processing.summary: Beamforming designs for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in cell-free multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems face the challenge to stay reliable under uncertainties from both channel state information (CSI) as well as clutter. To this end, this paper proposes an impairment-aware heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN) framework for beamforming that obtains the CSI error level and the clutter covariance as edge features, which enables a single trained model to adapt to both impairments. In particular, the GNN is trained on a low quantile of the minimum user rate with a clutter-aware signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio, balanced by a normalized Tchebycheff scalarization. Simulation results show that the proposed GNN framework outperforms the considered baselines in sensing-only and communication-only settings. Depending on the operating point, a single GNN model attains approximately 97\% of each baseline's rate while serving both functionalities at once. The model further generalizes to unseen CSI error levels and clutter counts and renders the ISAC system resilient.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 1 table, submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

Signal Processing.title: How Temporal Dispersion of Radio Channels Depends on Signal Bandwidth
Signal Processing.summary: The degree of temporal dispersion of a radio channel is the basis for assessing its transmission capabilities. This paper addresses the practical issue of measuring the temporal parameters of a signal transmitted in the millimeter-wave (38 GHz) range. These parameters provide the basis for assessing the degree of dispersion of the received signal. The measurement results show that both the mean and RMS values of the delay spread depend on the distance between the transmitter and receiver as well as the bandwidth of the transmitted signals. The function description of these relationships (model) is determined based on a statistical analysis of the obtained measurement data obtained in a selected indoor corridor under line-of-sight conditions.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables, 6 equations

Signal Processing.title: Hotplug Coded Caching: Uncoded versus Row-Wise Coded Placements
Signal Processing.summary: In the hotplug coded caching model, $K$ users fill their caches of size $M$ as a function of $N$ files, but only an unknown subset of $A\leq K$ users is active in the delivery phase. In all regimes where the optimal hotplug tradeoff is known, it depends only on $A$, not on $K$; whether this holds in general is open. We show that: (i) Under uncoded placement, YMA delivery with MAN placement, where offline users are assigned the demands of active users, is optimal. Hence, offline users cause a strict load penalty at intermediate memory sizes, while the MAN placement is optimal for every number of active users; (ii) Under row-wise placement (RWP), where each cache is a function of the user's own row of each file, every classical scheme can be embedded in a Reed-Solomon code. The resulting hotplug scheme has the tradeoff of the classical model with $A$ users, for every $A\leq K$: there is no load penalty, but the placement depends on $K$. We then derive a converse for RWP, which shows that: (a) for $2\leq N\leq A$, the scheme of Gomez-Vilardebo (GV) is RWP optimal for $AM\leq N/(N-1)$, which settles the RWP tradeoff for $N=2$; (b) YMA is RWP optimal at $AM=N$; and (c) for $N=A=3$, GV is RWP optimal for $M\leq 1$. Hence, the Reed-Solomon embeddings of these schemes are optimal among embedded RWP schemes.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to ICC 2027

Signal Processing.title: A Survey on Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces: Fundamentals, Recent Advances, and Challenges
Signal Processing.summary: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) cascade several closely spaced programmable metasurface layers so that an electromagnetic wave undergoes repeated modulation-propagation interactions before leaving the stack. The stack thereby implements, at the speed of propagation and with few radio-frequency chains, high-dimensional analog transformations that would otherwise require digital precoding, combining, spatial filtering, focusing, or inference. Since 2023, SIM research has produced more than two hundred articles, a dedicated magazine special issue, and two survey-level overviews organized around applications and wave-domain computing. This article complements them with a model-to-hardware perspective. First, we present the electromagnetic modeling hierarchy of SIMs, making explicit the assumptions under which the models coincide, their validity regimes, and their computational complexity, with a common notation for hardware non-idealities and power consumption. Second, we present a methodology-first taxonomy (SIM-aware channel acquisition, model-based optimization, statistical-CSI design, learning-based control, and hardware-aware robust design), compare the families in terms of CSI requirements, complexity, convergence, and hardware constraints, and reconcile conflicting findings in the literature. Third, we synthesize applications by the physical role of the SIM. Fourth, we quantitatively compare experimentally demonstrated multilayer prototypes, separate validated from conceptual architectures, and discuss thermal, tolerance, and calibration issues. Fifth, we provide a tutorial-style performance and trade-off analysis anchored in reported results. Finally, we map evidence-based challenges to research directions with measurable targets. Lessons learned are summarized at the end of every section.

Signal Processing.title: Joint Communications, Sensing, and Positioning in 6G Multi-Functional Satellite Systems: Survey and Open Challenges
Signal Processing.summary: Satellite systems are expected to be a cornerstone of sixth-generation (6G) networks, supporting communications, sensing, and positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) with global coverage. This survey develops a framework for multi-functional satellite systems (MFSS), which combine at least two of these services through shared or jointly designed payload resources. A two-dimensional taxonomy distinguishes the functional configuration---joint communications and sensing (JCAS), joint communications and PNT (JCAP), joint sensing and PNT (JSAP), or joint communications, sensing, and PNT (JCSAP)---from the integration depth---cooperative, integrated, or joint. After consolidating the communication, sensing, and PNT fundamentals and payload architectures into a single background section, the survey examines the three integration levels and then devotes a dedicated section to each configuration, covering its architecture, classification, state of the art, advantages, key challenges, and research directions. The achievable performance of each configuration is illustrated with representative trade-off results from the literature and compared across configurations, the differences between terrestrial multi-functional networks and satellite MFSS are made explicit, and a life-cycle techno-economic framework balances hardware, spectrum, launch, and operational reuse against engineering, qualification, verification, and common-mode risks. The analysis shows that deeper integration can improve resource utilization and functional synergy, but is not automatically the technical or economic optimum for every mission.

Signal Processing.title: Leakage-Aware Encrypted Semantic Communication with Key-Conditioned Signal Perturbation
Signal Processing.summary: Encrypted semantic communication systems protect transmitted messages by inserting key-conditioned modules into a deep-learning semantic communication pipeline, but existing designs rely on a fixed adversarial weight and operate mainly at the semantic-feature level. We propose two changes to the encrypted semantic communication system (ESCS): a key-conditioned signal-domain perturbation layer, called learned adversarial perturbation injection (LAPI), and an information noise-contrastive estimation (InfoNCE)-guided adaptive training rule that {adds an adaptive leakage penalty alongside the fixed adversarial objective} using an InfoNCE-based proxy for mutual information leakage. Experiments on the Europarl corpus over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Rayleigh fading channels show that InfoNCE-guided training is the primary source of eavesdropper suppression, reducing the eavesdropper's bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU) score to approximately 0.07 at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Adding LAPI to the InfoNCE-guided objective further lowers the InfoNCE-estimated leakage by 5-9% with low measured inference overhead, while its impact on legitimate-receiver BLEU depends on channel conditions. The two mechanisms operate on different parts of the pipeline and can be jointly applied.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted for presentation at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026

Signal Processing.title: Electromagnetic Information Theory for Programmable Metasurfaces
Signal Processing.summary: Programmable metasurfaces enable fine-grained control of electromagnetic waves and are creating new opportunities for information extraction, information transfer and information processing. Yet, despite exciting experimental demonstrations, their fundamental capabilities remain poorly understood. In this Perspective, we argue that programmable metasurfaces, and programmable wave systems more generally, call for an electromagnetic information theory that addresses limits at two levels, in a unified manner across applications like communications, sensing and computing. First, for a given physical platform, such a theory should bound achievable information manipulations, such as sensing precision, information-transfer rates, and computational performance. Second, at a more fundamental level, it should determine what non-programmable and programmable physical resources bound these system-specific limits, and what minimum resources are required to attain a prescribed level of performance. We discuss emerging theoretical approaches to these questions, and their connection to experimentally realizable systems. We examine how device thickness, programmable degrees of freedom, nonlocality, coupling and multiple scattering constrain these limits. Establishing the envisioned framework could clarify the ultimate capabilities of programmable metasurfaces and guide the design of future wave-based information systems.
Signal Processing.comment: 17 pages with 3 figures

Signal Processing.title: Asymptotic Frequency-Domain FIM for multidimensional stationary and cyclostationary compound-Gaussian processes: Application to DOA estimation
Signal Processing.summary: The classical Whittle formula provides a closed-form expression for the asymptotic Fisher information matrix (FIM) of stationary, zero-mean Gaussian processes (GPs) with finite-dimensional parameterizations, expressed in terms of their power spectra. While this result was recently extended to nonzero-mean, multidimensional, real-valued stationary compound-Gaussian processes (CGPs), its applicability remains limited. In this paper, we significantly broaden this theoretical framework with two primary contributions. First, we extend the Whittle formula to purely cyclostationary real-valued CGPs with parameterized cyclic spectra, and further generalize it to circular and noncircular complex-valued multidimensional stationary CGPs, encompassing both purely and almost cyclostationary CGPs. Second, we apply these novel Whittle-type formulas to evaluate the impact of source spectral characteristics on the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation, particularly in scenarios involving frequency offsets.

Signal Processing.title: Localization MSE Analysis for Cooperative OFDM-ISAC
Signal Processing.summary: This paper develops a receiver-specific mean-squared-error (MSE) framework for cooperative integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) localization using random orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) payloads. It captures local peak perturbations and incorrect ambiguity-peak acquisition for two classical receiver processing schemes: matched filtering (MF) and reciprocal filtering (RF). For scatterers well separated in delay, we quantify how frequency spread and interference induced by symbol-energy fluctuations affect local delay errors under MF. RF removes symbol-dependent weighting but amplifies noise for low-energy symbols. Payload-conditioned joint Gaussian delay profiles yield peak-selection probabilities, which combine with nonlinear multistatic fusion errors to approximate position MSE while accounting for network geometry. Numerical results illustrate receiver-dependent estimation errors and the benefits of frequency-dependent constellation allocation.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, submit to IEEE for possible publication

Signal Processing.title: Movable Antenna-Assisted Secret Key Generation over Temporally Correlated Channels
Signal Processing.summary: Physical-layer key generation (PLKG) exploits reciprocal channel dynamics to generate symmetric keys, addressing the key distribution problem in wireless communications. However, strong temporal correlation in slow-fading environments limits fresh randomness and results in low key generation rates. Movable antennas (MAs) introduce spatial degrees of freedom through antenna repositioning, providing a new approach to addressing the limitation. This paper investigates MA-assisted PLKG over temporally correlated channels. A first-order Gauss-Markov process is utilized to characterize the temporal correlation of multipath gains. We characterize the full-sequence mutual information (MI) over temporally correlated channels. For fixed antenna positions and beamforming, we establish a finite-horizon approximation error bound that vanishes as both effective signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) increase. We derive a closed-form expression for the one-step conditional MI and adopt it as a tractable key-information metric. A nonconvex problem is formulated to jointly optimize antenna positions and per-slot beamforming under transmit-power and minimum-spacing constraints. We develop an alternating optimization algorithm, combining an exact principal-eigenvector beamforming solution with feasible SCA-based projected gradient position updates. Simulation results demonstrate that the MA-assisted scheme outperforms the fixed-position antenna baseline. At a high temporal correlation coefficient, position optimization achieves approximately $51\%$ higher rates than fixed antennas. Joint position and beamforming optimization provides a further $106\%$ gain over position optimization alone, demonstrating more pronounced gains under strong temporal correlation.

Signal Processing.title: Design and Analysis of Pinching-Antenna Systems With Radially Deployed Waveguides (X-PASS)
Signal Processing.summary: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) reconfigure the wireless channel by positioning dielectric antennas along a waveguide. A single waveguide, however, confines its antennas to one line, so that good coverage of an area has relied on several waveguides or waveguide segments with separate feeds. This paper proposes X-PASS, in which a hub feeds radially deployed waveguide arms, one pinching antenna on each, and drives them by arm selection, aggregation or multiplexing. It models the hub with its insertion losses, derives a unified signal-to-noise ratio expression for these three operating modes, and derives in closed form a radius inside which aggregation outperforms selection. Numerical results validate the analysis and compare the coverage of X-PASS with that of the other layouts at equal transmit power.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

Signal Processing.title: A Distributed Microphone Network for Real-Time Gunshot Detection and Localization in GNSS-Challenged Large Areas
Signal Processing.summary:
This paper presents a scalable distributed acoustic surveillance system for real-time gunshot detection and localiza tion in large-area, GNSS-challenged environments. The system consists of multiple low-cost MEMS microphone array units (MAUs) deployed as distributed anchors. Each MAU performs edge-level sound-event detection using a lightweight Sound De tection and Echo Suppression (SDES) algorithm, followed by a TinyML-based classifier for gunshot identification. For detected gunshots, an enhanced Generalized Cross-Correlation (eGCC) al gorithm estimates intra-array time differences of arrival (TDoAs)
  with improved robustness under low signal-to-noise ratio and re verberant conditions. Angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimates obtained from individual MAUs are fused through a modified SCO-EV localization framework to determine the gunshot position in a global coordinate system. A misplacement calibration (MC)
  algorithm compensates for platform orientation errors, improv ing angular consistency and localization accuracy in practical field conditions. Extensive experiments conducted over coverage areas ranging from 4,985 m2 to 49,063 m2 demonstrate reliable operation across varying spatial scales. The proposed framework achieves a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.70 for gunshot recognition and average localization errors below 6.5 m over 25,000 m2 , while maintaining errors under 15 m at larger scales. The results demonstrate the practical potential of the proposed system for distributed gunshot surveillance in GNSS challenged large areas.
Signal Processing.comment: 15 pages, 12 figures

Signal Processing.title: Energy-Efficient Tri-Hybrid Beamforming with Movable Pattern-Reconfigurable Antennas
Signal Processing.summary: Conventional hybrid precoding is confined to the digital/analog domains, leaving the spatial and radiation-pattern degrees-of-freedoms (DoFs) largely untapped. To unlock these, we propose a movable pattern-reconfigurable antenna (MPRA) and an energy-efficient tri-hybrid framework that jointly optimizes the precoders, antenna positions, and radiation-pattern states. We develop a hardware-inspired power model capturing the energy and transmission-time costs of antenna reconfiguration. The resulting mixed discrete-continuous fractional problem is solved via an alternating-optimization framework combining fractional programming, Riemannian optimization, and switching-aware pattern optimization. Simulations demonstrate near-exhaustive-search performance and consistent energy-efficiency (EE) gains, validating the complementary benefits of antenna movement, pattern reconfiguration, and tri-hybrid precoding under hardware-inspired power and latency costs.

Signal Processing.title: First-Principles Channel Model and Capacity-Achieving Transmission Scheme in Thermal Noise Backscatter Links
Signal Processing.summary: Thermal noise communication systems transmit information by modulating thermal radiation, eliminating the need for a dedicated signal power source and making them attractive solutions for low-power sensor networks. Their efficiency enables long-lived, unobtrusive operation, which is valuable in the Internet of Things, electromagnetic interference-sensitive environments, and RFID tag systems. However, a limited understanding of the wireless channel model and efficient transmission schemes has hindered their practical deployment. Here, we present a wireless channel model that elucidates how systems operating at ambient temperature can modulate thermal noise to convey information. Our results reveal a thermal noise backscatter mechanism that enables significantly higher data rates than previously achieved. We designed and built a thermal noise communication system leveraging this mechanism to achieve data rates in the kilobits-per-second range - over two orders of magnitude higher than prior demonstrations. We also derive the system capacity and show that using polar codes, we are able to achieve this expected capacity. Our channel model and transmission scheme pave the way for new strategies in thermal noise sensing and communication, advancing practical low-power networking for next-generation wireless applications.

Signal Processing.title: Vehicle Speed-Aware Jammer-Resilient Receiver for Multi-User MIMO V2X Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication plays a crucial role in enabling connected and autonomous driving by supporting the reliable exchange of safety-critical information among vehicles and infrastructure. However, due to the open nature of wireless channels, V2X systems are vulnerable to various physical-layer attacks, among which jamming is one of the most intuitive and severe threats. In this paper, we propose a vehicle speed-aware jammer-resilient reception framework for multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) V2X systems. The proposed method exploits the fundamental difference in Doppler characteristics between stationary jammers and moving vehicles. By transforming the received signal into the Doppler domain, the receiver identifies low-Doppler components associated with static interference and suppresses them through Doppler-domain filtering. Notably, the proposed approach does not require prior knowledge of the jammer channel or its spatial direction, making it suitable for practical V2X environments. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively mitigates strong jamming signals and significantly improves the achievable sum-rate compared with conventional receivers.
Signal Processing.comment: Presented at the 17th International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN 2026)

Signal Processing.title: Energy-Efficient Velocity Profile Optimization for Movable Antenna-Enabled Sensing Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Movable antennas (MAs) enable the reconfiguration of array geometry within a bounded region to exploit sub-wavelength spatial degrees of freedom in wireless communication and sensing systems. However, most prior research has predominantly focused on the communication and sensing performance, overlooking the mechanical power consumption inherent in antenna movement. To bridge this gap, this paper investigates a velocity profile optimization framework for MA-assisted direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation, explicitly balancing sensing accuracy with mechanical energy consumption of MAs. We first establish a Newtonian-based mechanical energy model, and formulate a functional optimization problem for sensing energy efficiency (EE) maximization. By applying the calculus of variations, this formulation is transformed into an infinite-dimensional problem defined by the Euler-Lagrange equation. To solve it, we propose a spectral discretization framework based on the Galerkin method, which expands the velocity profile over a sinusoidal basis. In the regime where energy consumption is dominated by linear damping, we prove that the optimal velocity profile follows a closed-form sinusoidal shape. For more general scenarios involving strong nonlinear aerodynamic drag, we leverage the Markov-Lukács theorem to transform the kinematic constraints into strictly convex sum-of-squares (SOS) conditions. Consequently, the infinite-dimensional problem is reformulated as a tractable finite-dimensional nonlinear algebraic system, which is solved by a two-layer algorithm combining Dinkelbach's method with successive convex approximation (SCA). Numerical results demonstrate that our optimized velocity profile significantly outperforms baselines in terms of EE across various system configurations. Insights into the optimized velocity profiles and practical design guidelines are also provided.

Signal Processing.title: Cramer-Rao Bounds for Target Parameter Estimation in a Bi-Static IRS-Assisted Radar Configuration
Signal Processing.summary: The use of Intelligent Reflective Surfaces (IRS) to assist communication and sensing has proven cost-effective in challenging scenarios. For sensing, IRS is shown to sense non-line-of-sight (NLOS) and stealth targets, albeit with significant loss due to the four-hop path model. Amongst the available IRS-assisted configurations, we consider a three-hop model in which the IRS redirects the scattered target response towards the mono-static radar. With the IRS spatially displaced from the radar, this configuration mimics a bi-static radar. While target detection has been studied in this configuration, parameter estimation has not been investigated to date. To this end, we first develop the signal model for this configuration and derive the Cramer Rao Bounds (CRB) for target parameters. The dependence of CRB on system parameters such as SNR, number of snapshots, number of IRS elements and their weights is brought forward through extensive simulations. This study can enable a designer to customize the system parameters to meet the requirements. It also serves as a benchmark for parameter estimation techniques developed for this configuration.

Signal Processing.title: Learned Diffusion Channel Priors for Coded MIMO Turbo Receivers
Signal Processing.summary: Iterative receivers for coded multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) links estimate the channel from pilots, decoded data, and a prior. In short packets with few pilots and at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), the prior matters. An expectation propagation (EP) turbo receiver needs the channel's mean and covariance given an anisotropic Gaussian message from the pilots and decoder. A diffusion prior's denoiser, however, returns only a mean, and only for a channel in isotropic noise. We replace only the receiver's channel-prior module with a learned diffusion prior. At an isotropic query formed from the message, one network gives both moments: its output is the mean, its Jacobian the covariance. They form a matrix-valued EP site, the Gaussian factor representing the prior. We show why an indefinite Jacobian can make the receiver diverge, and we floor its eigenvalues. In coded block error rate (BLER), the diffusion prior fails less than a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) prior learned from the same channels. It does so on a controlled sparse specular model and a 3GPP model, at every tested receive-array and training-set size. On the former, scalar-site controls, with one variance instead of the covariance, keep this advantage, so the gain comes from the diffusion prior.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

Signal Processing.title: MirrorComm: A Communication-Efficient Cooperative Perception Framework via Mirrored World Models
Signal Processing.summary: Cooperative perception (CP) requires substantial communication bandwidth to exchange sensing information among connected agents. A variety of compression techniques have been proposed to reduce transmission costs while retaining task-relevant information. However, most existing methods follow a frame-wise compression paradigm, overlooking temporal predictability and repeatedly transmitting information that could be inferred from historical context. To address these limitations, we propose MirrorComm, the first world model-based communication-efficient CP framework. Specifically, mirrored world models at the transmitter and receiver predict the transmitter's current observation from a shared history of its reconstructed observations. The transmitter compares this prediction with its current observation and selectively transmits observation updates to correct prediction errors, reducing repeated transmission of predictable information. Experiments on the OPV2V dataset across two downstream tasks including object detection and semantic segmentation show that MirrorComm reduces communication bandwidth requirements by up to approximately 66-fold while maintaining comparable performance to a state-of-the-art (SOTA) method. Ablation studies further demonstrate the effectiveness of the individual components.

Signal Processing.title: Which Chains to Calibrate for Physical Backpropagation: Per-User Factors Versus Base-Station Chains
Signal Processing.summary: In physical backpropagation, users return loss derivatives over the time-division duplex uplink, giving the base station the downlink gradient without channel reconstruction. Reciprocity calibration conventionally prioritizes base-station chains, as column-normalized zero-forcing reduces a per-user factor to a stream rotation. This priority can reverse. With ideal base-station chains and no noise, per-user amplitude errors make the returned field a weighted sum-rate gradient. With zero-forcing full service at both optima, the loss is independent of array size. Otherwise the selection penalty, serving the wrong users, carries 86 to 94 percent of the amplitude-induced loss in five of six configurations. Per-user phase errors mainly slow the iteration. Base-station chain errors scale the returned field per antenna, and at 3 dB and 25 degrees they cost one user 1.3 dB of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) that no array size removes. With 80 users, such errors on both sides, and mismatched pilots, oracle per-user and base-station calibration leave 6.2 and 12.3 percent loss at 256 antennas on clustered channels. This ordering holds at 30 dB SNR and reverses for 1 dB, 10 degree user errors. A capped one-echo estimator comes within 2.4 percentage points of oracle per-user calibration but underperforms no calibration at 10 dB SNR.
Signal Processing.comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables

Signal Processing.title: Nearest Is Not Safest: Fluid-Antenna Port Selection for Over-the-Air Backpropagation in Urban Multipath
Signal Processing.summary: Over-the-air backpropagation returns a loss gradient through the reciprocal channel, which requires the return port to see the channel of the forward port. If the terminal moves in between, a fluid antenna system can return through the port nearest to the forward position. In ray-traced Chicago streets, with a pedestrian displacement of about half a wavelength and a street-level base station, this rule reverses 20 percent of the gradients at a port spacing of 0.7 wavelengths and 49 percent at 0.9 wavelengths, while one of the four nearest ports stays aligned in all but 2 and 9 percent. We derive a certificate for the sign of the mean correlation from the second moment of a planar angular spectrum. It reduces to a linear program with three variables and infinitely many constraints, is tight, and holds over a region of second moments. In a static Gaussian model, observations collected along a line cannot tell an angular spectrum from its mirror image, so the sign of the cross moment must come from other information. At unsurveyed positions of the same city, a knowledge map that transports surveyed paths through virtual sources and fits them to the causal channel history lowers the reversal rate at 0.9 wavelengths from 49 to 27 percent. Its gain over the nearest port survived every tested error, while its gain over a geometry rule stayed significant at the tested single-error levels of 5 degrees of phase drift per step and 2 mm of position error but not at the next tested levels. Without any survey, across five cities and ten base stations, the nearest port reverses 37 percent of the returns at 0.9 wavelengths and a rule based on the direction and elevation of the base station 20.5 percent. The multilayer perceptrons we tested did not beat these physical rules by the margin fixed in advance in the primary settings.
Signal Processing.comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, 13 tables. Extended version with appendices

Signal Processing.title: A Beam-Switched Sparse Circular Array for Passive Wi-Fi Sensing
Signal Processing.summary: Wi-Fi sensing applications require unambiguous angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation over the full azimuth plane. Uniform circular arrays (UCAs) are shown to remove this ambiguity, but deploying the four RF chains typically available on commercial Wi-Fi chipsets into a sparse layout suffers from spatial undersampling. Such undersampling produces strong grating lobes. To overcome this hardware bottleneck, we first establish a generalized array manifold incorporating element radiation patterns, revealing the suitability and degradation mechanisms of directional UCAs. Then we propose an angularly staggered beam-switched UCA architecture that leverages the spatial complementarity. Numerical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed scheme effectively mitigates grating-lobe ambiguities without increasing the number of RF chains, significantly reducing AoA estimation outliers and improving omnidirectional tracking performance.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 8 figures. Submitted to EuCAP 2027

Signal Processing.title: Clock-Shift-Aided Blind Doppler Matching in Passive SDR Monitoring Data for LEO Doppler Positioning
Signal Processing.summary: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite signals have recently attracted increasing attention as opportunistic signals for positioning, navigation, and timing. Most Doppler-based LEO positioning studies rely on tracked satellite signals or raw in-phase/quadrature (IQ) samples that preserve signal-level structures for acquisition, Doppler tracking, or satellite association. In contrast, passive software-defined radio (SDR) monitoring systems often retain only time-frequency power scans, in which LEO Doppler traces appear as unlabeled ridges without raw IQ samples or identifiable signal structures. This paper proposes a clock-shift-aided segment-based blind Doppler matching method that associates unlabeled Doppler traces with candidate satellites predicted using two-line element (TLE) data. The proposed framework consists of slope-consistent Doppler segment generation, clock-shift-aided temporal alignment, and multi-metric satellite matching based on Doppler-rate and trajectory-shape consistency. The proposed method was evaluated using a three-hour subset of open Starlink/OneWeb monitoring data collected in the United Kingdom. The clock-offset search selected an effective offset of +19 s, for which 56 of 69 segments had at least one slope-compatible candidate, compared with 19 segments at zero shift. Using the resulting satellite associations, the batch positioning error over the full three-hour period was 104.2 m, whereas the RMSE-based and slope-based simple-segment baselines failed to converge near the reference receiver location.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE NAVICON 2026

Signal Processing.title: Antenna Positioning and Beamforming Optimization in MA Enabled Secure ISAC Systems: A Gradient-Based Meta Learning Approach
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) significantly improves spectral efficiency but introduces security risks regarding the interception of embedded communication signals. This paper proposes an movable antenna (MA)-enabled secure ISAC system that utilizes the spatial degrees of freedom of MA to mitigate these risks. Then, a problem is formulated to maximize the system secrecy rate by jointly optimizing antenna positioning, transmit beamforming, and artificial noise. However, the principal challenge arises from the non-convexity of the optimization problem and the strong coupling of the optimization variables. Generally, traditional optimization methods for this problem suffer from complex mathematical derivations, while existing deep learning approaches rely heavily on the training data distribution. To address these issues, we introduce a gradient-based meta learning (GML) algorithm, which works without pre-training and demonstrates favorable performance. Specifically, the algorithm establishes a neural network for each optimization variable, where the gradient of the objective function with respect to the variable serves as the input, and the output of the network determines the variable's update step. By handling the constraints and constructing penalty terms, the global loss function is used to guide the optimization process. Extensive numerical simulations confirm that the proposed algorithm achieves satisfactory performance in terms of both communication security and sensing capabilities.

Signal Processing.title: Joint Delay--Doppler Modeling of Multipath LEO Channels
Signal Processing.summary: Multipath channel models for Low-Earth-orbit (LEO) non-terrestrial network (NTN) must contend with time variability due to rapid satellite orbital motion that in turn impacts local (near terrestrial) scattering near the ground terminal (GT) receiver. While 3GPP-defined NTN channel model pipelines TR 38.811, 38.901 incorporate elevation-dependence into statistical channel generators, these are inherited largely from 2-D terrestrial propagation and are largely insufficient. Further, they do not prescribe any integrated workflow that is broadly available for generating joint delay, Doppler/phase and component multipath power profiles as a function of satellite location over a pass. This work addresses this gap by developing a geometry-based stochastic channel model driven by prescribed slant range, elevation, and azimuth over a LEO pass. A ground scene generates wall-reflected, ground-reflected, and roof-edge-diffracted components, from which joint delay-Doppler statistics and temporal channel impulse response (CIR) evolution are obtained. The resulting locally wide-sense stationary tapped-delay-line CIR enables analysis of key statistics such as the $K$-factor of the taps, multipath delay and Doppler spreads as a function of elevation and scene parameters. Depending on the scenarios (urban and rural), our model-based results show that with omnidirectional antennas, the LoS probability, delay-spread and $K$-factor trends broadly match 3GPP NTN models in TR 38.811 as a function of elevation. Beamforming instead produces a mid-elevation $K$-factor peak, which is not predicted by TR 38.811 and 6G NTN. Doppler spreads are smaller than those from our previous model and QuaDriGa because the proposed model accounts for path existence. Stationarity durations for CIR are reported and generally decrease with elevation, but with local increases at mid-elevation due to path geometry effects.

Signal Processing.title: Joint PAPR Reduction and Over-the-Air Computing in Multi-User OFDMA Systems
Signal Processing.summary: We consider the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction challenge of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems utilizing tone reservation (TR) under an over-the-air computing constraint, such that the signals placed in the reserved tones simultaneously enable distributed computation at the receiver. To that end, the problem is cast as a fractional programming problem and solved via the iterative quadratic transform (QT), which guarantees convergence to a stationary point. A key contribution is the decomposition of the reserved-tone vector into an orthogonal pair of components: one satisfying the sum-computation constraint and the other providing the remaining degrees of freedom for PAPR reduction. This decomposition reveals that the proposed method and the benchmark sacrifices the same number of degrees of freedom. However, the proposed design distributes the computational payload across all reserved tones, yielding superior robustness against multi-user interference and quantization noise. Analytical and simulation results confirm that the proposed method matches the benchmark in PAPR reduction while outperforming it in computation accuracy, particularly in multi-user scenarios.
Signal Processing.comment: ISITA 2026

Sound.title: From Senses to Decisions: The Information Flow of Auditory and Visual Perception in Multimodal LLMs
Sound.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can listen and see, but how do audio and visual signals actually travel through the network to shape an answer? Despite their growing role in research and real-world applications, the internal pathways through which audio and visual tokens influence the final prediction remain poorly understood. In this study, we examine audio-visual information flow inside Audio-Visual Large Language Models (AVLLMs), tracing how AVLLMs route, utilize, and integrate audio and visual information across two input configurations, audio-visual video and multiple interleaved audio-visual items. We find that for audio-visual video, AVLLMs follow the sequential information flow pathway established for VLMs and VideoLLMs, with audio and visual contribution flowing along this pathway in proportion to the task's reliance on each modality. In settings with multiple interleaved audio-visual items, this routing shifts to different parallel streams. Furthermore, we demonstrate that audio-visual and other token types can be discarded once their information is transferred to LLM, with minimal impact on the model's prediction or even slight improvement, generalizing across multiple tasks and datasets, enabling more efficient inference. These findings hold across multiple models and scales, Qwen2.5-Omni and Video-SALMONN2 Plus at 3B and 7B scales, leading to hypotheses on why these flow structures emerge. Together, these results deliver the first coherent picture of how AVLLMs orchestrate sound and sight inside the network and lay the groundwork for the next wave of interpretability, design, and efficiency advances in audio-visual and broader MLLMs.

Sound.title: Clean-anchored excess-emission control for CTC adaptation under competing speech
Sound.summary: Competing speech can cause excess emissions in a connectionist temporal classification (CTC) recognizer. We penalize the amount by which the noisy student's expected collapsed token count exceeds a frozen teacher's count on the paired clean utterance. The one-sided objective caches one scalar per utterance and adds no inference module. With 147,456 trainable parameters in wav2vec 2.0, it improves competing-speech word error rate (WER) over matched CTC-only adaptation across three development seeds. On a locked LibriSpeech test, speech-interference WER falls from 45.198% to 44.323%, while clean WER changes by 0.004 percentage points. Unseen VCTK interferers yield a 0.307-point improvement. Ablations favor collapsed-count control over frame-mass regularization. Longer training increases the speech gain but worsens noise and music performance, identifying an insertion-deletion tradeoff rather than uniform robustness.

Sound.title: PianoBench: Evaluating Musical Perception and Reasoning in Language Models
Sound.summary: Multimodal language models continue to improve on broad music understanding benchmarks, but which musical features can they perceive and reason about? We investigate this question by introducing PianoBench, a benchmark that tasks language models with reasoning about musical performances across congruent acoustic and symbolic input representations. PianoBench is derived from our new multimodal, training-scale dataset comprising more than 20,000 hours of interleaved transcripts of music and spoken musical commentary from instructional piano videos. Open-weight audio-language models achieve at most 52.8% accuracy on PianoBench, and at best only modestly outperform their accuracy on a no-audio control. In contrast, frontier models using chain of thought achieve up to 93.2% accuracy when provided transcripts of music as text, exposing a gap between perceiving musical features from audio and reasoning about musical events when they are given explicitly. We then test whether mid-training on interleaved musical instruction can improve question answering without chain of thought, raising Qwen 3.5 9B Base's zero-shot accuracy on PianoBench with music transcripts from 42.8% to 56.0% after instruction tuning. These experiments suggest that instructional videos may represent an overlooked source of multimodal supervision for music. Available: https://gclef-cmu.org/pianobench.

Sound.title: Memory Efficient Audio Synthesis with Decoupled Temporal Depth Diffusion Transformers
Sound.summary: Siri Expressive Voices synthesize rich, configurable speech in real time and entirely on device, powered by AFM 3 Core Advanced, Apple's most powerful on-device foundation model. This work presents the memory-efficient audio synthesis architecture behind that capability: a detokenizer that converts the semantic audio tokens emitted by the foundation model into high-fidelity audio within the tight compute and memory budget of the Scalable Matrix Extension (SME). We convert semantic audio tokens to a residual vector quantization (RVQ) representation with a three-component design, a streaming encoder, a temporal decoder, and a depth decoder, that systematically decouples temporal and depth processing. A single reusable depth decoder with Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-style stage conditioning generates all RVQ levels autoregressively, replacing the dedicated per-level decoders of prior multi-decoder architectures, while causal sliding window attention with fixed-window key-value caching yields constant memory complexity independent of sequence length. Deployed on the AMX, the detokenizer sustains roughly 10 ms per generation step, about 16x faster than real time, with a peak runtime memory of only 21 MB and 329 MB of on-device assets, enabling continuous streaming synthesis of 20-320 seconds of audio. This constant, small footprint replaces the linear and quadratic memory scaling of conventional transformer- and GAN-based approaches.
