Robotics.summary: Pre-touch sensing, or sensing information about an object before contact, is an attractive modality for robot hands as it can allow a robot to anticipate and respond to a contact before it happens. In this work, we introduce ToFTouch, a multimodal tactile sensor combining three multizone (4$\times$4 resolution) time-of-flight sensors with an optics-based pressure sensing array. We mount this sensor on a parallel jaw gripper and demonstrate its utility on three distinct tasks: (i) pre-grasp adjustment, (ii) item extraction from clutter, and (iii) item insertion into tight spaces. For pre-grasp adjustment, ToF feedback reduced cycle time by 7.4$\%$ by enabling anticipatory gripper closure during approach. For extraction, ToF sensing enabled successful retrieval across all tested depth offsets ($\pm$2 cm) deviating from the nominal pick point, including conditions where baseline approaches failed, with standard deviations below 0.4 cm. For insertion into dense clutter, we explore the proximity and tactile information provided from ToFTouch during an insertion trajectory. The results demonstrate the utility of multizone ToF sensing in a manipulation environment.

Robotics.title: Reusable Neural Reachability via Local Refinement
Robotics.summary: This paper studies obstacle avoidance under translation invariant dynamics using an avoid-side travel cost Hamilton Jacobi formulation. For running costs that are zero outside an obstacle and strictly negative inside it, we prove that the value function is non-positive everywhere, equals zero exactly outside the avoid set, and is strictly negative exactly on it. Under translation invariance, this yields a reuse principle: the value of any translated obstacle is obtained by translating a single template value function. We show that the pointwise minimum of translated template values exactly characterizes the union of the translated single-obstacle avoid sets and provides a conservative inner certificate of unavoidable collision in clutter. To reduce conservatism, we introduce a blockwise composition framework in which subsets of obstacles are merged and solved jointly. This yields a hierarchy of conservative certificates from singleton reuse to the exact clutter value, together with monotonicity under block merging and an exactness criterion based on the existence of a common clutter avoiding control. The framework is illustrated on a Dubins car example in a repeated clutter field.

Robotics.title: Evaluating Depth-Augmented Visual Features for Cross-Dataset Lunar Traversability Estimation
Robotics.summary: Autonomous mobility is essential for sustained lunar surface operations, as communication delays and line-of-sight occlusions limit continuous teleoperation. Although recent traversability estimation methods increasingly rely on deep learning, the domain gap between terrestrial analogue environments and real lunar terrain can limit their generalisation, and real lunar traversability labels are scarce, making fully supervised training difficult. To address these challenges, we build a weakly supervised framework trained on sparse pairwise annotations and study whether augmenting visual features with depth-derived geometric information: depth, surface normals, and combined geometric descriptors. We evaluate the models in both in-domain and cross-domain settings using two terrestrial analogue datasets and the real lunar Chang'E PCAM dataset. Contrary to expectations, we find that naive geometric augmentation yields no consistent improvement over a strong visual-only baseline in either setting, with effects small relative to seed-to-seed variance. Instead, the choice of training source emerges as the dominant factor in transfer quality: models trained on domain-relevant sources transfer substantially better to real lunar imagery than the geometric fusion strategy improves any single model. Our evaluation runs onboard a resource-constrained edge device and provides a controlled baseline for designing more expressive multimodal fusion architectures in future lunar perception systems.

Robotics.title: Toward Uncertainty-Aware, Physics-Grounded Human World Models
Robotics.summary: A robot that acts around people needs a world model of the human: a belief over the person's body state and a dynamics model that predicts where that state goes next. This abstract argues that two published components form exactly these two halves, and specifies how to couple them. KNOWN [1] reconstructs the 3D human body while estimating both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty in real time (11.6 ms per frame); its aleatoric term identifies unreliable observations, its epistemic term identifies inputs from low-density regions of the training data, and refinement driven by the epistemic term reduces the error on such inputs from 81.3 to 70.3 mm. PhysMoP [2] predicts future body configuration by solving the Euler-Lagrange equations of the body with learned dynamics terms, reducing the 80 ms prediction error from 9.6 to 2.1 mm on Human3.6M and from 12.1 to 0.7 mm on 3DPW. We define the interface between the two, propose three mechanisms by which KNOWN's uncertainty enters PhysMoP, and specify an evaluation protocol on in-the-wild video. No new experimental results are reported here.

Robotics.title: When Human Corrections Travel: Safety in Federated VLA Adaptation
Robotics.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can adapt to local human intervention, while federated learning can combine distributed robot experience without pooling raw records. We examine their prospective intersection: sharing adaptations derived from diverse human corrections across tasks, environments, people, and robot embodiments. Corrections differ in modality, safety semantics(urgency, behavioral scope, etc.), and privacy sensitivity. A shared update that improves mean task success may suppress a rare safety intervention or produce an unsafe response on another robot. We argue for three requirements: preserve the context and uncertainty of multimodal corrections when deciding what to share; assess candidate updates in each receiving robot's closed loop before deployment; and evaluate leakage alongside retention of safety-critical evidence. Immediate, legible defensive behavior remains necessary during human interaction. We offer counterexamples and a falsifiable evaluation agenda, not experimental results.
Robotics.comment: Accepted for presentation at SPAIS workshop in CoRL 2026

Robotics.title: DiffContact: Differentiable Contact Dynamics for Policy Learning and Contact-Implicit Trajectory Optimization
Robotics.summary: This paper proposes DiffContact, a smooth analytic gradient for frictional contact, and applies it to policy learning and contact-implicit trajectory optimization for legged locomotion. The exact contact sensitivity is available in closed form but describes changes within the current contact mode, providing no first-order information toward neighboring contact modes. The proposed gradient replaces this sensitivity only in the backward pass, leaving the hard-contact forward solve unchanged and the realized rollout feasible. A central-path relaxation of the de Saxcé-corrected second-order-cone complementarity problem for Coulomb friction smooths the conditions defining the separating, clamping, and sliding modes. The relaxed sensitivity is evaluated at a point on the central path obtained by a Newton iteration initialized from the hard-contact solution. The sensitivity remains continuous through contact-mode transitions and converges to the exact sensitivity as the relaxation vanishes. Using 100,000 samples and less than 2 min of training on a desktop PC, policy learning with the proposed gradient produces a policy that transfers to hardware without fine-tuning. On hardware, the robot under a trotting policy withstands pushes and traverses debris and slippery ground. In trajectory optimization, the proposed gradient reaches contact-rich solutions missed by exact and Signorini-relaxed gradients. Project page: https://diffcontact.github.io
Robotics.comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Robotics (T-RO)

Robotics.title: Myoelectric Control for Upper-Limb Exoskeletons: A Decoder-Shaper-Controller Framework, Design Guidelines, and Future Directions
Robotics.summary: Myoelectric Control Systems (MCSs) enable voluntary control of wearable robots through muscle activity. However, intention decoding, assistance shaping, and low-level actuator control are often not explicitly distinguished, making their contributions difficult to evaluate and compare. This review introduces a functional decoder-shaper-controller framework for continuous myoelectric control of upper-limb exoskeletons. The decoder estimates an intention-related variable from surface electromyography (sEMG), the shaper maps it to a control reference according to an assistance policy, and the controller realizes that reference through actuator control. This decomposition separates intention estimation from assistance-policy design and enables comparison of heterogeneous architectures. Representative approaches are critically examined in terms of module design, calibration, and evaluation. The analysis highlights that the shaper, despite determining the magnitude and shape of assistance, lacks established design and tuning methodologies and is often embedded within the decoder or controller. Key open issues include inconsistent reporting of assistance levels, limited use of interaction-aware stability and passivity tools, and insufficient validation across degrees of freedom, users, and tasks. Building on these findings, this review provides design guidelines for systematic module-wise tuning and identifies future research priorities to bridge the gap between accurate intention decoding and safe, effective, and generalizable assistance under real-world operating conditions.

Robotics.title: OpenZilo: An Open Smart-Ring Platform for Human-Centric Sensing and Interaction with Robots
Robotics.summary: Wearable robot interfaces must connect user input to timely physical action. We present the proposed platform, an open smart-ring platform for studying this connection across task stages. The ring integrates a microphone, an inertial measurement unit, photoplethysmography, and skin-temperature sensing. Its software architecture separates acquisition, event interpretation, interaction policy, and robot execution. We characterize seven operating modes and evaluate speech and gesture control with 10 participants. Across five commands and 250 trials per modality, speech and gestures achieved task success rates of 90.4% and 88.8%, respectively. Recognition accuracy exceeded task success for both modalities. Gaussian hidden Markov models achieved higher accuracy than a support vector machine across three vocabulary sizes, with longer scoring times. Following a shared spoken task start, gesture-based adjustments had shorter median response times than speech. Whole-task success was 70.0% with gestures and 64.0% with speech. We further examine physiological-event-triggered robot interaction using simulated event notifications. Mean notification-receipt-to-arrival times were 11.71 s for the robot and 9.20 s for an on-site person. These descriptive findings support evaluating wearable robot interfaces through both recognition and physical outcomes, with timing measures appropriate to each task stage.

Robotics.title: ROOF: Learning Humanoid Fall Recovery under Overhead Constraints
Robotics.summary: A fallen humanoid beneath an overhead obstacle faces a coupled recovery problem. It must create clearance while organizing support for a stable rise, since attempting to stand before making room can further increase obstruction. We introduce a reinforcement learning method with contact-supported geometric escape guidance, which rewards incremental reduction of robot-obstacle overlap without prescribing an escape path. To achieve this, a learned motion prior, together with posture-dependent support and joint-stall costs, is proposed to shape a single policy that learns when to clear the obstacle, how to establish support, and when to complete the rise, all using proprioception alone. In simulation, it recovers in 88.5% of trials beneath plates that can only be lifted, compared with 18.9% without geometric guidance, and in 98.6% of trials beneath free plates with randomized size, mass and placement. On a Unitree G1, the deployed policy recovered in 95 of 150 attempts across seven real-world obstacle scenes, including furniture and multi-object arrangements absent from training. Project page: https://lu-yidan.github.io/ROOF/

Robotics.title: A Phenomenology of Neural Geometry in Vision-Language-Action Models
Robotics.summary: Robotic manipulation is inherently geometric, but what shape does the world take inside the policy that performs it? Prior work on vision-language-action (VLA) policies establishes that task-relevant variables are linearly readable from activations, yet readability certifies only that a variable is present and says nothing about the shape its values trace, which may be curved and multi-dimensional. Using controlled sweeps, natural rollouts, linear probes, and activation interventions, we build a taxonomy of seven task-relevant concepts in VLA models. We find that realized geometry is predominantly multi-dimensional and is shaped by the constraints under which the policy acts. Physical joint limits, for example, leave wrist orientation an open arc rather than a circle, and distance to the target, a single scalar, is realized in two orthogonal subspaces, a coarse ruler for the approach and a fine ruler for the grasp. The same geometries reappear in two further VLA models on real-world robot data, indicating that they are neither model-specific nor artifacts of simulation. We demonstrate how the findings are actionable by steering along the geometry a concept realizes. Overall, this work lays out an initial phenomenology of realized geometry in VLA policies and demonstrates that a concept's shape carries as much importance as its readability.
Robotics.comment: 41 pages, 10 pages of main text, 8 main text figures

Robotics.title: Safe-Ballbot: Tilt-Consistent MPC with Control Barrier Functions for Ballbot Navigation
Robotics.summary: Ball-balancing robots (ballbots) must lean to accelerate, and the lean is limited by the wheel torques and by safety. Planners that use the full robot model are expensive, while planners that ignore the balance dynamics produce references that cannot be followed. This paper presents a two-layer navigation scheme for a three-omni-wheel ballbot. The upper layer is a model predictive controller on a \emph{jerk model} of the ball position, with discrete-time control barrier functions for static, moving, rotating and concave obstacles. The lower layer is a hierarchical sliding mode controller with an extended state observer and a robust exponential control barrier function on the tilt (HSMC-ESO-ECBF). The layers are linked by an acceleration bound derived in closed form from the largest steady tilt that the barrier function admits, so that the plan never asks for a lean the tracker refuses. For obstacles whose motion is only predicted, the obstacles are inflated by conformal prediction radii that bound the prediction error with a prescribed probability. In MuJoCo, with omni-wheel roller contacts and torque saturation, the scheme keeps at least $10$\,cm of clearance, tracks the plan within $2$\,cm RMS, keeps the tilt below the limit and plans in $9$--$12$\,ms, $10$--$15$ times faster than a full-model nonlinear MPC that enters the inflated obstacles; with predicted obstacles, the conformal inflation removes the collisions of a constant-velocity predictor in $30$ random crossing scenarios and reduces them in an endless run on a closed path.The source code and video illustrations are available at https://safe-ballbot.github.io

Systems and Control.title: Time to AC-t: When AC-transmission changes capacity expansion planning
Systems and Control.summary: Capacity expansion models often dramatically simplify the physics of how power flows through a transmission network in order to preserve computational tractability. However, with the rapid growth of electrification, large loads, renewables, and storage, increased realism in planning future grids is imperative. We extend the open-source capacity expansion model GenX with AC optimal power flow physics, and analyze generation, storage, and transmission investment decisions for 20-zone, hourly models of Germany and Texas. We compare our results against those using two common approximations, the transport model and DC optimal power flow. We find that total costs and emissions largely agree across all formulations. However, we find substantial differences in outputs related to transmission, generation siting, storage, and reactive-power support between the approximate formulations and the true AC physics formulation. We identify where AC physics changes planning decisions and discuss how to potentially capture these effects without the full computational cost.
Systems and Control.comment: 35 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables; plus 16 pages of supplemental information (8 figures, 6 tables). Submitted to Joule

Systems and Control.title: Methods for Accelerating and Stabilizing Nonlinear Magnetic Equivalent-Circuit Analysis
Systems and Control.summary: Design and optimization of electromagnetic devices require models that converge reliably and quickly and can represent intense localized magnetic saturation. This paper presents a parameterized 2D nonlinear magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) and proposes solution methods for it: an approximate Jacobian that is symmetric positive definite, so each Newton-Raphson iteration can use sparse Cholesky factorization with fill-reducing reordering, and Anderson mixing as step control. These methods are compared with alternative nonlinear iterations, linear solvers, and step-control methods in convergence, computational cost, and prediction accuracy. Radial-flux magnetic gears (RFMGs) with structural bridges serve as a challenging test case, because their thin bridges exhibit intense local saturation. The methods are evaluated on three bridged base designs and on 1,024 bridged designs, each paired with the same design without the bridge. On the base designs, Newton-Raphson iteration with the approximate Jacobian reached much lower residuals than fixed-point iteration, which converged for none of them. Sparse Cholesky factorization with reordering was the fastest linear solver tested. Across the 1,024 design pairs, full-step Newton-Raphson converged for 193 bridged and 564 bridge-free designs, whereas Anderson mixing converged for 1,003 and 1,022 and required fewer iterations. Bridged designs converged less often and more slowly under every method. The nonlinear MEC was 2.17 and 1.84 times faster than fixed-mesh nonlinear finite element analysis (FEA) in total computation time for the bridged and bridge-free populations. The median outer-rotor torque discrepancy relative to FEA was 0.22%, and the Spearman rank correlations of the design rankings were at least 0.9996.
Systems and Control.comment: 14 pages, 11 figures. v5: substantially revised and reframed around solution methods for the nonlinear MEC (SPD approximate Jacobian with sparse Cholesky; Anderson mixing), with new comparisons on 1,024 bridged/bridge-free magnetic gear design pairs. Timing and accuracy results supersede earlier versions

Systems and Control.title: A Review of Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control Algorithms: State of the Art and Research Opportunities
Systems and Control.summary: Max-Pressure (MP) has emerged as a widely studied decentralized traffic signal control framework, thanks to its desirable theoretical properties and strong control performance. Early research on MP focused on improving control performance by exploring different variables of the traffic state for the definition of pressure. Subsequent studies expanded MP to incorporate the complexity of real-world transportation systems and emerging technologies. This paper provides a comprehensive review of these developments. The review first introduces the theoretical foundations of MP and examines early developments in movement weight definition. It then synthesizes major extensions for multimodal and multiscale network control, followed by recent developments in connected and automated vehicle (CAV) environments and the integration of MP with artificial intelligence (AI) and data-driven methods. Beyond summarizing existing approaches, this review examines their underlying assumptions, data requirements, implementation considerations, and practical limitations. Based on this comprehensive review, key research gaps and future directions are identified, including remaining limitations in the theoretical foundations of MP and the underexplored integration of autonomous vehicle control with the MP framework. Overall, this review provides a structured perspective on the evolution and current state of MP control and highlights opportunities for developing more proactive, robust, and practically deployable MP-based traffic control methods.

Systems and Control.title: Holonic Graceful Transitions Across Centralized, Decentralized, Distributed, and Local Control in DER-rich Cyber-Power Distribution System
Systems and Control.summary: The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) in distribution system necessitates adaptive coordination frameworks. These frameworks must remain optimal during normal operation and resilient under cyber physical disturbances. Existing coordinated control approaches are typically deployed as static architectures with limited ability to adapt when communication degrades, local instability emerges, and operating conditions become spatially heterogeneous. This work addresses the gap by proposing a DER service-independent edge autonomous holonic adaptive coordination framework. In this framework, each DER controller executes its own control actions and transitions among centralized, distributed, decentralized, and local autonomous coordination modes without always relying on static coordination commands from the grid operator. The framework preserves coordination continuity across modes by retaining local controller states while reconfiguring only the coordination topology, information exchange pattern, and fallback action associated with the active DER service. Graceful transitions are enabled through dwell timers, rate limiting, and safety overrides to prevent dynamic instability during mode changes. Volt VAR control is used as a representative distribution automation application to validate the proposed architecture in a cyber-physical Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testbed. The proposed approach is evaluated under diverse cyber-physical event-based scenarios, showing region-confined adaptation under localized disturbance, reduced coordination traffic during coordination switching, and node-confined mitigation under cyber attack through edge anomaly detection and neighbor-corroborated impact estimation.
Systems and Control.comment: The paper is rejected based on multiple reviewers due to major concerns. So the full paper need to be revised before new submission and will change more that 50% of the contents

Systems and Control.title: MusiSPARQ: Subscription-Aware Adaptive Resource Control for Musical Metaverse Services
Systems and Control.summary: The Musical Metaverse relies on distributed audio, visual, inference, and delivery functions deployed across heterogeneous edge-cloud resources. Queue-aware orchestration frameworks such as SPARQ jointly optimize service placement, routing, and resource allocation, but fix the execution regime of each resource in advance: it is either shared, favoring statistical multiplexing, or guaranteed, favoring performance isolation. This paper introduces MusiSPARQ, a subscription-aware control framework that promotes resource isolation from a fixed infrastructure attribute to a runtime decision. Each switchable resource is represented through coupled shared- and guaranteed-resource pools drawing from the same physical-capacity budget, and at each orchestration epoch the controller selects which class-specific service flows remain shared and which receive isolated capacity. The per-epoch decision jointly accounts for class-specific latency objectives, per-class maximum-latency limits, queueing stability, isolation cost, and switching overhead. In a dynamic virtual-concert scenario, MusiSPARQ reduces the Premium latency-target violation rate from 16.19% to 0.29% relative to fully shared execution, while reserving on average only 0.71% of capacity and, unlike static isolation, keeping Standard and Basic traffic within their latency targets.
Systems and Control.comment: 10 pages, 9 figures. Accepted and Presented at IEEE International Symposium on the Internet of Sounds (IS2) 2026

Systems and Control.title: When Music Needs Meaning: Semantic Communication as a Transformative Enabler for the Musical Metaverse
Systems and Control.summary: The Musical Metaverse (MM) enables geographically distributed musicians, audiences, sound engineers, and AI agents to interact through synchronized audio, visual, kinematic, and haptic streams, imposing latency, synchronization, bandwidth, and scalability requirements that are difficult to satisfy with conventional bit-level communication. This paper argues that semantic communication, understood here as the transmission of musically meaningful information rather than raw audio-visual-haptic samples, provides a principled communication paradigm for the MM. We define the MM from a communication perspective and derive modality-specific require ments; propose a three-pillar framework for musical semantic communication comprising semantics extraction, semantic-aware orchestration, and cross-modal semantic synchronization; survey representative work across semantic communication, music AI and edge orchestration, identifying the gaps that prevent their integration; and propose a semantic-first reference architecture based on device-side semantic encoders, edge semantic routers, and cross-modal semantic synchronization. The resulting framework positions the MM as a concrete and demanding use case for 6G semantic communication.
Systems and Control.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures. Accepted and Presented at IEEE International Symposium on the Internet of Sounds (IS2) Conference 2026

Systems and Control.title: Contingency-Aware Planning via Certified Neural Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability
Systems and Control.summary: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability provides formal safety guarantees for dynamical systems, but repeatedly solving the HJ partial differential equation in changing environments limits its use in real-time planning. This paper introduces learning-based reachability and an online safety certification that together enable real-time contingency-aware planning in unknown environments with probabilistic safety guarantees. We use Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) to approximate the HJ solution operator under varying obstacle configurations. To certify the learned reach-avoid set, we recast robust scenario optimization as multiple hypothesis testings over its sublevel sets, which yields a simultaneous guarantee across candidate levels and recovers the largest certifiable volume at the prescribed safety level. Within this certified set, the induced recovery policy is guaranteed to return the system to a safe region in finite time under any admissible disturbance. Numerical results show that the learning and certification pipeline updates reach-avoid sets at real-time rates and is demonstrated on youBot simulation.

Systems and Control.title: Model-Based Koopman-Galerkin Lifting for Guaranteed H-Infinity Output Feedback Control of Nonlinear Systems
Systems and Control.summary: In this paper, we present a model-based Koopman-Galerkin framework for output-feedback control of nonlinear systems with known dynamics. With a suitable actuator augmentation, the finite-dimensional realization preserves the actuator dynamics and the constant input matrix. The approach is based on an exact decomposition of the lifted dynamics into an LTI system and a finite-order closure residual. It also applies to non-control-affine systems and allows dictionaries that do not span an invariant subspace. Regional bounds are derived for the closure residual, actuator-realization defect, and output-reconstruction error. We use these bounds to formulate a standard $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ output-feedback problem. The controller is linear and dynamic and is implemented using only the measured tracking error. Neither full-state measurements nor a separate state observer are required. Lifting is performed offline. With the state coordinates retained in the dictionary, we obtain explicit transient bounds on the original state and tracking error. A sufficient condition for regional containment is also given. Under this condition, the nonlinear closed loop is forward complete, and the state and tracking error are uniformly ultimately bounded. The cart-pendulum example illustrates the nonlinear closed-loop guarantees. The proposed output feedback gives lower RMSE and peak tracking error on average than Jacobian-based $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ feedback, full-state backstepping, and Koopman-based hybrid MPC.

Systems and Control.title: A Modular Open-Source Python Framework for Small Satellite Attitude Determination and Control
Systems and Control.summary:
Advanced attitude determination and control (ADCS) techniques can be difficult for small satellite teams to adopt: tightly coupled implementations require substantial code changes to evaluate different actuators, sensors, orbits, mission goals, and control laws. Existing tools often emphasize orbit mechanics or flight software rather than closed-loop ADCS. This paper presents an open-source, modular ADCS framework in pure Python for rapid development, repeatable testing, and flight-oriented integration across heterogeneous spacecraft.
  The package supports torque- and command-level control, bound-respecting allocation, and full- and reduced-attitude objectives. Interchangeable estimation, control, planning, and actuator/sensor modules are reconfigured through configuration changes. Integrated simulation includes attitude and orbit propagation, sensor and actuator bias and noise, and environmental disturbances. An actuator-aware planner supports underactuated architectures, while hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) capability enables testing on mission-representative computers.
  Case studies include a 3U CubeSat with three magnetorquers and one reaction wheel, a magnetorquer-only 1U, and a 6U with three reaction wheels and thrusters. These demonstrate actuator and sensor failures, full- and reduced-attitude goals, and momentum management. HIL testing on a Raspberry Pi uses the same package. Adapting a published control law to a new actuator configuration requires fewer than five lines of configuration changes. The framework underpins flight software for an Earth-observing CubeSat with visible and long-wave infrared imagers, three magnetorquers, and one reaction wheel, without star trackers or propulsion.

Systems and Control.title: A Quantitative Approach to Reach-Avoid Reachability Analysis for Discrete-Time Nonlinear Control Systems
Systems and Control.summary: A reach-avoid specification requires a dynamical system to reach a target set of states while avoiding a failure set. Reachability analysis partitions the state space into parts starting from which the specification can be satisfied by following some control signal and those from which it cannot despite the best control effort. In this paper, we present a quantitative approach for reachability analysis to analyze the satisfaction of avoid and reach-avoid specifications for discrete-time nonlinear control systems. In such an approach, a value function assigns a value to each state that determines how robustly the system can satisfy the specification starting from it and following the optimal control signal. However, computing such a value function is difficult. Instead, our approach constructs discrete abstractions on which it performs value iteration to compute sound bounds on the desired value function. The resulting lower bound enables a sound under-approximation of the reach avoid set (RAS) and, in the avoid case, a sound over-approximation of the backward reachable set (BRS). When the control set is finite, the upper bound additionally enables a sound over-approximation of the RAS and, in the avoid case, a sound under-approximation of the BRS. The lower bound also yields quantitative guarantees on safety margins and safe target-reaching times. Our approach further refines the abstraction by splitting the grid cells that could not be classified as within or outside the BRS (or RAS) to improve the usefulness of the bounds. We evaluate our approach on five example systems with up to five-dimensional state spaces.

Systems and Control.title: Timely Ground-Station Status Delivery via UAV-Assisted Data Collection and Hierarchical RL
Systems and Control.summary: We consider a UAV-assisted status-update system in which a rotary-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) collects updates from multiple sensors, stores the newest update of each sensor, and forwards selected buffered updates to a ground station (GS). We minimize a weighted sum of the time-average GS-side age of information (AoI) and UAV energy consumption over a finite horizon. The optimization is subject to half-duplex operation, sensor and UAV energy-causality constraints, transmission-rate and power limits, and a terminal-location constraint. Because collection changes the information age at the UAV but does not reduce the GS-side AoI until the buffered update is forwarded, mobility, collection, and forwarding decisions are coupled over time. We use a hierarchical AoI-energy actor-critic (HAE-AC) controller in which a coarse-timescale actor selects return-feasible UAV movements, while a deterministic per-slot scheduler constructs feasible collection or forwarding sets and assigns the minimum transmit power required for each scheduled transmission. In a 100-sensor deployment, HAE-AC reduces the average GS-side AoI by about 22% relative to an adaptive staleness-gated benchmark. Compared with forward-upon-collection, selective buffered forwarding reduces the number of downlink bursts by roughly 30% while increasing the number of collections per sensor by more than 23%.
Systems and Control.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures. Author's accepted manuscript. Accepted for publication in the proceedings of the 2026 Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers

Systems and Control.title: Trajectory and Morphology Planning for Morphing Quadrotors in Ultra-Narrow Passages using Limited Perception
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents an online trajectory and morphology planning framework for morphing quadrotors to traverse passages narrower than their unfolded width using only a 2D LiDAR for obstacle sensing. Fixed-frame vehicles cannot pass through such gaps, and classical artificial potential field (APF) based obstacle costs seal them off for planners as well, because the repulsive cost grows sharply inside a tight gap. The core enabler of our framework is a novel cost reduction factor, computed in closed form from the LiDAR data, that cancels the obstacle cost along the medial axis of a narrow passage. A true opening thus becomes a low-cost corridor, while the full repulsive cost is retained everywhere else. The cost reduction factor is embedded at every prediction node of an acados-based nonlinear MPC, which jointly plans the trajectory, yaw, and fold angle of the platform. A user-specified minimum-width limit ensures that the cost reduction factor only opens the corridors that the platform can actually pass. Gazebo/PX4 simulations and hardware experiments on the MorphoCopter demonstrate autonomous folding and unfolding through curved, inclined, and cluttered passages narrower than the unfolded width, where the standard repulsive cost fails to pass safely in most of the trials. The implementation code is available at \href{https://github.com/harshjmodi1996/morphocopter_mpc}{\textcolor{blue}{Github}} and a short video about the paper is available at \href{https://zh.engr.tamu.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/310/2026/10/Morphocopter_planning_final.mp4}{\textcolor{blue}{\textbf{video link}}}.

Systems and Control.title: A Tutorial on Shape Servoing of Deformable Objects-Part II: Advanced Concepts
Systems and Control.summary: In robotics, shape control, or shape servoing, refers to the automatic manipulation of a deformable object toward a desired shape. This article is the second of a two-part tutorial on data-driven, Jacobian-based shape control, in which the deformation Jacobian, a local model of how robot motion changes the measured shape, is estimated from measurements. Part I built the shape-servoing loop and derived a local stability condition. This paper starts by using the singular value decomposition of the deformation Jacobian to identify shape changes that can be produced by small robot motions, those that require large robot motions, and those that are locally unavailable. It then analyses how the choice of shape features determines how the controller regulates the object's shape and, therefore, how much the object deforms on its way to the target. It then describes three ways in which the shape control loop can fail: loss of controllability, loss of observability, and occurrence of mechanical instabilities. It closes with shape-control extensions to time-varying targets, secondary tasks, and three-dimensional objects.
Systems and Control.comment: Part II of a two-part tutorial. 10 pages, 9 figures. Code: https://github.com/nachocz/tutorial_on_shape_servoing_of_deformable_objects. Interactive demos: https://nachocz.github.io/tutorial_on_shape_servoing_of_deformable_objects/

Systems and Control.title: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
Systems and Control.summary: Sensorized human demonstrations offer scalable data for mobile manipulation, but embodiment differences complicate policy learning. We present Pixel-UMI, a pipeline for learning environment-aware whole-body policies from human data. We first introduce Environment-Aware Retargeting (EAR), which combines reconstructed scene geometry with demonstrated head and gripper trajectories to determine robot posture and generate collision-aware joint and base targets. Delay-calibrated action assignment converts these trajectories into actions. However, kinematic differences can leave residual pose errors, creating viewpoint mismatches between human demonstrations and robot observations. We therefore introduce Retargeting-Error-Aware Masking (REAM), which uses these errors during training to reduce reliance on mismatched views at deployment. Finally, because estimated actions cannot fully capture contact-rich interactions, we collect on-policy human corrections through DAgger to improve performance. We evaluate Pixel-UMI on five challenging tasks spanning articulated-object manipulation, deformable-object handling, constrained-space reaching, whole-body collision avoidance, and contact-rich bimanual coordination, achieving 87.0% average task progress. Video results are available at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel-umi
Systems and Control.comment: Video results are available at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel-umi

Systems and Control.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
Systems and Control.summary: General-purpose mobile manipulation requires a combination of capable robot hardware, scalable demonstration collection, expressive whole-body control, and effective policy learning. Yet these components are often developed independently, creating mismatches that limit the capabilities of the complete system. We present Pixel, a co-designed full-stack system for learning general-purpose mobile manipulation. Pixel combines a low-cost wheeled humanoid with human-aligned kinematics and compliant grippers, multiple teleoperation and robot-free human data-collection interfaces, a unified whole-body controller, and a common policy learning pipeline across human and robot demonstrations. A hierarchical learning stack further enables language-conditioned visuomotor control and long-horizon task execution. We evaluate the system across hardware, data collection, and policy learning, and demonstrate mobile-manipulation behaviors requiring dexterity, active perception, navigation, and whole-body coordination. We hope that Pixel provides an integrated and extensible foundation for studying how robot hardware, data, control, and learning can be designed together for robot learning. More results at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel

Systems and Control.title: Adaptive Low-Rank Quantum Kernel Acquisition under Finite-Shot Measurements: Perturbation Guarantees for QSVMs
Systems and Control.summary: Quantum kernel methods require estimating entries of a dense Gram matrix through repeated circuit measurements, making kernel construction expensive and statistically noisy. For a dataset of size $n$, dense construction requires $O(n^2)$ kernel queries, while existing approximation methods typically assume inexpensive access to kernel entries or use non-adaptive sampling. We study adaptive low-rank quantum kernel acquisition when the kernel is accessible only through a finite-shot quantum overlap oracle. Our framework, ICAQKL, uses residual-driven incomplete Cholesky construction to acquire informative kernel columns sequentially and form a positive-semidefinite rank-$r$ surrogate, reducing the training-kernel acquisition cost to $O(nrN_s)$ circuit executions for $r\ll n$, where $N_s$ is the number of shots per queried entry. The central difficulty is that finite-shot errors perturb both the queried kernel values and the adaptive pivot sequence that determines the low-rank factor. We develop a non-asymptotic perturbation framework for this stochastic adaptive process, establishing concentration over the realized queries, stability of noisy pivot selection and factor construction, and propagation of the coupled sampling and approximation errors to the QSVM objective, optimizer, prediction function, and classification margin. The resulting rank--shot conditions characterize when ICAQKL approaches the full QSVM induced by the same quantum feature map. Experiments on benchmark and biomedical datasets show favorable accuracy--query-cost tradeoffs, competitive performance with the full QSVM, and competitive or improved performance relative to the evaluated Nyström baselines under comparable settings. ICAQKL is intended to enable measurement-efficient and theoretically controlled use of a selected quantum kernel, rather than to establish quantum advantage over classical kernels.

Systems and Control.title: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models
Systems and Control.summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) hold promise for zero-shot video task-progress estimation in robot learning, yet existing frameworks frequently suffer from confirmation bias, hallucinating progress in failed executions due to implicit success assumptions or relative temporal ranking designs. Naive prompting of frontier models collapses into a binary success detector that fails to capture nuanced, non-linear progress and failures. While post-training approaches can mitigate this through explicit training, they demand expensive real-world robotics data and require computationally intensive post-training for every individual base model. To resolve these limitations, we introduce D&A (Describe & Assess): our approach decouples progress estimation into an objective, task-grounded textual description of scene dynamics followed by an assessment phase using explicit rubrics. By compelling the VLM to synthesize an explicit, text-based definition of absolute success before scoring, the framework anchors evaluations to an external, global criterion rather than the video's internal timeline. Empirical results demonstrate that our method calibrates zero-shot estimates and mitigates confirmation bias, providing fine-grained, partial progress metrics that accurately penalize failed executions while correctly interpolating successful runs. Being purely prompt-based, D&A generalizes across tasks, embodiments, and benchmarks---matching or surpassing post-trained reward models---and its reward estimates enable efficient downstream reinforcement learning.

Systems and Control.title: Dynamical Unbalanced Optimal Transport: Duality, Reachability, and Computation
Systems and Control.summary: We study dynamical unbalanced optimal transport for nonlinear control-affine systems in which the control input affects both the transportation of mass and its growth or decay. This phenomenon arises naturally in controlled transport-reaction systems such as cancer treatment, and distinguishes the problem from standard unbalanced optimal transport, where transport and mass variation are typically independent. To address this problem, we combine classical relaxed-control theory with a weighted superposition principle to obtain an infinite-dimensional linear programming reformulation over weighted trajectories. Under suitable convexity and compactness assumptions, we show that this relaxation is tight. Based on the relaxation, we derive a Kantorovich dual formulation in terms of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman inequalities, and establish strong duality over smooth subsolutions. We then utilize the dual formulation to characterize reachability of the system, namely, when a given terminal measure is reachable from a given initial measure. In addition, tractable sufficient conditions for reachability are provided. Finally, we develop an augmented-Lagrangian algorithm based on the dual formulation for numerical computation of the optimal transport plan. The framework is illustrated on a phenotype-structured cancer treatment problem in which therapy simultaneously drives phenotypic adaptation and population growth or death.

Systems and Control.title: Reinforcement Twinning via Twin-Calibrated Bayesian Policy Search and Replay-Driven Identification
Systems and Control.summary: The feasibility of updating and synchronising digital twins of actuated systems from operational data depends strongly on how the system is controlled and, consequently, on the data generated during operation. This establishes a direct link between control actuation and model identifiability. This work presents a reinforcement-twinning framework that exploits this link through three computational components. A Gaussian-process surrogate of the physical return combines the twin prediction, used as a calibrated trend, with a discrepancy learned from measured returns, allowing Bayesian policy search to exploit the twin without being tied to its predictions. Candidate policies are proposed around the policy that is optimal for the twin, while measured returns can expand this region. The resulting physical episodes are replayed on the twin after observer-based synchronisation with sparse measurements, and its parameters are identified by combining Bayesian optimisation with gradient-based refinement. Selected information-oriented episodes deploy an excitation policy to improve parameter identifiability. The framework is demonstrated on a Burgers-flow analogue of dynamic-induction control in wind farms, with a deliberately misspecified model structure. Despite substantially biased return predictions, the twin provides a useful starting policy and search region, placing the guided search ahead of unguided Bayesian optimisation from its first physical evaluations. This advantage is maintained when the search region is allowed to expand in response to changes in measured returns, whereas searches over-constrained by the twin-defined region are eventually overtaken by the unguided alternatives. The results support reinforcement twinning as a framework for jointly adapting models and control policies when physical interaction is limited and model discrepancy cannot be neglected.

Systems and Control.title: Delay-Certified Readiness Barriers for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation Without Lipschitz Constants
Systems and Control.summary: Overactuated multirotors can produce the same wrench with many rotor-speed combinations, some of which leave the vehicle unable to change its wrench quickly, e.g., to reject a gust. Readiness barriers keep this ability, the readiness, above a floor, but only in continuous time; with sampled commands and varying speed-controller delays, the available robustness bound covers less than one millisecond. We remove this limit by exploiting the structure of the problem: each rotor responds monotonically and in closed form to its own torque, so the speeds reachable under uncertain switching times lie in a cheaply computed box, and the lowest readiness over that box sits at a corner known in advance. This yields a Lipschitz-free test that a command keeps the readiness above its floor until the next sample, plus a fallback torque that keeps the vehicle on a certified plan. In hexarotor simulations with 2--40~ms delays and $\pm2$~ms jitter, the filter never violated the floor. At $10\pm2$~ms, it matched a delay-compensating predictor within the design envelope and cost 2--30\% more tracking error beyond it, where the predictor alone violated the floor in 2 to 16 of 16 missions.
Systems and Control.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

Systems and Control.title: Reusable Neural Reachability via Local Refinement
Systems and Control.summary: This paper studies obstacle avoidance under translation invariant dynamics using an avoid-side travel cost Hamilton Jacobi formulation. For running costs that are zero outside an obstacle and strictly negative inside it, we prove that the value function is non-positive everywhere, equals zero exactly outside the avoid set, and is strictly negative exactly on it. Under translation invariance, this yields a reuse principle: the value of any translated obstacle is obtained by translating a single template value function. We show that the pointwise minimum of translated template values exactly characterizes the union of the translated single-obstacle avoid sets and provides a conservative inner certificate of unavoidable collision in clutter. To reduce conservatism, we introduce a blockwise composition framework in which subsets of obstacles are merged and solved jointly. This yields a hierarchy of conservative certificates from singleton reuse to the exact clutter value, together with monotonicity under block merging and an exactness criterion based on the existence of a common clutter avoiding control. The framework is illustrated on a Dubins car example in a repeated clutter field.

Systems and Control.title: ISAC-Assisted Proactive Handover in mmWave Networks: Value of Foresight and Localization Requirements
Systems and Control.summary: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) links can lose tens of decibels within milliseconds when a person or vehicle crosses the line of sight, and reactive handover recovers only after the outage has begun. Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) promises to let the network see blockers coming and move users to another cell in advance. This paper asks how much such foresight is worth relative to the best reactive handover, and what sensing accuracy is needed to harvest it. We formulate cost-aware cell selection with knowledge of the future signal-to- noise ratio as a sequential decision problem, define the value of foresight through a policy-independent bound, and develop an ISAC-assisted handover framework in which a radio unit senses blockers with its own communication waveform and a simulated Open RAN xApp plans handovers. Ray-traced experiments in a 28 GHz street canyon, reported on held-out scenarios, show that, with a short look-ahead, perfect foresight closes most of the gap between service-aware (Layer-3) reactive handover and an instantaneous oracle. Harvesting this value, however, requires the user and nearby blockers to be localized to about a decimeter, well beyond what our radar tracker and meter- level user positioning provide; with realistic errors, even an uncertainty-aware planner largely defers to reactive handover.

Systems and Control.title: On the Comparison of Reinforcement Learning and Adaptive Control for Linear Systems under Packet Loss and Uncertainty
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents a comparative study between Adaptive Quantized Control (AQC) and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) reinforcement learning for uncertain linear systems with input quantization over communication channels subject to packet loss. The considered setting also includes dynamic switching from a nominal unstable system to a more unstable one during operation. The AQC is designed for unknown system dynamics using acknowledgment messages to compensate for packet losses, whereas the DDPG controller is trained using the nominal system model without acknowledgment messages. Numerical results show that the DDPG controller achieves faster transient responses and improved damping within its training environment. However, under model uncertainty, packet loss, and dynamic switching, the AQC consistently demonstrates superior robustness owing to its rigorous Lyapunov stability guarantees. These results highlight the trade-off between data-driven performance and model-based robustness, and provide insight into the applicability of reinforcement learning and adaptive control for networked uncertain systems.
Systems and Control.comment: Extended and revised version of the paper published in the Proceedings of the SIAM Conference on Control and Its Applications (CT23). doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611977745

Systems and Control.title: A Bayesian Framework for Safe Optimal Control of Unknown Systems from Input-Output Data
Systems and Control.summary: As control engineering is applied to increasingly complex systems, learning-based control, which uses empirical data to reduce the reliance on first-principles models, has emerged as a promising paradigm. However, such approaches must cope with nonlinear and stochastic dynamics, the absence of state measurements, and scarce data, while ensuring safe operation under constraints, which requires rigorous uncertainty quantification. Whereas existing methods treat these challenges in isolation, this article proposes a Bayesian framework that jointly addresses them. A prior in state-space form is updated from input-output data using particle Markov chain Monte Carlo methods, yielding a representation of joint uncertainty over dynamics and latent states. Building on this representation, a validation procedure is developed that provides probabilistic guarantees for constraint satisfaction under arbitrary causal control laws. For control synthesis, a formulation penalizing the conditional value-at-risk of the constraint function is proposed, together with an adaptive calibration mechanism that adjusts the performance-robustness trade-off to achieve a desired robustness level. The probability of successful certification is characterized theoretically. The framework is extended to a receding-horizon setting, where posterior updates from new measurements allow the controller to progressively reduce uncertainty and improve performance. The approach is demonstrated on the optimal control of a vertical farm.
Systems and Control.comment: 15 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to Automatica. Code available at https://github.com/TUM-ITR/PosteriorScenarioPlanning.jl

Systems and Control.title: A Survey of Freshness-Aware Wireless Networking with Reinforcement Learning
Systems and Control.summary: The age of information (AoI) has become a central measure of data freshness in modern wireless systems. Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising approach to AoI optimization, enabling adaptive decision-making in dynamic and stochastic wireless environments without requiring precise system models. Yet existing surveys either focus on classical AoI formulations or provide broad discussions of RL in wireless networks without addressing freshness as a unified learning problem. Motivated by this gap, this survey examines RL specifically through the lens of AoI and generalized freshness optimization. Motivated by this gap, this survey examines RL specifically through the lens of AoI and generalized freshness optimization. We organize AoI and its variants into native, function-based, and application-oriented families, providing a clearer view of how freshness should be modeled in B5G and 6G systems. Building on this foundation, we introduce a policy-centric taxonomy that reflects the decisions most relevant to freshness, consisting of update-control RL, medium-access RL, risk-sensitive RL, and multi-agent RL. This structure provides a coherent framework for understanding how learning can support important wireless networking problems, including sampling, scheduling, UAV trajectory planning, medium access, and distributed coordination. We further synthesize recent progress in RL-driven freshness control and highlight open challenges. The goal is to establish a unified foundation for learning-based freshness optimization in next-generation wireless networks.
Systems and Control.comment: Revised and expanded manuscript with an updated author list

Systems and Control.title: Distributed Adaptive Estimation with ISS Guarantees for Sensor Networks with Partially Unknown Source Dynamics
Systems and Control.summary: This paper studies distributed adaptive estimation over sensor networks with partially unknown source dynamics. We present parallel continuous-time and discrete-time designs in which each node runs a local adaptive observer and exchanges information over a directed graph. For both time scales, we establish stability of the network coupling operators, prove boundedness of all internal signals, and show convergence of each node's estimate to the source despite model uncertainty and disturbances. We further derive input-to-state stability (ISS) bounds that quantify robustness to bounded process noise. A key distinction is that the discrete-time design uses constant adaptive gains and per-step regressor normalization to handle sampling effects, whereas the continuous-time design does not. A unified Lyapunov framework links local observer dynamics with graph topology. Simulations on star, cyclic, and path networks corroborate the analysis, demonstrating accurate tracking, robustness, and scalability with the number of sensing nodes.
Systems and Control.comment: This version is accepted for publication in the 2026 IFAC World Conference

Systems and Control.title: Beyond GNSS: Leveraging LEO Satellite Signals of Opportunity for Doppler Positioning
Systems and Control.summary: Large constellations of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites provide ubiquitous global connectivity; yet, their rapid motion introduces significant Doppler shift effects. While challenging for communication, these effects can be leveraged for precise user terminal (UT) positioning, particularly in GNSS-denied environments where traditional satellite-based navigation struggles. Unlike GNSS, most LEO satellites lack dedicated navigation signals, motivating signals-of-opportunity (SOPs) approaches that repurpose existing LEO signals and use publicly available two-line element (TLE) files for orbital information, although ephemeris errors can limit accuracy. This article explores the fundamental principles, challenges, and enabling technologies for LEO-based Doppler shift positioning, highlighting its advantages over conventional non-Doppler methods, and discussing future research directions. Furthermore, to facilitate realistic and reproducible performance evaluation beyond stochastic modeling, we propose SionnaNTN-RT, a ray tracing framework for non-terrestrial network (NTN) built upon Sionna, enabling end-to-end simulation of Doppler-based positioning. Simulation results demonstrate that Doppler-based positioning can achieve high positioning accuracy in both urban and open-sky environments, highlighting its promise for next-generation positioning systems.

Systems and Control.title: Grid-Mode-Aware AI Data Center Power Smoothing via Bayesian-Optimized Hybrid Energy Storage System
Systems and Control.summary: AI data centers exhibit highly stochastic, volatile power demands from intensive workloads and synchronized GPU training cycles, which can excite grid natural frequencies and threaten system stability. This paper proposes a real-time, forecasting-independent control framework utilizing a Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS) that coordinates a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) and a supercapacitor (SC). Employing a parameterized frequency-decoupling and active modal-damping policy, the framework mitigates critical oscillatory load components while smoothing overall power fluctuations. To bypass the heavy computational burden of online receding-horizon optimization, this work introduces an offline Bayesian Optimization (BO) approach to optimally tune real-time control parameters, minimizing a multi-objective cost function that balances grid compliance penalties and storage degradation. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed method ensures grid stability and strong target envelope adherence. Specifically, it reshapes extreme 75-160 MW raw demand fluctuations to largely fit within a tight 10 MW target band, with only brief transient excursions, while attenuating the critical 20 MW oscillatory component below 1 MW to suppress resonant excitation.
Systems and Control.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, Submitted, 2027 IEEE Texas Power and Energy Conference (TPEC)

Systems and Control.title: Transformer-guided Variable Projection for Phasor and Fault-Time Estimation Under DDC Offset
Systems and Control.summary: Decaying DC (DDC) offsets introduce substantial phasor estimation errors during the first post-fault cycle. Recent approaches have sought interpretable waveform representations, but identifying analytical expressions can incur substantial computational costs. This paper proposes a transformer-guided variable-projection estimator that extracts the fundamental phasor, DDC parameters, and fault inception time from point-on-wave (POW) samples as an interpretable analytical expression. An offline-trained transformer provides the signal structure and decay rate, while variable projection refines the parameters and handles windows containing the fault without knowledge of time of fault. Across single- and dual-DDC scenarios with time constants of 2.5--400~ms, the mean maximum overshoot (MO) is at most 2.7% on post-fault windows and 2.2% during online operation, where the DFT reaches 10--14%. The post-fault phasor settles within 5% approximately 12.5~ms after inception. Circuit-level validation on a 230-kV two-source system yields 1.6% mean MO, compared with 9.5% for the DFT.
Systems and Control.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to PESGM

Systems and Control.title: Non-Coherent Over-the-Air Distributed Consensus: Algorithm Design and Power Control Optimization
Systems and Control.summary: Non-coherent over-the-air (NCOTA) aggregation offers a scalable and communication-efficient approach to distributed average consensus in wireless networks, without requiring instantaneous channel state information (CSI) or phase alignment. However, persistent aggregation errors pose fundamental challenges in achieving exact average consensus under nominal distributed averaging protocols. In this paper, we develop an NCOTA consensus framework that accommodates row-stochastic mixing, without requiring the conventional average-preservation property of doubly stochastic mixing matrices. Building on a distributed optimization formulation of average consensus, we propose a decentralized projected gradient descent with row-stochastic mixing (DPGD-RS) algorithm and establish its mean-square convergence to the exact average of the agents' initial states. We further derive a closed-form upper bound on the mean-square consensus error, characterizing the effects of aggregation uncertainty, network connectivity, and mixing imbalance. Guided by this analysis, we propose a spectral-reshaping power control (SR-PC) scheme that jointly optimizes transmit powers and receive-scaling factors to accelerate convergence by balancing aggregation accuracy and network mixing. Numerical results validate the theoretical convergence guarantees and demonstrate that the proposed power control scheme significantly accelerates convergence compared with full-power transmission and spectral-radius-minimization benchmarks.
Systems and Control.comment: 13 pages, 4 figures. Extended version of a paper published in Proc. IEEE ICC 2025

Systems and Control.title: Algebraic Characterization of Time-Varying Set Invariance
Systems and Control.summary: The verification of temporal forward invariance for dynamical systems subject to time-varying constraints is a foundational problem in the analysis of safety-critical systems. Existing methodologies rely on restrictive geometric assumptions, such as the Linear Independence Constraint Qualification (LICQ), or suffer from exponential computational complexity when applied to time-varying polytopes. This paper establishes a rigorous, unified, and computationally tractable framework for temporal safety verification. First, utilizing tools from nonsmooth analysis, we prove that a Nagumo-type geometric inclusion evaluated strictly on the boundary of the augmented graph is both necessary and sufficient for temporal forward invariance. Second, we provide an algebraic characterization of this condition requiring only the weaker Abadie Constraint Qualification (ACQ), generalizing standard Control Barrier Function (CBF) boundary conditions to non-smooth, multi-constraint domains. Finally, for the practical class of Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems with time-varying polytopic constraints, we deploy Farkas' Lemma to eliminate exponential vertex enumeration. By introducing a Lipschitz-bounded time-discretization scheme, we reduce the infinite-dimensional continuous-time verification problem to a finite, highly tractable set of decoupled Linear Programs (LPs).
Systems and Control.comment: The paper was accepted for publication in the CDC 2026

Systems and Control.title: Residual-Corrected Equivalent-Circuit Model with Universal Differential Equations for Robust Battery Voltage Prediction under Operating-Condition Shift
Systems and Control.summary: Accurate terminal-voltage prediction underpins model-based battery management, yet low-order equivalent-circuit models (\ecm{}) lack expressiveness under transient conditions, whereas purely data-driven predictors sacrifice interpretability and may degrade under operating-condition shift. This paper introduces a residual-corrected hybrid formulation in which a first-order Thevenin \ecm{} (\ecmrc{}) provides the dominant voltage structure, and a compact neural network embedded as a universal differential equation (\ude{}) corrects only the latent polarization mismatch. The \ecmrc{} parameters identified by nonlinear least squares warm-start the hybrid model so that the learned component operates in a low-residual regime. Experiments on a public Panasonic 18650PF dataset compare the proposed \ecmude{} with standalone \ecmrc{} and Long Short-Term Memory (\lstm{}) baselines across four axes: matched-condition prediction on UDDS at \SI{25}{\celsius}, inference-time perturbation of the supplied state-of-charge (\SOC{}, denoted $z$) input, zero-shot temperature transfer (\SI{25}{\celsius} to \SI{-20}{\celsius}), and zero-shot drive-cycle transfer to US06, LA92, and HWFET. The proposed \ecmude{} achieves the lowest voltage error in every setting, reducing mean absolute error (\mae{}) by 48\% relative to the \lstm{} under matched conditions and showing an order-of-magnitude lower inter-seed variability (coefficient of variation: 0.44\% vs.\ 6.20\%). Substantial gains persist under challenging distribution shifts, indicating that the physical model anchors prediction where a purely learned model is most vulnerable. These results position residual-corrected \ecmude{} as a lightweight and interpretable enhancement of low-order circuit models for voltage prediction in battery management systems (\bms{}).
Systems and Control.comment: This paper has been withdrawn by the author. The reported improvement of the hybrid model was found to depend on an evaluation protocol in which the state of charge was computed with information from the complete test profile. A revised study using a causal evaluation protocol reaches different conclusions and will be released separately

Systems and Control.title: Safe-Ballbot: Tilt-Consistent MPC with Control Barrier Functions for Ballbot Navigation
Systems and Control.summary: Ball-balancing robots (ballbots) must lean to accelerate, and the lean is limited by the wheel torques and by safety. Planners that use the full robot model are expensive, while planners that ignore the balance dynamics produce references that cannot be followed. This paper presents a two-layer navigation scheme for a three-omni-wheel ballbot. The upper layer is a model predictive controller on a \emph{jerk model} of the ball position, with discrete-time control barrier functions for static, moving, rotating and concave obstacles. The lower layer is a hierarchical sliding mode controller with an extended state observer and a robust exponential control barrier function on the tilt (HSMC-ESO-ECBF). The layers are linked by an acceleration bound derived in closed form from the largest steady tilt that the barrier function admits, so that the plan never asks for a lean the tracker refuses. For obstacles whose motion is only predicted, the obstacles are inflated by conformal prediction radii that bound the prediction error with a prescribed probability. In MuJoCo, with omni-wheel roller contacts and torque saturation, the scheme keeps at least $10$\,cm of clearance, tracks the plan within $2$\,cm RMS, keeps the tilt below the limit and plans in $9$--$12$\,ms, $10$--$15$ times faster than a full-model nonlinear MPC that enters the inflated obstacles; with predicted obstacles, the conformal inflation removes the collisions of a constant-velocity predictor in $30$ random crossing scenarios and reduces them in an endless run on a closed path.The source code and video illustrations are available at https://safe-ballbot.github.io

Systems and Control.title: Dynamic Modeling of Transmission Networks, Grid-Following Inverters, and UPS-Based AI Data Centers
Systems and Control.summary: This document presents dynamic models of a transmission network and average models of power-electronic devices and loads in the synchronous $dq$ frame. We model the network in the positive sequence and its synchronous generators with the classical swing equation and a first-order turbine governor. The power-electronic models cover grid-following inverters and AI data centers. Each inverter has a phase-locked loop, a power controller, and a current controller. Each data center connects to the grid through two step-down transformers. Its low-voltage bus feeds an IT load, an induction-motor cooling load, and a constant-impedance load. A double-conversion uninterruptible power supply (UPS) serves the IT load. We model its rectifier, grid-forming output inverter, battery, and bidirectional DC-DC converter. A measured GPU power trace drives the IT demand. We replace every non-smooth operation with a smooth surrogate. This keeps the discretized model continuously differentiable for the nonlinear solver. We also show how we initialize each model at its power-flow operating point.

Systems and Control.title: Output-feedback controller design for switched systems under graph-constrained switching
Systems and Control.summary: Switched systems operating under a switching constraint are commonly paired with a digraph encoding the possible mode switches. Thereby, edges are associated with the modes of the switched system and the vertices encode the mode switching history. To control those switched systems under graph-constrained switching, an established method is to design vertex-dependent controllers, that is one controller gain per vertex of the graph, which has lead to various results for static feedback controllers. In this paper, we explore the design of edge-dependent controllers. Edge-dependency allows to synthesize dynamic output feedback controllers in a convex manner by means of a Linear Matrix Inequality problem with the additional requirement that the active mode is known. Further, we show that edge-dependency offers a potentially less conservative static output feedback controller design compared to vertex-dependent controllers. We illustrate our results by a numerical example.

Systems and Control.title: Susceptibility optimization for wisdom of crowds: A social power reformulation and realization framework
Systems and Control.summary: Whether social influence makes a crowd wiser or more biased hinges on who yields to others and who holds firm. Such heterogeneous susceptibilities to social influence, together with the influence network, determine the weight each agent's initial estimate carries in the collective estimate, known as social power. This paper studies susceptibility optimization for maximizing the wisdom of crowds under the Friedkin-Johnsen model. Minimizing the squared collective bias over susceptibilities leads to a nonconvex problem. To overcome this nonconvexity, we develop a social power reformulation and realization framework, which decomposes the problem into two stages: first characterizing the social power that minimizes the collective bias, then determining the susceptibilities that induce such social power. Social power reformulation yields a quadratic program over the probability simplex. Under uniform-sign biases, the optimal social power concentrates on the least biased agents and immediately determines the optimal susceptibilities; under mixed-sign biases, its geometry enables a linear-time construction algorithm. For social power realization, we introduce the notions of susceptibility realizability and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for them, under which we derive all optimal susceptibilities in closed form using the Laplacian pseudoinverse and eigenvector centrality. These results yield a unified algorithm that solves the original problem globally, with worst-case complexity cubic in the number of agents when realizability holds. Finally, we develop a fully distributed implementation with linear communication complexity, illustrating how collective intelligence can emerge from local interactions.

Systems and Control.title: Model Predictive Control of Heating Systems via Koopman-Operator Bilinearization
Systems and Control.summary: Hydronic heat emitters are widely used in buildings, but their control is challenging due to nonlinear dynamics, arising from both the heat transfer in each emitter and the hydraulic coupling among those that share a circulating pump. These nonlinearities are often simplified or neglected in the literature. In this paper, we use Koopman theory to make the resulting model more tractable for control. In particular, we propose an input reparameterization and construct an infinite-dimensional set of observables that yields an exact bilinear representation of the system in the chosen lifted space. We then show that truncating the infinite-dimensional representation leads to bounded approximation errors that decrease as the truncation order increases, as well as bounded trajectory deviations over a finite horizon. The resulting bilinear model is incorporated into a model predictive control (MPC) framework to provide thermal comfort in multi-zone buildings while reducing energy use. Using a numerical case study of a five-story building with 20 zones, we show that the proposed Koopman-based MPC achieves a realized performance cost close to that of nonlinear MPC with faster solve times, and outperforms MPC formulations based on time-invariant and time-varying linearizations.

Systems and Control.title: BeyondContact: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Airflow-Based Non-Contact Manipulation
Systems and Control.summary: Contact-based robotic manipulation is constrained by end-effector reachability and the mechanical properties of objects. Airflow can exert forces without direct robot-object contact, enabling manipulation of objects beyond the reach or when direct contact is undesirable. However, the lack of suitable simulation has hindered the application of reinforcement learning to airflow-based manipulation, limiting the broader adoption of this mechanism compared with contact-based methods. To address this gap, we developed a robot- and task-agnostic airflow extension for Isaac Lab that supports massively parallel training. The extension uses experimentally identified airflow models to compute the forces and torques exerted on objects. Based on this extension, we train a hybrid push-blow (HPB) policy that combines contact-based pushing with airflow manipulation and a rectangular reorientation (RR) policy that controls a cuboid's heading using airflow alone. To enable physical execution, we design a lightweight, high-speed blower that coexists with a gripper. In zero-shot real-world deployment, HPB achieves an 80% success rate over 20 trials, while RR achieves a mean absolute heading error of 2.6 degrees across four target headings. The project materials are available at https://github.com/iit-DLSLab/BeyondContact.
