On chromosome 19 haplotypes from the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium, finding the maximal exact matches of length at least 1000 of two haplotypes, on both strands, takes 5.5 to 5.7 seconds with 16, 32 or 64 other individuals, while backward search on a run-length compressed suffix array of the same collection takes 40 to 60 seconds and grows with the collection. We compare this with suffix-tree path decompositions (STPDs): over the parse, an STPD is no faster and needs about twice the memory; over the text it is about 1.7 times faster but needs the whole text in memory, about five times the space; and the published STPD-index, which compresses its text with relative Lempel-Ziv, is 8 to 10 times slower. Keeping a toehold through all three kinds of steps lets the search also list every occurrence of every MEM, for about 2 more seconds.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Reportable Shortcuts with RLBWTs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Backward search over a run-length compressed Burrows-Wheeler transform (RLBWT) takes one step per pattern character, even when long stretches of the pattern match material that recurs throughout a highly repetitive collection. We describe shortcuts: for a precomputed set of pairs $(α,β)$ of strings, a backward search that has just matched $β$ and finds $α$ immediately to its left in the pattern can cross $α$ in one step. Since a shortcut is taken only after its pair has been recognized in the pattern, the search returns a report of the shortcuts it took along with the usual BWT interval. Our motivation is pangenome graphs, where such pairs mark the places where a pattern passes through a vertex, so the report gives the path a match takes through the graph. We work out the case of a single linear reference $R$, with $β$ ranging over the length-$\ell$ windows of $R$ starting at multiples of $\ell$, and $α$ over the $2^t \ell$ characters preceding such a window. We show that the search counts correctly, that under stated conditions it crosses a stretch of the pattern matching $m$ consecutive windows of $R$ with $O(\log m + m / 2^τ)$ shortcuts, where $2^τ\ell$ is the longest shortcut, and that the shortcuts can be built efficiently from the RLBWT. On the Pizza&Chili cere collection of 37 genomes, shortcuts make backward search 2.3 to 4.2 times faster on exact patterns of length 200 to 1000, and 1.7 to 2.0 times faster with 1% of the characters substituted, for 86% more space. On 11 gigabases of genomes of seven bacterial species, they make it 1.6 to 1.9 times faster on exact patterns for 32% more space. On whole chromosome 19 haplotypes against 16 to 64 others from the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium, shortcuts in both directions make Boyer-Moore-Li search for maximal exact matches of length at least 1000 about 8 times faster.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Polynomial Lower Bounds for Steiner Shortcuts via Test Functions
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
The Steiner shortcut problem asks whether every directed graph $G=(V,E)$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges admits an augmentation $G_{+}=(V\cup V_{+},E\cup E_{+})$ with $m^{1+o(1)}$ edges such that $G_+$ has the same reachability structure as $G$ (i.e. for all $s,t\in V$, $s$ reaches $t$ in $G$ iff $s$ reaches $t$ in $G_+$), and the diameter of $G_{+}$ is $m^{o(1)}$. This is a core combinatorial question underlying many reachability algorithms in the dynamic, streaming, and CONGEST models, and all parallel algorithms with almost-linear work and sublinear depth.
  A sequence of works ruled out such a shortcut $G_{+}$ in the non-Steiner setting where $V_{+}=\emptyset$. However, as recently shown by Bernstein et al. [STOC '26], all known non-Steiner lower-bound constructions fail once Steiner vertices $V_{+}$ are allowed.
  This paper rules out almost-optimal Steiner shortcuts: we show an infinite family of graphs $G=(V,E)$ with the property that, for any $\varepsilon>0$, a Steiner shortcut $G_{+}=(V\cup V_{+},E\cup E_{+})$ with $m^{1+\varepsilon}$ edges must have diameter at least $n^{1/56-O(\varepsilon)}$.
  Our construction strengthens the standard non-Steiner lower-bound framework via an additional structure that allows Steiner vertices to be replaced by original vertices; we can then reduce back to the standard arguments without Steiner vertices. This new structure is achieved via a new general strategy based on test functions, which is quite flexible and can potentially be extended to applications beyond our work.
  We also generalize our lower bound to exact Steiner hopsets in undirected graphs and to depth reduction for monotone circuits. The latter significantly strengthens the classical lower bound based on Sylvester matrices.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Resolving Tusnády's Problem
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We prove a lower bound of $Ω_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ for the worst-case combinatorial discrepancy of $N$-point sets with respect to anchored boxes in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$. Together with Nikolov's upper bound of the same order and Wei's planar lower bound, this settles Tusnády's problem: the discrepancy of axis-parallel boxes is $Θ_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. The proof combines smoothed product test functions, sampling discretization, and an entropy argument for conditioned Gaussian vectors.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Constructive Arboricity in Almost-Linear Time for Dense Graphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
The arboricity of a graph is the minimum number of forests needed to partition its edges. We present an algorithm that computes the exact arboricity of a simple graph and constructs an optimal forest partition in $\min\{n^{2+o(1)},m^{4/3+o(1)}\}$ time, where $n$ and $m$ denote the numbers of vertices and edges. This improves the previous $O(m^{3/2}\log(n^2/m))$ bound of Gabow. In particular, it runs in almost-linear time, $m^{1+o(1)}$, on dense graphs with $m=Θ(n^2)$.
  We also give an algorithm that constructs a partition into at most one more forest than optimal in $m^{1+o(1)}$ time. To our knowledge, it is the first almost-linear time algorithm for this problem.

Signal Processing.title: Joint Association and Beamforming Design for Cooperative ISAC Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Cooperation among multiple base stations (BSs) improves both communication and sensing in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks. However, it requires deciding which BSs serve each communication user (CU) and each target, and how each BS beamforms. In this work, we consider joint BS-CU and BS-target association, and beamforming for a general cooperative ISAC system, overcoming prior simplifications such as single-user or target setups, fixed BS roles, coherent radar or separate waveforms. We maximize a joint communication rate and position Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) based tradeoff utility while guaranteeing a minimum service per-CU using a data queue model. We develop a successive convex approximation (SCA)-based beamforming with closed-form updates. The discrete association problem is solved as an overarching layer using a low-complexity algorithm. Numerical results validate the effectiveness of the algorithm and unveil benefits of cooperative communication and sensing.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures

Signal Processing.title: Improper Signaling for Clutter-Limited Angle Estimation in ISAC
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) transmit designs typically optimize the transmit covariance under proper signaling, leaving the potential sensing benefits of pseudo-covariance unexplored. This paper investigates the conditions under which transmit pseudo-covariance can influence the angle Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) of a deterministic target in the presence of clutter. For a prescribed transmit covariance and a single clutter patch, we establish that CRB sensitivity occurs if and only if the clutter is illuminated, exhibits nonzero non-circularity, and overlaps the angle-informative component of the target response. This characterization demonstrates that angular separation alone does not determine whether transmit impropriety can improve sensing performance. We derive a closed-form optimal incident-field pseudo-variance that minimizes the angle CRB over the set of feasible transmit pseudo-covariances. Under fully non-circular clutter scattering, the optimal design eliminates the clutter-induced CRB penalty. Numerical results for a 32-antenna ISAC system show CRB reductions of up to 99% relative to proper sensing under complete overlap and 30% under partial overlap, as well as up to approximately 7 dB lower clutter-induced CRB penalty across target-clutter separations. These findings identify transmit pseudo-covariance as a conditional sensing design resource whose effectiveness depends on clutter statistics and projected target-clutter geometry.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, submitted to the IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC), 2027

Signal Processing.title: Integrated Identity Protection for Semantic Communications in Embodied IoT Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Embodied Internet of Things (IoT) systems are promoting the adoption of task-oriented semantic communication (SemCom), in which the trustworthy task decisions require both semantic information reliability and source legitimacy. However, existing trustworthy designs in SemCom mainly focus on semantic content recovery and protection, with limited attention to source legitimacy. Motivated by this limitation, this paper establishes a new information exploitation paradigm for integrated SemCom-identity protection to address active source impersonation and passive identity inference by treating each SemCom signal as an inherent carrier of both task-relevant semantic information and transmitter physical identity information. We first examine these two information resources and then analyze their integration feasibility at the observation, processing, and decision levels. To exploit these resources for trustworthy decision making, we further develop a dual-branch identity protection mechanism under different operating modes. In the authentication mode, semantic recovery and physical-layer source verification are performed in parallel using the same received observation. In the concealment mode, identity exposure is suppressed while semantic recovery quality is maintained to support anonymous sensing reports. The resulting outputs are jointly interpreted to support task decisions under mode-specific identity protection requirements. Finally, two representative case studies on active source impersonation and passive identity inference are presented to evaluate the proposed framework.

Signal Processing.title: A Foundation Model for Large-Scale Wireless Network Planning , Operation and Optimization
Signal Processing.summary: Wireless cellular networks form the connective tissue of human society, sustained by a continuous physical dialogue between engineered infrastructure and its surroundings. Radio signals emitted from base stations traverse terrain, diffract around buildings and scatter through streets before reaching billions of users. Together, these interactions produce the city-wide radio environment on which every network decision rests. Shaping this environment through deployment and optimization determines the connectivity societies rely on, yet learning it effectively at city scale and generalizing across diverse cities and deployments remain open challenges. Here we answer positively by introducing ChaRT, a foundation model that learns transferable radio representations from measurement reports generated by deployed cellular networks. These reports provide abundant multi-cell, multi-beam observations without dedicated campaigns, forming a scalable data foundation for city-scale learning. ChaRT embeds beam-level angular structure, network hierarchy and propagation-regime diversity in its architecture, and is pretrained through context-aware masked beam modelling and self-distillation with channel-model-constrained augmentation. We pretrain ChaRT on over one billion reports comprising 18.2 billion beam-level observations from 3,503 cells in one city. With a single set of weights, ChaRT reconstructs radio environments in unseen cities and transfers to radio map construction, new-site prediction and network parameter tuning. With only 1% of labelled data, it supports user localization, beam prediction, propagation scenario classification and estimation of the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio. The learned representation further enables beamspace clustering for reusable radio-grid construction. These results establish ChaRT as a transferable foundation for network-wide intelligence.

Signal Processing.title: ISAC-Assisted Proactive Handover in mmWave Networks: Value of Foresight and Localization Requirements
Signal Processing.summary: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) links can lose tens of decibels within milliseconds when a person or vehicle crosses the line of sight, and reactive handover recovers only after the outage has begun. Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) promises to let the network see blockers coming and move users to another cell in advance. This paper asks how much such foresight is worth relative to the best reactive handover, and what sensing accuracy is needed to harvest it. We formulate cost-aware cell selection with knowledge of the future signal-to- noise ratio as a sequential decision problem, define the value of foresight through a policy-independent bound, and develop an ISAC-assisted handover framework in which a radio unit senses blockers with its own communication waveform and a simulated Open RAN xApp plans handovers. Ray-traced experiments in a 28 GHz street canyon, reported on held-out scenarios, show that, with a short look-ahead, perfect foresight closes most of the gap between service-aware (Layer-3) reactive handover and an instantaneous oracle. Harvesting this value, however, requires the user and nearby blockers to be localized to about a decimeter, well beyond what our radar tracker and meter- level user positioning provide; with realistic errors, even an uncertainty-aware planner largely defers to reactive handover.

Signal Processing.title: Positivity of a Hadamard Product
Signal Processing.summary: A notable difference between the ordinary and Hadamard products is that the Hadamard product of two singular positive semidefinite matrices can be nonsingular. We present an eigenvalue lower bound for a Hadamard product that depends on a leading spectral projection of freely selected rank for one factor, and the smallest eigenvalues of certain principal submatrices of the other factor. Maximizing over the selected rank gives a stronger estimate; an effective-condition-number bound follows as a simpler consequence. We establish sharpness for prescribed ranks and effective condition numbers and examine limiting examples that delineate the bounds' usefulness. We give numerical examples and discuss applications in array signal processing and matrix time series analysis.

Signal Processing.title: Intra-Cell Spatial Reuse in LEO Downlinks: Beam-Leakage-Aware Satellite Scheduling
Signal Processing.summary: Dense low-earth-orbit (LEO) constellations offer an opportunity to increase local broadband capacity by serving multiple terminals in the same cell through concurrent satellite beams. However, interference between overlapping beams limits spatial reuse, and satellite selection based solely on link strength or angular separation may result in suboptimal performance. This paper proposes beam-leakage-aware satellite scheduling for Ku-band LEO downlink transmissions. With matched transmit and receive beamforming, we formulate a fixed-cardinality sum-rate maximization problem that jointly accounts for satellite-dependent received powers and pairwise receive-array leakage. A beam-leakage-aware branch-and-bound (BL-BnB) algorithm combines an admissible upper bound with greedy-plus-swap initialization to obtain globally optimal schedules for the reference-point model. We evaluate the method using a 24-h ephemeris-derived Starlink visibility trace with antenna and transmit-power models calibrated to public SpaceX filings. The results show that total capacity increases with beam count, but less than proportionally. With eight concurrent beams, BL-BnB improves mean per-beam capacity by 27.2% over nearest-satellite selection, primarily benefiting weaker links. BL-BnB achieves millisecond-scale runtimes in our evaluation, supporting the computational feasibility of optimal scheduling.

Signal Processing.title: Delay-Doppler Synchronization for Distributed Uplink Interference Nulling in LEO Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Cooperation among low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites provides spatial diversity for mitigating uplink interference that is difficult to suppress with a single onboard array. Coherent interference cancellation across satellites, however, requires compensation of the relative delay and Doppler of a common interferer. We analyze two-branch interference nulling with finite training and derive a closed-form approximation to the mean residual interference-to-noise ratio (INR). The approximation separates wrong acquisition, local synchronization errors, and weight-learning losses, linking performance to input INR, branch power imbalance, training length, and effective search size. Under a Gaussian surrogate with small errors and efficient, approximately unbiased refinement, correct acquisition yields a high-INR plateau of $2/N_v$, where $N_v$ is the valid training length. Synchronization and weight learning contribute equally to this limit, whereas persistent alignment bias adds a penalty that grows with input power. Monte Carlo experiments compare dense FFT/zoom and coarse FFT/gradient acquisition using matched final FIR refinement, branch-noise normalization, and independent test blocks. Both approach the predicted plateau at high input INR. Coarse search reduces measured search time by $6.7\times$ at an approximately 0.7-dB acquisition-threshold penalty. Controlled power-ratio sweeps show how branch imbalance delays reliable acquisition at fixed stronger-branch INR. A separate Starlink snapshot evaluation demonstrates comparable nulling performance under changing satellite geometry.

Signal Processing.title: Consistent Geometric Deep Learning via Hilbert Bundles and Cellular Sheaves
Signal Processing.summary: Modern deep learning architectures increasingly contend with sophisticated signals that are natively infinite-dimensional, such as time series, probability distributions, or operators, and are defined over irregular domains. Yet, a unified learning theory for these settings has been lacking. To start addressing this gap, we introduce a novel convolutional learning framework for possibly infinite-dimensional signals supported on a manifold. Namely, we use the connection Laplacian associated with a Hilbert bundle as a convolutional operator, and we derive filters and neural networks, dubbed as \textit{HilbNets}. We make HilbNets and, more generally, the convolution operation, implementable via a two-stage sampling procedure. First, we show that sampling the manifold induces a Hilbert Cellular Sheaf, a generalized graph structure with Hilbert feature spaces and edge-wise coupling rules, and we prove that its sheaf Laplacian converges in probability to the underlying connection Laplacian as the sampling density increases. Notably, this result is a generalization to the infinite-dimensional bundle setting of the Belkin \& Niyogi \cite{BELKIN20081289} convergence result for the graph Laplacian to the manifold Laplacian, a theoretical cornerstone of geometric learning methods. Second, we discretize the signals and prove that the discretized (implementable) HilbNets converge to the underlying continuous architectures and are transferable across different samplings of the same bundle, providing consistency for learning. Finally, we validate our framework on synthetic and real-world tasks. Overall, our results broaden the scope of geometric learning as a whole by lifting classical Laplacian-based frameworks to settings where the signal at each point lives in its own Hilbert space.
Signal Processing.comment: NeurIPS 2026 Spotlight. 52 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables

Signal Processing.title: Iteration-Free Candidate Pruning and an Index-Domain VLSI Architecture for Sort-Free MIMO Box Decoding up to 1024-QAM
Signal Processing.summary: Wi-Fi~7 and 5G NR use constellations up to $4096$-QAM and $1024$-QAM at multi-gigabit peak rates. The MIMO detector must sustain these rates at a low cost. Linear MMSE detection meets these rates at low cost but loses several dB in SNR. $K$-Best detection recovers this loss, but its per-layer sorting grows with the modulation order and needs large sorting networks or deep pipelines at these rates. Box Decoding is a sort-free tree-search detector whose complexity does not depend on the QAM order, and its deterministic pruning keeps the cost fixed as the MIMO size grows. Single-step candidate pruning (SCP) is fully parallel but less accurate, while iterative candidate pruning (ICP) is more accurate, but its selection loop costs either throughput or area. This paper proposes Max-Min-Exchange Candidate Pruning (MMECP), which replaces the selection loop of ICP with a single max-min exchange without a feedback path and keeps \mbox{near-$K$-Best} performance. The paper also presents a VLSI architecture that represents each candidate by its integer constellation index, so that candidates and their distances are obtained by bit selection instead of operations on symbol values. A $4\times4$ detector synthesized in TSMC $16$\,nm detects one vector per cycle at $1$\,GHz for $64$- to $1024$-QAM and produces up to $40$\,Gb/s, while its gate count grows by $63\%$ over this range. Its normalized hardware efficiency is $2.3\times$, $12\times$ and $14\times$ that of the best compared hard-output detector at $64$-, $256$- and $1024$-QAM.

Signal Processing.title: Box-Shift: Fixed-Complexity Counter-Hypothesis Generation for Soft-Output MIMO Box Decoding
Signal Processing.summary: Box Decoding is a sort-free tree-search multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detector with a fixed per-layer cost independent of the quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) order. Its regular datapath is well suited to hardware implementation, but the detector has so far been limited to hard-output operation in uncoded systems. Its fixed four-point box spans two adjacent Gray-coded QAM levels per axis, leaving most bits without counter-hypotheses for higher-order QAM. This missing counter-hypothesis (MCH) problem prevents the direct computation of finite max-log log-likelihood ratios (LLRs). We propose the \emph{Box-Shift} algorithm, which shifts the existing box to the nearest node carrying the complementary value of each Gray-coded bit at each detection layer. Unlike Bit-Flip, Box-Shift analytically identifies the partially optimal counter-hypothesis using one inverter per bit and updates the path metric through an index-domain increment. The proposed method preserves the sort-free, QAM-order-independent structure of Box Decoding. Coded $4\times4$ MIMO simulations using 5G~NR low-density parity-check (LDPC) coding show that Box Decoding with Box-Shift achieves a $0.7$--$1.5$\,dB gain in $E_b/N_0$ over the same detector with Bit-Flip at a bit error rate of $10^{-5}$, with equal soft-candidate budgets. For the soft-candidate metrics, the incremental update of Box-Shift needs $75\%$ fewer real multiplications than the explicit evaluation of Bit-Flip at a comparable number of real additions.

Signal Processing.title: A Bayesian Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg Model for Real-Time EEG Phase Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: Real-time phase estimation on stimulus-aligned transient EEG is critical for closed-loop neuromodulation systems targeting the theta-band, yet most real-time phase estimation methods have been developed and validated on resting-state, high-fidelity signals in the alpha band. Recent work has pursued deep learning architectures, while individualized classical bandpass filter tuning remains underexplored. This study characterizes the spectral and temporal properties of non-anticipative bandpass filtering and demonstrates the performance gains achieved through individualized tuning. We present a Bayesian-Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg (BOB) model evaluated on EEG recorded during peripheral vibrotactile stimulation of the left median nerve (theta, N=20 healthy subjects) and on resting-state recordings from the Max Planck Institute's LEMON dataset (alpha, N=20 healthy subjects). BOB was benchmarked against the Deep Dual-Branch Complex Neural Network (DBCNN), EEG Phase Prediction Network (EPN), Phastimate, and Phase Estimation with Autoregressive Padding (PEAP) under matched testing conditions: channel selection, individualized optimization, evaluation time points, and an offline reference phase obtained through zero-phase filtering and the Hilbert transform. Under these testing conditions, BOB achieved matched or better performance than these models at a fraction of the calibration time.
Signal Processing.comment: 24 pages, 12 figures (9 main, 3 supplements)

Signal Processing.title: Adapting Sleep Foundation Models for Dense Sleep Spindle Localization
Signal Processing.summary: Adapting sleep foundation models to dense electroencephalography (EEG) event localization is challenging because multi-second representations may not preserve sufficient temporal detail for precise boundary recovery. We address sleep spindle localization by adapting a frozen SleepFM encoder with a local time-frequency pathway that preserves spindle-relevant spectral content and intra-token position. The local representation drives localization, while residual cross-attention incorporates SleepFM temporal context. Dense predictions are obtained through localized token-to-sample reconstruction and temporal refinement. Tested on the Massive Online Data Annotation (MODA), the proposed model achieves an event-level $F_1$ of $0.8080 \pm 0.0040$ at IoU 0.2 across six folds. Ablations show that localization primarily depends on local spectral and sub-token temporal information, while the pretrained representation provides complementary context. These results indicate that dense adaptation benefits from preserving information below the pretrained token scale. Code will be released upon acceptance.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Submitted to IEEE ICASSP 2027 (under review)

Signal Processing.title: Distributed Consensus, Optimization, and Learning under Communication Constraints
Signal Processing.summary: Many modern engineering applications require distributed problem-solving in which multiple nodes in a network cooperate to achieve a common optimization objective. Numerous distributed optimization and learning algorithms rely on consensus-based distributed coordination to ensure network-wide agreement via iterative local interactions. In these algorithms, the accuracy, frequency, and reliability of information exchange among network nodes directly influence system performance, including convergence behavior, training delay, and model accuracy. This tutorial article adopts a bottom-up approach to present the fundamentals of consensus averaging and distributed optimization methods, and highlights the impact of network connectivity, information flow, and communication uncertainty on network cooperation and optimization performance. Building on these theoretical insights, we discuss key design principles for communication-constrained distributed learning across diverse network topologies and review common approaches to communication-efficient learning, particularly in wireless networks. Despite substantial progress, further efforts are needed to bridge the gap between theory and practice and fully realize the potential of cooperative and networked intelligence.
Signal Processing.comment: 20 pages, 3 figures, to appear in IEEE JSAC

Signal Processing.title: ARIA: Anti-diagonal Reduced-cost Index-masked Adaptive BLMS Algorithm
Signal Processing.summary: The block least-mean-square (BLMS) algorithm supports high-throughput adaptive filtering but incurs high computational cost as the filter length and block size increase. This letter proposes anti-diagonal reduced-cost index-masked (ARIA) adaptive BLMS, which reduces coefficient-update multiplications through anti-diagonal index masking and tap-wise step-size scaling while keeping the filtering exact. Mean-square error (MSE) analysis establishes an explicit step-size bound, and misadjustment. An extension, ARIA-MF (ARIA with masked filtering), also applies the mask during filtering; its analysis shows that the excess MSE is redistributed across block rows while its block average is approximately preserved. Simulations validate the analysis and shows very good agreement with the estimates

Signal Processing.title: OSD-JSCC: Neural Joint Source-Channel Coding with One-Step Diffusion
Signal Processing.summary: Neural joint source-channel coding (JSCC) enables efficient image transmission over noisy channels, yet distortion-optimized approaches often produce blurry reconstructions. While diffusion priors can enhance visual fidelity, their iterative sampling incurs substantial decoding latency. To address this limitation, we propose OSD-JSCC, an SNR-adaptive JSCC framework with a single diffusion step. Specifically, OSD-JSCC transmits pretrained variational autoencoder (VAE) latents through an SNR-conditioned JSCC codec and incorporates two key designs. First, we introduce a stochastic diffusion-state interface that enables the JSCC decoder to predict a Gaussian diffusion state rather than a clean latent, while extracting image-specific semantic tokens. The sampled diffusion state preserves spatial structure and provides a good initialization for one-step refinement, whereas the semantic tokens, together with an SNR token, guide the reconstruction process. Second, we develop SNR-conditioned feature modulation and adaptive timestep selection to jointly adapt latent transmission and diffusion refinement to varying channel conditions. Furthermore, we adopt a three-stage training strategy with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to efficiently adapt the pretrained diffusion prior to the JSCC task. Extensive experiments on Kodak and CLIC2020 demonstrate that OSD-JSCC achieves superior perceptual quality and decoding efficiency. Compared with existing diffusion-based JSCC baselines, OSD-JSCC reduces LPIPS by approximately 43% on Kodak and 53% on CLIC2020, while achieving up to a 50.6$\times$ reduction in decoding latency.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures. Code: https://github.com/tangshunpu/OSD-JSCC

Signal Processing.title: PARGAR: Pilot-Aware Graph Attention for Sparse-Pilot Neural OFDM Receivers
Signal Processing.summary: Reliable channel estimation and symbol detection in 5G New Radio (NR), as well as emerging 6G radio systems, rely on demodulation reference signals (DMRS). The density and placement of these pilots on the orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) time--frequency resource grid affect both receiver reliability and spectral efficiency. Sparse DMRS layouts increase the time--frequency distance between pilot observations and data resource elements (REs), which can make pilot information harder to exploit with purely local processing. This paper proposes \textbf{PARGAR (Pilot-Aware Graph Attention Receiver)}, a graph-attention neural receiver that represents the OFDM resource grid as a graph for bit detection. The graph combines local time--frequency edges with pilot-anchor links from data REs to selected pilot REs, and we further study a channel-scaled pilot-anchor rule based on approximate coherence time and coherence bandwidth. Using Sionna-generated OFDM simulations, we evaluate \textsc{PARGAR} against DeepRx, a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based receiver, across dense, two-symbol sparse, and single-symbol sparse DMRS layouts under channel-mismatch scenarios. Under the considered SISO uncoded setup, channel-scaled \textsc{PARGAR} explicitly injects pilot-aware inductive bias and yields lower BER in selected sparse-pilot scenarios while remaining competitive under dense pilots.

Signal Processing.title: Robust Beamforming Design for Integrated Sensing and Communications with Mutual Coupling Effect
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) is a key technology for next-generation wireless networks, enabling communication and radar sensing over shared spectral and hardware resources. In practical multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) ISAC transmitters, however, mutual coupling (MC) between antenna elements distorts the array steering vector and each communication user (CU) channel, so that the sensing beampattern deviates from the desired one and the communication link to each user degrades. To address this limitation, we propose a robust MC-compensated beamforming design that guarantees both the sensing and communication performance of MU-MIMO ISAC transmitters against the residual MC error. We introduce a residual error on the MC matrix, so that a norm-bounded residual error induces both the sensing beampattern uncertainty and the communication channel uncertainty. The transmit covariance is then optimized against the worst-case of each uncertainty, minimizing the worst-case beampattern matching mean-squared error (MSE) for sensing while guaranteeing the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) for each CU. Each worst-case constraint is converted into a linear matrix inequality, and the problem becomes a convex semidefinite program (SDP). Numerical results show that the proposed robust design attains both a lower sensing beampattern matching MSE and a higher communication SINR than those of the conventional designs, with an advantage that widens as the residual error grows.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 5 figures, submitted to IEEE Wireless Communication Letters, 2026

Signal Processing.title: Multi-Threshold Sampling: Signal Space, Sampling Operators, and First Recorded Crossing-Time Distributions
Signal Processing.summary: Multi-threshold (MT) sampling records crossing times for parameter estimation and waveform reconstruction. We develop signal and observation spaces and stochastic crossing, timing, and selection operators with associated Markov kernels. Finite point measures accommodate variable crossing counts and preserve multiplicity after quantization. For nonhomogeneous Poisson photon arrivals with shared threshold noise, shared timing jitter before quantization, and identity selection, we derive exact first recorded crossing-time distributions. A Poisson series covers general admissible paths with a time-uniform truncation bound. For continuous paths, interval extrema give the exact cumulative distribution function (CDF) and a Fourier representation with contact corrections. A biexponential arrival-intensity and response model admits a two-dimensional first-crossing integral equation on arbitrary finite observation windows, with a unique bounded measurable solution and a Poisson-tail approximation bound. For continuous causal responses with finitely many analytic pieces and bounded first and second branch derivatives, we prove a conditional standard-deviation (SD) limit at first mean crossings with positive slope under relative threshold-noise and fine timing scales. For the biexponential model, its coefficient increases strictly on a parameter-uniform interval and, under a shape condition, up to the first mean peak. Scintillation experiments compare the calculated CDF and conditional SDs with independent waveform simulations on a window extending beyond the single-photon response peak.

Signal Processing.title: Vision-Aided Near-Field Channel Estimation for XL-MIMO
Signal Processing.summary: In wideband extremely large-scale MIMO (XLMIMO) systems, the transmitter (TX) is often in the near field of the base station array. The resulting spherical wavefront makes the line-of-sight channel depend on both the TX angle and distance. Existing polar-domain estimators sample both parameters across the entire coverage region, requiring many candidate positions and pilots. This paper proposes a vision aided framework that uses the object carrying the TX, as seen in a camera image, to restrict the candidate positions to a small grid on that object. An on-grid vision-aided coarse localization (V-CL) algorithm obtains a coarse estimate from the grid points that best fit the received pilots, and an off-grid vision-aided Nelder-Mead refinement (V-NMR) algorithm refines it over continuous angle and distance, from which the channel is reconstructed. Simulations show that the proposed algorithms achieve higher accuracy than both wideband and narrowband polar-domain estimators while requiring far fewer pilots and candidate positions.

Signal Processing.title: Interference-Aware Instantaneous Frequency and Amplitude Estimator for Multicomponent Signals
Signal Processing.summary: In this paper, we introduce a novel instantaneous frequency (IF) estimator for multicomponent signals (MCSs), that takes into account the potential presence of interference in the time-frequency (TF) plane. Our approach optimizes the spectrogram window locally in the TF domain to enhance signal representation, adapting to isolated or interfering modes. This optimization leads to the definition of candidate IF points, which are then gathered together using a novel ridge detection approach, and, finally, IF estimates are obtained by adapting a spline fitting procedure to the potential presence of crossing modes. An extra benefit of the proposed technique is that it also gives access to estimates of the instantaneous amplitudes of the modes, and thus to that of the ideal TF signature of the signal. The proposed IF estimation method compares favorably with state-of-the-art techniques especially on MCSs containing modes with very different frequency modulation.

Signal Processing.title: Gap-Induced Sidelobes in Multiband Wi-Fi CSI and Their Impact on Multipath Delay Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: Leveraging channel state information from multiple Wi-Fi bands has the potential to improve delay resolution for ranging and sensing when wide contiguous spectrum is unavailable. However, non-contiguous spectrum access reshapes the spectral window, producing sidelobes and secondary peaks that can mask closely spaced multipath components. Prior work either designs the bands, which fixed Wi-Fi channelization does not allow, or addresses only the first multipath component. To characterize these secondary peaks, multipath delay estimation is studied in Wi-Fi-compliant multiband settings using channel state information. For a two-path model with unknown complex gains and delays, the Cramér-Rao lower bound for delay separation is derived and analyzed, confirming the benefit of larger frequency aperture at every separation considered, while revealing pronounced, separation-dependent oscillations driven by gap geometry and coupling of the two multipath components. Increasing aperture sharpens the mainlobe but also intensifies sidelobes and multipath interference, yielding competing peaks and a dominant peak shifted from the true delay. For the single-path matched filter, this shift is a deterministic offset governed by the slope of the autocorrelation function (ACF) of the allocation at the separation. A closed-form expression is derived for this offset, predicting it to within 21 ps for the analyzed channel combinations. Since the spectrum allocation enters both the bound and the offset, the impact of its gaps can be assessed for any legal aggregation before a measurement is taken.
Signal Processing.comment: 17 pages, 9 figures, 5 tables. v2: revised and extended version with new title; added co-authors M. Mohorčič and C. Fortuna

Signal Processing.title: Consistency Learning and Distillation for One-Step MIMO-OFDM Channel Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: Iterative neural channel estimators can improve recovery under pilot contamination, but repeated network evaluations increase inference cost. This paper develops observation-anchored consistency and Consistency Mid-Training (CMT) estimators for one-step channel estimation in multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems. Both estimators refine pilot-derived least-squares channel estimates in the delay-beam domain. Consistency learning couples endpoint predictions along noisy-to-clean paths. CMT then refines a compact consistency-trained student to predict a flow-matching teacher's endpoint from intermediate trajectory states. Across the evaluated SNR range, the compact CMT student reduces uncoded symbol error rate (SER) by 9.6-20.2% relative to the one-step flow-matching baseline (0.44-0.98 dB in logarithmic SER reduction), while using 74.5% fewer parameters and 73.0% fewer network multiply-accumulates.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables

Signal Processing.title: SonoDyno: A Sonic Dynamometer for Engine Speed and Load Estimation from Audio
Signal Processing.summary: Controllable engine sound synthesis, Active Sound Design and engine order analysis all build on the relationship between the sound of an engine and its momentary operating state: its speed and its load. Recordings of engine sound are abundant in archives, sample packs and online video, yet they rarely carry time-aligned annotations of that state, which limits their applicability to controllable engine sound generation. We present SonoDyno, which estimates the engine speed, the cylinder count and an engine-normalized load intensity from a microphone signal alone, with no tachometer, no bus access and no prior knowledge of the engine configuration. A convolutional scorer of 124,302 parameters reads the harmonic order energy of each frame at three time-frequency resolutions to jointly score cylinder count and speed, and a decoder imposes the rotational dynamics of the engine on the speed trajectory. A second head estimates the load intensity, the position of the torque between the engine's drag floor at 0 and its full-load ceiling at 1, from the order levels at the decoded speed. On recordings of engines it has never heard, with microphone position, engine type and cylinder count unknown, SonoDyno places 93 to 97% of the frames within 2% of the true speed, identifies the cylinder count with 80% accuracy and confuses the octave on fewer than 2% of the frames. On an unseen engine of a known type, the load intensity has a mean absolute error of 0.12, and the sign of the torque, driving or braking, is right on 91% of the frames. General pitch trackers fall behind even when the harmonic order of each engine is supplied: on our validation recordings and at a tolerance of 5%, the best of them places 62% of the frames within the tolerance, against 96% for SonoDyno.
Signal Processing.comment: 16 pages, 10 figures, 7 tables

Signal Processing.title: Ghost Target Elimination in 5G Reference Signals ISAC via Multi-static Multilateration
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems can reuse 5G New Radio (NR) reference signals to enable joint communication and environmental sensing. Among these signals, the Positioning Reference Signal (PRS) is particularly suitable for range and Doppler estimation. However, its comb structure introduces periodic ambiguities that generate ghost targets. Existing solutions resolve these ambiguities by combining PRS with additional signals such as the DeModulation Reference Signal (DMRS), which increases sensing overhead. This paper proposes a PRS-only sensing framework that resolves ambiguities using multi-static observations. Instead of removing ghosts locally at each receiver, the proposed method exploits spatial diversity and performs ambiguity resolution at a fusion anchor. The anchor jointly estimates target locations and ambiguity indices via multilateration across multiple sensing nodes. This approach eliminates the need for additional reference signals while maintaining low receiver complexity. Simulation results show that the proposed method reliably resolves ghost targets and achieves superior detection performance compared to benchmark methods across various scenarios, while significantly enhancing resource efficiency by enabling sensing using PRS-only transmissions.

Signal Processing.title: One ISAC Array, Two Worst Cases: Hardware Impairments in Beamforming and AoA Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), the same base-station array beamforms toward users and estimates their angle of arrival (AoA). In this paper, we study how element-level gain, phase, and position errors affect both functions of a beam-scanning uniform linear array. Any array produces a correlation peak at the true angle, of finite height and width, surrounded by sidelobes. Impairments shift this peak, make it lower and wider, and raise the sidelobes relative to it. A single decomposition explains these three effects: the gain-weighted least-squares fit of the per-antenna phase errors splits them into a tilt, which shifts the peak, and a residual, whose power is taken from the peak and redistributed over the sidelobes according to its spatial spectrum. A beam steered toward the strongest direction suffers from the lower peak only, whereas the AoA estimate suffers from its shift even without noise, and also from the lowering and sidelobes with noise. The worst cases for the two ISAC functions are thus nearly disjoint, and we characterize both: the worst case for beamforming leaves the AoA estimate unbiased, and the worst case for localization loses little beamforming gain. The worst case for localization is a single defect at the junction between two subarrays, and its error, relative to the main-lobe width, does not decrease with the number of antennas. We also characterize random impairments and the effect of noise. In practical terms, our analysis shows that the calibration of a dual-function array must be assessed with respect to both functions.

Signal Processing.title: Ambiguity Elimination via Successive Estimation in ISAC Systems with Reference Signals
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems can efficiently reuse 5G New Radio (NR) reference signals to enable joint communication and passive target detection. Among these, the Positioning Reference Signal (PRS) is widely adopted for high-performance sensing activities. However, the PRS configuration, given by the comb structure, introduces periodic ambiguities, resulting in ghost targets. Existing approaches mitigate this issue by combining PRS with additional reference signals, such as the DeModulation Reference Signal (DMRS), effectively removing ghosts but at the cost of higher complexity and sensing overhead. This paper proposes a low-complexity successive estimation strategy that initially allows ghost targets but progressively eliminates them using historical ambiguity-free estimations. The method comprises a matching process to associate current detections with historical real targets, and a pattern deviation detection mechanism to trigger a fallback to ambiguity-free estimation when the target set changes. We derive a sufficient condition that guarantees the correct matching as a function of target velocity, PRS comb size, subcarrier spacing, and sensing refresh rate. Using this condition, a parameter selection strategy is proposed to jointly improve sensing and communication performance. Numerical results demonstrate that our method achieves unambiguous detection while significantly reducing sensing resources, thus releasing more resources for communication compared to State-of-the-Art (SotA) approaches.

Signal Processing.title: ST-CGMDiff: Sparse-Conditioned Cross-Frequency Spatio-Temporal Latent Diffusion for Dynamic 3D Channel Gain Map Reconstruction
Signal Processing.summary: Accurate and efficient reconstruction of channel gain maps (CGMs) is essential for environment-aware wireless communications. Unlike prior works that focus on static CGMs at a single frequency band, this paper studies the construction of dynamic three-dimensional (3D) CGMs across multiple frequency bands over consecutive time slots, using limited channel measurements. Specifically, for a given transmitter (Tx) location, we represent the CGM at any given receiver (Rx) height as a two-dimensional (2D) grayscale image, where each pixel indicates the average channel gain over the corresponding Rx spatial grid cell. Accordingly, we propose ST-CGMDiff, a spatio-temporal latent diffusion framework that integrates sparse-observation conditioning and cross-frequency modeling to reconstruct dynamic 3D CGMs across multiple carrier frequencies and varying Rx heights within a unified model. In this framework, we jointly encode the input parameters, including the current sparse observations, observation masks, physical Tx and Rx z-coordinates, and carrier frequencies as spatial conditions. A frequency-conditioned convolutional gated recurrent unit (ConvGRU) then extracts causal information from previously constructed CGMs, while a spatially adaptive fusion mechanism balances historical information and current observations. Furthermore, bidirectional convolutional long short-term memory (BiConvLSTM) modules are introduced to capture the ordered dependencies among the selected Rx z-layers. Finally, we perform few-step latent diffusion followed by high-resolution residual refinement to generate the final CGM with improved spatial fidelity.

Signal Processing.title: Data-Driven Likelihood-Ratio Construction for Radar Detection via Bernstein Induction Operators
Signal Processing.summary: Accurate likelihood-ratio (LR) construction is challenging when clutter statistics are unknown. Prespecified clutter models may not adequately describe the observed data, and evaluating target-present densities may require computationally expensive marginalization. This paper proposes a data-driven LR construction framework based on a Bernstein polynomial model (BPM) and a Bernstein induction operator (BIO). The BPM weights are estimated from clutter-only samples, whereas the target-induced responses of the Bernstein basis densities are approximated offline in the same basis to construct column-stochastic matrices. These matrices map clutter-density weights to target-present density weights at specified signal-to-clutter ratios (SCRs), and mixtures of the matrices account for target fluctuations. For a fixed target model and basis representation, the matrix library is independent of the clutter-density weights and can be reused across clutter distributions. The resulting LR construction avoids repeated online evaluation of the physical-induction integrals. Simulations under analytical clutter models show close agreement with the reference LRs and detection probabilities, with lower online computation times in the non-Gaussian cases considered. Experiments using synthetic target echoes embedded in measured sea clutter further show improved detection probabilities relative to the evaluated baselines in the weak-target regime.

Signal Processing.title: Continuous Wideband Multicarrier Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receiver
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates continuous wideband orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) reception using an auxiliary (AUX)-assisted five-level Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (RAQR) with a single microwave local oscillator (LO), without requiring additional atomic reception transitions or LO frequency combs. By exploiting Floquet theory, the proposed framework characterizes the dynamic atomic response at finite signal-LO detunings without relying on a quasi-static Taylor expansion around the LO operating point. Specifically, closed-form radio-frequency (RF)-to-electrical conversion expressions are derived from the Lindblad master equation under weak-probe and weak-signal approximations. Building on these expressions, an equivalent multicarrier communication model is established, revealing the inherent frequency selectivity of the atomic response and the resulting subcarrier-dependent amplitude and phase distortions. RAQR-aware zero-forcing (ZF) equalization is developed to enable reliable OFDM reception. Furthermore, analytical results reveal how LO and AUX driving influence the atomic response through dressed-state splitting and energy-level shifts. An upper bound on the LO-referenced half-power span is derived, and an approximately $18$-dB reduction in center-response power per bandwidth doubling is established in the AUX-free strong-LO regime. Simulation results validate the analytical response model and reveal pronounced subcarrier-dependent amplitude and phase variations across over $10$~MHz, highlighting the potential of RAQRs as wideband receiving front ends for future wireless communications.

Signal Processing.title: Sensing the Variation of Wireless Propagation Environment Based on Channel Knowledge Map
Signal Processing.summary: With the evolution of sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has raised the demand for high-precision environmental perception. To address the limited capability of existing techniques in sensing environmental variations, this work proposes a novel channel knowledge map (CKM)-based sensing framework that enables structural change sensing in the wireless propagation environment. By leveraging historical CKM data and real?time user channel, a mathematical model is formulated to infer the changing reflectors which represents the environment variations. Specifically, we propose the Information Aggregation Based Robust Two-Stage Reflection Point Refinement (IA-TS-RPR) scheme for reflection point (RP) estimation, which first uses block coordinate descent (BCD) and Riemannian manifold optimization (RMO) for initial estimation, then applies virtual base station (VBS) clustering for information aggregation in the sensitive area (SA) to refine the estimation. Furthermore, we propose an Environment Variation Sensing scheme based on the Hausdorff-Nearest Neighbor Criterion and Time-Window Voting (EVS-HC-TWV). Specifically, the Hausdorff distance is used to match each user to its most relevant CKM grid point (GP), and a time-window-based multi-user voting mechanism is further employed to improve robustness against positional deviations. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed IA-TS-RPR scheme maintains sub-meter RP position estimation accuracy under user positioning errors, significantly outperforming the scheme based on time of arrival (ToA), linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) and least squares (LS). The proposed scheme successfully senses and localizes dynamic reflectors, showing strong generalizability and robustness.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted by IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications

Signal Processing.title: EEG-based listened-language classification
Signal Processing.summary: From an early age, individuals are continuously exposed to other languages beyond their native tongue; however, the brain s response to these auditory stimuli remains unclear. To investigate this, an experiment was designed to record electroencephalography (EEG) signals from subjects listening to sentences in five different languages, and a specific database was built to enable performing classification tests to distinguish between different languages, and varying levels of language comprehension. By analysing the energy difference between the EEG channels to characterize these signals, different classification tests were conducted using bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (bi-LSTM), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) neural networks. The main objective is the analysis of the brain s response in two different scenarios: when the subject listens to sentences in different languages, and when the subject understands or misunderstands the meaning of a sentence. In tire multi-class classification involving sentences in five different languages, the accuracy attained is 36.37 %. However, in the multi-class classification between understood/understood part of the meaning/didn t understand, the accuracy attained reaches 81.36%. The results obtained for binary classification tests of understand native language or foreign language is 89.09 %. The bi-LSTM neural network achieved the overall best performance. These results demonstrate that the analysis of the EEG signals alone can give information regarding a person s language comprehension level, and can be used for monitoring the learning curve of a new language or to assess comprehension in patients with conditions such as aphasia.
Signal Processing.comment: 12 pages, 7 figures

Signal Processing.title: PRISM-AMC: Replay-Free Continual Learning for Automatic Modulation Classification
Signal Processing.summary: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is a key component of cognitive wireless systems, enabling spectrum awareness and adaptive communication. Most deep learning approaches to AMC assume a fixed set of modulation classes and access to previously observed training data. In practice, modulation classes and channel conditions may evolve over time, while storage or data-retention constraints may preclude replay of raw baseband I/Q samples. We propose PRISM-AMC, a replay-free continual learning framework that mitigates catastrophic forgetting by preserving task-relevant subspaces of intermediate representations via gradient projection memory. We further analyze projected stochastic-gradient updates under an SNR-dependent gradient-noise model. PRISM-AMC is evaluated in both class-incremental and domain-incremental settings. Experiments on the MIGOU and DeepSig 2018.01A datasets show substantially reduced forgetting relative to sequential fine-tuning and elastic weight consolidation, while remaining competitive with or outperforming replay-based RSD-AMC in class-incremental settings, without storing raw I/Q samples.

Signal Processing.title: AFDMA with Heterogeneous Post-Chirp Parameters: Supporting User-Specific Waveform Configurations
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates a downlink affine frequency division multiple access (AFDMA) framework supporting flexible user-specific waveform configurations with heterogeneous post-chirp parameters. The proposed framework is in sharp contrast to conventional disjoint chirp-subcarrier allocation, which may destroy inter-user orthogonality when users employ heterogeneous post-chirp parameters. Such a loss of orthogonality manifests as cross-basis leakage onto user-allocated chirp subcarriers, which we characterize by analyzing the cross-projection between user-specific discrete affine Fourier transform bases. Specifically, we express the cross-projection entries as quadratic Gauss sums whose quadratic coefficients depend on pairwise post-chirp differences. This yields a sufficient pairwise residue-class orthogonality rule that preserves inter-user orthogonality by satisfying the leakage-free condition. The resulting chirp-subcarrier allocation problem with pairwise modular constraints is reduced to the residue-class level. To solve this problem, we develop a two-stage framework that recursively searches for a feasible representative allocation and deterministically assigns the remaining residue classes. We prove that the problem is either infeasible or admits an optimal full-loading solution. Simulations show that the proposed allocation avoids the bit error rate (BER) floors and signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) ceiling of conventional localized allocation, achieves near-single-user BER, and provides comparable BER while reducing receiver complexity compared with conventional common-maximum-post-chirp AFDMA.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages, 10 figures

Signal Processing.title: EEG-Based Characterization of Samatha and Vipassana Meditation States
Signal Processing.summary: Meditation has been associated with a range of cognitive and physiological benefits. However, the underlying neural mechanisms of different meditation practices are not yet fully understood. This study investigates whether electroencephalogram (EEG) signals can be used to characterize and distinguish two commonly practiced meditation techniques, namely Samatha and Vipassana, which involve distinct cognitive processes, with Samatha emphasizing sustained concentration and Vipassana emphasizing mindful observation and insight. By extracting features such as band power, coherence and wavelet entropy from EEG signals recorded during pre-meditation resting, Samatha, and Vipassana states, we provide an assessment of how spectral power, signal complexity, and functional connectivity differentiate these practices. Preliminary results from $12$ experienced meditators indicate condition-dependent EEG differences, with the most pronounced effects observed in the delta frequency band. These results demonstrate the utility of EEG-based metrics for the objective characterization of meditation and advance our comprehension of the neural processes underlying different contemplative practices.
authors: M. A. B. C. A. Bandaranayake
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted for APSIPA ASC 2026

Signal Processing.title: Vertical Segmented Waveguide-Enabled Pinching Antenna (V-SWAN)-Assisted EDMA-NOMA Integrated Sensing and Communication Systems
Signal Processing.summary: This paper proposes a vertical segmented waveguide-enabled pinching antenna (V-SWAN)-assisted downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) environmental division multiple access (EDMA) framework for simultaneously supporting multi-user communication and target sensing. In the proposed framework, multiple pinching antennas (PAs) are deployed along a segmented vertical dielectric waveguide to serve communication users (CUs), aerial users (AUs), and sensing target (ST). CUs are distributed on the ground, whereas AUs and ST are above the ground, where line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) propagation conditions coexist. In particular, SWAN provides an effective platform for realizing EDMA by reducing the effective propagation distance and in-waveguide attenuation, thereby suppressing co-channel interference and enabling efficient multi-user transmission. The communication and sensing model are formulated, followed by the corresponding SINR expressions. We formulate the statistical characterizations for the combination of LoS and NLoS propagation for CUs, and LoS propagation for AUs and sensing channels for generalized multi-user, multi-PA scenarios. Based on these statistical characterizations, the segment outage and sensing outage probabilities are derived and evaluated for the generalized framework. The asymptotic evaluation is also done at a high transmit signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) to gain further insights. The results show that the proposed framework outperforms the conventional H-SWAN and single vertical pinching antenna system (V-PASS) in terms of segment outage probability, sensing outage probability, and segment sum rate. Monte Carlo simulation results closely match the analytical results, validating the accuracy of the derived expressions.

Signal Processing.title: SIM-Enabled Wave-Domain Processing in MIMO-OFDM Receivers: Architecture, Modeling, and Validation
Signal Processing.summary: This paper develops a wave-domain linear receiver for wideband MIMO-OFDM, where the main high-dimensional linear processing conventionally performed after sampling is physically shifted to propagation through stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs). The proposed receiver transforms receive-port waveforms into OFDM-domain symbols through three cascaded SIM-enabled functional sections. The first section, SIM_1, performs channel-memory processing and channel shortening in an energy-concentration sense, suppressing the out-of-cyclic-prefix (CP) effective tail before OFDM analysis. SIM_2 realizes CP removal and discrete Fourier transform (DFT) analysis as cyclic-windowed OFDM matched filtering by exploiting useful-window memory and analytical Fourier phase coding. SIM_3 implements residual virtual-subcarrier MIMO linear detection, completing the wave-domain linear receive chain up to symbol slicing. Synchronization, control, slicing, and decoding remain digital, while the dominant linear receive operations are moved to the wave domain. A staged configuration framework is developed: the numerology-dependent OFDM analyzer is compiled offline, whereas the channel-dependent memory processor and detector are configured over the coherence time using architecture-aware learning-assisted control. Numerical results validate both functional replacement and link performance, confirming nearly lossless replacement under CP-sufficient MIMO-OFDM conditions, with robustness to residual timing offsets and effective channel-delay-profile perturbations. Substantial gains under CP-insufficient channels are also demonstrated by suppressing out-of-CP leakage before OFDM analysis.

Signal Processing.title: Look Before You Move: Multimodal Sensing-Aided Trajectory and Beamforming Design for 6DMA
Signal Processing.summary: Six-dimensional movable antenna (6DMA) technology allows a base station (BS) to adjust the three-dimensional (3D) positions and 3D rotations, i.e., the 6D poses, of its surfaces. Many existing 6DMA designs select the poses based on prior channel knowledge. However, the channels at a new pose can be estimated only after the surfaces have moved to this pose, and the limited movement speeds of the surfaces restrict the poses reachable at the next time step. To address these challenges, we propose a learning-based multimodal sensing-aided trajectory and beamforming design for multiuser 6DMA systems with mobile users and surrounding objects. The BS observes the users and surrounding objects with RGB images, LiDAR point clouds, and GPS positions, independently of the poses of the surfaces. Since a surface may need several time steps to reach a favorable pose, the BS designs a 6DMA trajectory over several future time steps and executes only its first step, following receding-horizon control. We propose a neural network, in which user-centric cross-modal attention and temporal self-attention modules relate each user to the scene and its sensing history, and surface-to-user attention relates each surface to the users. A projection layer keeps the poses feasible under the geometric and kinematic constraints, and a graph attention module allocates the transmit power along the pilot-based beamforming directions. Performance evaluations using the CARLA driving simulator and Sionna ray tracing (RT) demonstrate significant minimum-rate gains of the proposed design over fixed-position antennas. Ablation studies validate the contributions of multimodal sensing and the proposed attention modules to these gains. The results further highlight the importance of designing the trajectory several time steps ahead, which is more beneficial under tighter speed limits of the surfaces.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages, 9 figures

Signal Processing.title: Secrecy and Covertness Analysis of SWAN-Enabled Uplink EDMA-NOMA Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Environment division multiple access (EDMA) has recently emerged as a promising multiple-access paradigm by exploiting the wireless propagation environment for user separation, while physical-layer security, including secrecy and covert communication, is becoming increasingly important for protecting confidential information and user privacy. Motivated by these considerations, this paper proposes an EDMA-enabled non-orthogonal multiple access for secrecy and covert communications (EDMA-NOMA-SC) framework for uplink wireless systems. In the proposed framework, a segmented-waveguide-enabled pinching antenna system (SWAN) is employed, where a secrecy user and an intermittently active covert user share the same transmission resource through NOMA within each segment, while a malicious warden attempts to eavesdrop on the secrecy transmission and detect the presence of the covert communication. To capture practical operating conditions, distance-dependent blockage, inter-segment interference, in-waveguide attenuation, imperfect channel state information (ipCSI), and imperfect successive interference cancellation (ipSIC) are considered. Semi-analytical frameworks are developed to characterize the secrecy outage probability (SOP), average secrecy capacity (ASC), false alarm probability (FAP), missed detection probability (MDP), detection error probability (DEP), and covert rate (CR), with their accuracy verified through Monte Carlo simulations. Numerical results, including comparisons with conventional and EDMA-based benchmark schemes, show that the proposed framework generally achieves improved secrecy and covert-rate performance owing to reduced user-to-pinching-antenna propagation distances and in-waveguide attenuation. However, excessive segmentation can degrade performance when inter-segment interference outweighs these propagation benefits.

Signal Processing.title: Physical-Layer Anonymous Communication Design Under Symbol-Aware Identification and Transmitter-Dependent Noises
Signal Processing.summary: Physical-layer characteristics, such as channel state information (CSI) and transmitter noise induced by hardware impairments, are often uniquely associated with a transmitter. This paper investigates transmitter anonymity at the physical layer from a signal design perspective. We consider an anonymous communication problem where the receiver should reliably decode the signal from the transmitter but should not make use of the signal to infer the transmitter's identity. Transmitter anonymity is quantified using a Kullback-Leibler divergence (KLD)-based metric, which enables the formulation of explicit anonymity constraints in the precoder design. We then develop a transceiver design that preserves reliable communication under spatial multiplexing while preventing transmitter identification. The proposed framework employs a partitioned equal-gain combining (P-EGC) scheme that leverages receiver diversity without requiring transmitter-specific CSI. Simulation results demonstrate anonymity-reliability tradeoffs across different signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), numbers of data streams, and alias selection methods. Moreover, the results reveal opposite trends of anonymity with respect to transmitter-dependent noise variations in the low-SNR and high-SNR regimes.
Signal Processing.comment: To appear in IEEE Transactions on Communications

Signal Processing.title: Frequency-Frame Covariance for Reactive-Power Scalarization
Signal Processing.summary: Measured voltage and current waveforms may be represented in a reference frame whose frequency differs from the physical fundamental frequency. Reactive-power readouts calculated from such frequency-shifted coordinates may change if their readout operators are not transformed consistently. This paper presents a frequency-frame covariance formulation for finite-spectrum, zero-mean periodic waveforms with complete harmonic information over one physical period. A necessary and sufficient covariance condition is derived, requiring the readout operator to transform consistently with the waveform representation. Consequently, frequency-dependent harmonic weights must be evaluated at physical harmonic orders rather than relative frame labels. In particular, the derivative/Iliovici readout equals a relative-derivative contribution plus an explicit reference contribution. The formulation also separates readout-operator errors from errors caused by changes in the physical components retained by waveform projections. Three analytical cases illustrate conditional carrier recovery for a memoryless resistor, physical-frequency weighting at relative zero in an RLC branch, and the possibility that an exact reactive-power scalar can coexist with a substantial waveform error after projection. The scope is deterministic calculation consistency in frequency-shifted coordinates rather than instrument measurement uncertainty.

Signal Processing.title: Agentic Wireless Optimization: Workflow Automation, Algorithm Design, and Multi-Timescale Network Operations
Signal Processing.summary: Optimization is fundamental to wireless communications, from characterizing channel capacity and designing transmission schemes to allocating network resources. However, conventional workflows require substantial expertise and manual effort, particularly for high-dimensional or nonconvex problems, black-box objectives, and interdependent decisions across time scales. Recent advances in agentic artificial intelligence (AI), particularly agents based on large language models (LLMs), offer new opportunities to address these challenges by integrating reasoning, tool use, and numerical feedback. This article presents an overview of agentic AI for wireless optimization, focusing on workflow automation, algorithm design, and multi-timescale network operations. First, LLM-based agents streamline optimization workflows by automating problem formulation, code generation, numerical solution, and result verification in a closed loop. Second, they facilitate algorithm design by combining and configuring existing numerical methods and refining learning-based optimizers, using numerical feedback to improve solution quality and computational efficiency for nonconvex and black-box problems. Third, they support multi-timescale network operations by decomposing coupled problems into interdependent subtasks and coordinating their solutions to satisfy network-level objectives and service requirements. A multicast beamforming case study demonstrates performance gains from agent-developed solvers, particularly in execution time, and a network energy-saving example illustrates how agents coordinate dynamic base station activation, user association, and beamforming across time scales. Finally, we discuss open challenges and research opportunities in agentic wireless optimization.

Signal Processing.title: Hotplug Coded Caching: Embedding the YMA and Interference Elimination Schemes via Reed--Muller Codes
Signal Processing.summary: In the hotplug coded caching model, $K$ users fill their caches of size $M$ as a function of $N$ files, but only an unknown subset of $A<K$ users is active in the delivery phase. We recently showed that (i) under uncoded placement, offline users cause a strict load penalty at intermediate memory sizes, so that coded placement is needed; and (ii) for $AM\leq N$, every classical scheme with row-wise placement, including the scheme of Gomez-Vilardebo (GV), can be embedded in a Reed-Solomon code, which removes the penalty. In this note, we show that every point of the scheme of Yu, Maddah-Ali and Avestimehr (YMA) for a classical system with $A$ users is achievable in the hotplug model for every $K\geq A$. Each user is associated with a hyperplane and each file with a homogeneous polynomial; each user caches the restriction of the polynomial to its hyperplane, and the subfiles seen by the active users are the values of the polynomial at the points where their hyperplanes meet. This is a projective Reed-Muller code, which reduces to the Reed-Solomon code when each subfile is cached by one user. We then show, by an existence argument, that every classical scheme whose cache is a linear compression of the Maddah-Ali-Niesen cache and whose correctness holds for generic coefficients can also be embedded over a sufficiently large field; this includes the interference elimination (IE) schemes of Tian and Chen. These embeddings complement the Reed-Solomon one, which allows any row-wise placement and any delivery. Together with past work, our results show that every point attained by a GV, YMA or IE scheme ($N\leq A$ for IE), and every corner point of the linear tradeoff for $A=N=3$, is achievable in the hotplug model with a load that does not depend on $K$. Whether the optimal hotplug tradeoff depends only on $A$ remains open, but these results support a positive answer.
Signal Processing.comment: companion paper to arXiv:2611.03045

Signal Processing.title: Energy Efficiency Maximization in RSMA-Based LEO Satellite Networks Assisted by UAV-Mounted BD-Active RIS: A Hybrid DRL Strategy
Signal Processing.summary: This paper proposes a novel non-terrestrial communication architecture that integrates Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) with a UAV-mounted Beyond-Diagonal Active Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (BD-ARIS) under the coverage of a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite. The BD-ARIS employs a group-connected structure to provide signal amplification and enhanced beamforming flexibility, while RSMA splits user messages into common and private parts to improve SE and interference management. A joint optimization of satellite beamforming, UAV placement, power allocation, and RIS configuration is formulated to maximize the system overall energy efficiency. To solve the resulting non-convex, high-dimensional problem, we first develop a model-based iterative algorithm using Dinkelbach transform, weighted minimum mean-square error reformulation, successive convex approximation, and sequential quadratic programming. We then propose two deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approaches: a standard trust-region policy optimization (TRPO) baseline and a novel Dinkelbach-Guided TRPO (DG-TRPO) scheme. DG-TRPO is initialized via supervised pretraining on Dinkelbach solutions and subsequently fine-tuned with TRPO in noisy, time-varying environments. Simulation results show that DG-TRPO closely matches the model-based benchmark while providing sub-millisecond inference, making it suitable for real-time LEO operation. It also exhibits superior robustness to CSI uncertainty and satellite mobility, and the RSMA BD-ARIS framework significantly outperforms benchmarks employing NOMA or conventional RIS designs. These results establish the proposed architecture and DG-TRPO algorithm as a scalable, energy-efficient solution for future 6G massive IoT non-terrestrial networks.

Signal Processing.title: A Particle-Based Multiuser Communication with a Budget Limit
Signal Processing.summary: Multiuser networks can aggregate local observations through a shared receiver. In this paper, we study the particle budget required to recover the exact sum of binary inputs in a multiuser network. We show that, for the considered model, the minimum budget grows quadratically with the number of transmitters when the symbol duration and target error probability are fixed, even when the receiver observes all particle arrival times. Simultaneous on-off keying (OOK) achieves this quadratic scaling, while any slower budget growth makes the error probability approach one at a fixed symbol duration, regardless of the transmission and decoding scheme. We then examine how this particle requirement can be reduced by allowing longer symbol durations and more counting intervals. We develop a groupwise OOK counting (GOC) scheme with staggered group releases and sequential estimation of group input sums, accounting for delayed arrivals.
